PART V
CHAPTER 50

BIOGRAPHICAL NOTES ON SENIOR MEMBERS OF THE STAFF OF THE COMMONWEALTH RELATIONS OFFICE

A

ABBEY, Donald Alfred; born 7th April 1922; educated Ruckholt School, Leyton; m. 1945 Olive Pinwell (1 s. 1948; 1 d. 1950); enlisted Royal Army Ordnance Corps 1941–46; Temporary Clerk, India Office, 7th January 1947; Executive Officer 3rd September 1955; British Information Services, Johannesburg, 1956–59; Passport Officer, Karachi, 1960–62; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

ADAIR, Arthur Robin, cvo (1961), mbe (1947); born 10th February 1913; educated Boujeloud School, Fez, Morocco, Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School, Wimborne, and Emmanuel College, Cambridge; Modern Languages Tripos (French and Spanish) Class II Div. I; m. 1952 Diana Synnott (1 s. 1956); Indian Civil Service 16th September 1937 to 1947, including three years in Army as Assistant and later Deputy Recruiting Officer under Lucknow Recruiting Area; commissioned 2nd Lieutenant April 1941 and placed in charge of recruitment for Province of Bihar and some of the Eastern States; reverted to Government of Bihar with rank of temporary Major February 1944; District Magistrate and Deputy Commissioner 1944 to 1947 with short period as Additional Director of Agriculture; Temporary Principal, Treasury, 17th July 1947; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st October 1947; Principal 28th May 1948; Dacca July 1947 to October 1950; Colombo September 1952 to March 1956; Deputy High Commissioner, Dacca (local Assistant Secretary), August 1960; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962.

ADAMS, Charles Christian Wilfrid; born 2nd June 1939; educated the King's School, Canterbury, and New College, Oxford, (Open Exhibitioner) 1958–61; 2nd Class Honours in Modern History; Temporary Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 22nd October 1962; seconded to Central African Office 22nd October 1962; Resident Clerk July 1963.

ADAMS, Mary Campbell; born 28th March 1917; educated Commonweal Lodge School, Purley, and Croydon Art School; Civil Defence, Civil Nursing Reserve and V.A.D., R.N., 1939–46; Temporary Clerk, Commonwealth Relations Office, 20th October 1947; Clerical Assistant 6th January 1949; Clerical Officer 8th November 1949; Executive Officer 3rd September 1955; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

ALLAN, James Nicholas; born 22nd May 1932; educated Greshams 1946–50 and London School of Economics (Laski Scholar) 1953–56; 1st Class Honours asc (Econ.); m. 1961 Helcna Susara Crouse; National Service, R.A.C. and R.A.S.C., 1951–53; commissioned August 1951; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 29th October 1956; Resident Clerk March 1957 to January 1958; Capetown/Pretoria February 1958 to September 1959; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 16th November 1959 to April 1961 (Private Secretary to Minister of State June to September 1960); Principal (local) 4th April 1961; Freetown May 1961; Principal 1st August 1961.

ALLEN, Mark Echalaz, cvo (1961); born 19th March 1917; educated Charterhouse 1930–35 and Christ Church, Oxford, 1936–39; 2nd Class Honours in Philosophy, Politics and Economics; m. 1948 Elizabeth Bowdler (1 d. 1950; 2 s. 1951, 1957); Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 2nd October 1939; military service 1940–45; commissioned in Intelligence Corps; Western Desert and G.H.Q., Cairo, 1941–43; Sicily and Italy 1943–45; released with rank of Captain; Principal (in absentia) 10th March 1944; Dublin 1945–46; Bombay 1948–50; Permanent United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations in New York 1953–56; Assistant Secretary 1st November 1956; Deputy High Commissioner, Madras, February 1960; Delhi October 1961 to November 1963.

ALLISON, Walter Leonard, mvo (1961); born 1st May 1926; educated Fiern Barnet Grammar School and Merton College, Oxford; 1st Class Honours, History, 1947; m. 1951 Margaret Patricia Watts (twin d. 1956, 1 d. 1959); Temporary Assistant Principal, Ministry of Fuel and
Power, 1947-48; Assistant Principal, Ministry of Education, 23rd August 1948; Assistant Private Secretary to Minister of Education January 1953 to April 1954; Principal 20th April 1954; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st October 1958; Lahore May 1960 to June 1962; Acting Deputy High Commissioner July to November 1960 and November 1961 to June 1962; Karachi June to August 1962; Madras April 1963; Acting Deputy High Commissioner May to September 1963.

Anderson, George David; born 11th September 1913; educated King Edward VII Grammar School, King's Lynn, (King's Gold Medallist) and Emmanuel College, Cambridge; Modern Languages Parts I and II Class I; m. 1950 Audrey Money (1 d. 1961); social welfare work with National Association of Boys' Clubs 1935-37; Mercantile assistant in Rangoon 1938-41; Hon. Secretary, Rangoon Boys' Home Trust, 1938-42; Burma Auxiliary Force 1938; Commissioned in Burma Rifles April 1942; Combined Services Detailed Interrogation Centre (India) April 1944; Lieutenant-Colonel O.C. Indian Wing March 1945, and Commandant April 1946; released August 1946; Principal, Ministry of Food, 1st October 1946; Delhi December 1946 to December 1948; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st October 1947; Calcutta April 1949 to June 1951; on Secretariat, Meeting of Commonwealth Finance Ministers, London, January 1952; attached to U.K. delegation to Geneva Conference on Korea and Indo-China April to July 1954; Dublin February 1957 to December 1960; Counsellor (local Assistant Secretary) 1st May 1960; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 9th January 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Colombo, October 1961; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962.

Archer, Margaret, MBE (1952); born 7th August 1921; educated King Edward's High School for Girls, Birmingham, 1932-39 and Birmingham University 1940-43; Honours in Social and Political Science 1943; BA; Burroughs' Operator, Austin Motor Works, September 1939 to April 1940; Women's Land Army 1940; Welfare Officer, Telecommunications Research Establishment, 1943-45; Welfare Officer, Ministry of Education, 1945-49; Senior Temporary Assistant, Commonwealth Relations Office, 26th October 1949; Delhi October 1949 to January 1953; Executive Officer (local Higher Executive Officer) 1st August 1951; Higher Executive Officer 1st August 1952; Wellington February 1954 to April 1956; Senior Executive Officer (temporary) 7th August 1959; Senior Executive Officer 20th May 1960; Principal 9th June 1960; Salisbury July 1960 to June 1963.

Arthington-Davv, Humphrey Augustine, MBE (1953); born 30th October 1920; educated Eastbourne College and Trinity College, Cambridge; commissioned into the Rajputana Rifles 1941; transferred to the Indian Political Service 1946; Civil Service of Pakistan 1947-56; Assistant Adviser, Western Aden Protectorate, 1957; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 21st April 1958; Political Adviser with the Royal Air Force, Gan, 1959; British Representative in the Maldives Islands 1960.

Ashford, William Stanton; born 4th July 1924; educated Winchester; m. 1957 Rosalind Anne Collett (1 s. 1960); joined R.A.F. 1943; commissioned 1944; released 1947; Information Officer, Air Ministry, 1948; Deputy Command Information Officer, Middle East Air Force, 1949; Command Information Officer, Middle East Air Force, 1953; established Senior Information Officer, September 1957; Head of Information 1(a), Air Ministry, September 1959; on loan to Commonwealth Relations Office May 1961; Director, British Information Services, Freetown, June 1961; transferred to Commonwealth Relations Office 1st May 1962; Director of Information Services, Ghana, December 1962; Acting Principal Information Officer April 1963.

Aspin, Norman; born 9th November 1922; educated Darwen Grammar School 1934-41 and Durham University 1941-42 and 1945-47; 1st Class Honours in Geography 1947; BA; MA 1947; m. 1948 Elizabeth Irving (3 s. 1950, 1952, 1963); enlisted as rating in R.N.V.R. July 1942; commissioned January 1943 and appointed to Naval Meteorological Service; served in East Africa; Lieutenant; Demonstrator in Geography, Durham University, 1947-48; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th August 1948; Bombay November 1948 to February 1951; Principal 1st July 1952; Salisbury October 1954 to February 1957; on loan to Treasury February 1958 to March 1960; Adviser to the Governor of Sierra Leone, Freetown, August 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Freetown, April 1961 to June 1963; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 1st July 1963.

Aston, Thomas William; born 14th May 1922; educated Saltley Grammar School, Birmingham, 1932-39; m. 1947 Eve Dunning (1 d. 1949); Employment Clerk, Ministry of Labour, 14th August 1939; joined R.A.F. 1941; in training in U.K., U.S.A. and Canada 1941-43; commissioned (Navigator) 1942; served in Middle East 1943; Flight-Lieutenant 1944; served in Palestine, Persian Gulf, Egypt and South Africa 1944-46; demobilized May 1946; Executive Officer (Inspector), Ministry of National Insurance, 13th October 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th March 1951; Delhi February 1953 to April 1954; Principal 6th July 1954; seconded to Joint Intelli-
AUSTIN, Brian Patrick; born 18th March 1938; educated St. Olave's Grammar School 1946-56 and Clare College, Cambridge, 1958-61; English Tripos Part I Class I, Part II Class II Division I; BA 1961; National Service with R.A.F. 1956-58; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 21st August 1961; Resident Clerk December 1961 to March 1963; seconded to Central African Office March to December 1962; Lagos April 1963.

AVERY, David Robert; born 20th October 1921; educated Plympton Grammar School 1931-37 and Devonport Dockyard Technical College 1938-39; m. 1948 Vera Andrews (1 s. 1951; 1 d. 1955); Clerical Officer, Admiralty, 17th April 1939; Executive Officer (Assistant Naval Cashier), Freetown, 1942-44; Lieutenant, R.N.V.R., Bombay and Madras, 1944-48; Higher Executive Officer 18th May 1953; Secretary, R.N. Yard, Trincomalee, 1953-57; Senior Executive Officer 19th April 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st December 1961; Lagos April 1963.

BACHE, Andrew Philip Foley; born 29th December 1939; educated Shrewsbury School and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, 1958-61; 2nd Class Honours Part I Economics, Part II Law; m. 1963 Marged Shan Headley; Temporary Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 25th February 1963.

BADMAN, Francis Leonard; born 8th May 1918; educated Abertillery Grammar School 1929-30 and Bassaleg Grammar School 1930-36; m. 1947 Gwyneth Mathias (2 s. 1948, 1954); Clerical Officer, Board of Trade, 1936; enlisted Territorial Army, 1st Battalion Monmouthshire Regiment, 1938; demobilized April 1946; Executive Officer, Ministry of Transport, w.e.f. 1943; Higher Executive Officer, Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation, June 1955; Commonwealth Relations Office November 1958; Karachi 1959 to 1962; Senior Executive Officer (Notional) 1st August 1963; Kuching January 1963.

BAILEY, Louisa; born 12th January 1909; educated Ursuline Convent, Ilford; Telefonist, G.P.O., September 1926; Clerical Officer, Air Ministry, January 1942; Dominions Office May 1947; Executive Officer October 1950; Higher Executive Officer 18th June 1959.

BAKER, George William, VRD; born 7th July 1917; educated Chigwell School 1927-35 and Hertford College, Oxford, (Colonial Service Course) 1948-49; m. 1942 Audrey Day (2 d. 1945, 1947); member of London Division, Royal Naval Volunteer Reserve since 1936; present rank Lieutenant Commander; active service at sea 1939-42 and in Commandos 1942-45; Administrative Officer, Colonial Service, Tanganyika, 1946; District Officer 1948; Second Devonshire Course, Oxford, 1948-49; seconded to Foreign Service as Assistant Colonial Attaché, Washington, 1957; British Delegation to Trusteeship Council, United Nations, 1957; returned to Tanganyika 1958; Administrative Officer, Class IIb, 1958; Class IIIa 1959; Class I 1960; Director (later re-styled Controller) of Information Services, Tanganyika Government, 1960-62; retired from Tanganyika under Africanisation scheme 1962; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th October 1962; Director of Information Services, Freetown, December 1962; Member of Institute of Public Relations; Member of Royal Photographic Society.

BAMBURY, Thomas, MVO (1961); born 1st March 1921; educated King Edward VI School, Nuneaton, 1931-38; m. 1942 Priscilla Johnson; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Health, 12th April 1938; served in Royal Air Force 1940-46; Ministry of National Insurance 18th July 1946; Executive Officer 9th October 1947; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st August 1957; Karachi October 1958 to February 1962; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1962.

BANKS, John Anthony Gorst; born 27th June 1933; educated Eton College and King's College, Cambridge, (Minor Scholar in Classics); 2nd Class History Tripos; m. 1960 Gillian Theresa Brimblecombe (2 d. 1961, 1962); military service 1952-54; commissioned in Royal Artillery; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 16th September 1957; Resident Clerk January to October 1958; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State September 1958 to July 1960; member of Secretariat of Commonwealth Prime Ministers' Meeting May 1960; Delhi August 1960; member of British Delegation to Second Commonwealth Education Conference, Delhi, 1962.

BARLTROP, Roger Arnold Rowlandson; born 19th January 1930; educated Solihull School, Leeds Grammar School and Exeter College, Oxford, 1950-54; Classical Hon. Mods. and Lit. Hum.; BA; m. 1962 Penelope Pierronet Dalton (1 d. 1963); Midshipman, Royal Navy, 1949-50; Permanent R.N.V.R. 1950; Lieutenant 1954; R.N.R. 1958; Lieutenant-Commander 1962; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 18th October 1954; Delhi March 1956 to July 1957; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 6th August 1957 to 21st October 1959; Principal (temporary)
22nd October 1959: Private Secretary to Minister of State 22nd October 1959 to 22nd June 1960; Principal 1st March 1960; Enugu August 1960 to April 1962; Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Enugu, December 1961 to April 1962 and Ibadan, April to July 1962; Salisbury July 1962: Assistant Secretary-General, Central African Conference, June to July 1963.

BARRACLOUGH, Mrs. Margaret Elizabeth, OBE (1956: MBE 1947): born 5th February 1912; educated Wycombe Abbey School, Bucks; widow; Colonial Service 1945 to April 1946; Office of Special Commissioner for the U.K. in South-East Asia May 1946; Consulate-General, Canton, July 1949; Second Secretary, British Embassy, Rangoon, October 1949; First Secretary (Information) September 1950; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th November 1957; Ottawa January 1958 to January 1962; Principal Information Officer (local) April 1958; Principal Information Officer 1st October 1960; Delhi April 1962.

BARROW, John Frederick; born 28th December 1918; educated King Edward VII School, King's Lynn, 1930-36; m. 1947 Mary Young (2 d. 1947, 1950); Clerical Officer, Post Officer Engineering Department, Cambridge, 1936; Ministry of Transport, Cambridge, 1937; enlisted R.A.S.C. 16th October 1939; Commissioned R.I.A.S.C. April 1942; served in India and Burma 1942-46; Major; Executive Officer (in absentia), Ministry of Transport, 1942; Higher Executive Officer, Central Land Board, 1948; H.M. Treasury June 1953; Assistant Financial Adviser, Delhi, October 1954 to April 1957; Principal February 1958; Commonwealth Relations Office August 1962; Kuala Lumpur August 1963.

BARTON, Olive May, MBE (1954); born 30th March 1906; educated Kent College, Folkestone; served in U.K. Trade Commissioner's Office in Queensland 1937-53; Board of Trade (South-East Asian Division of C.R.E.D.) 1953-54; Assistant to U.K. Trade Commissioner in Western Australia 1954-55; Assistant Information Officer, Perth, Western Australia, 1955-57; Information Officer in Western Australia 1958; Information Officer, Melbourne, September 1958; Senior Information Officer 1st October 1960; Adelaide January 1961.

BASS, Harry Godfrey Mitchell; born 26th August 1914; Scholar of Marlborough College 1928-33 and of Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, 1933-37; Classical Tripos Part I Class I, Part II Class I; BA (Cantab.) 1937; St. John's College, Oxford, 1937-39; BA (Oxon) 1937; MA (Cantab.) 1940; m. 1948 Monica Burroughs (2 s. 1949, 1950; 1 d. 1955); Assistant Keeper II, British Museum, 27th March 1939; lent to Admiralty 4th March 1940; Acting Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 9th September 1946; member of United Kingdom Delegation to Food and Agriculture Organization Conference, Geneva, 1947; Principal 9th September 1947; Canberra May 1948 to October 1950; temporarily transferred to Wellington September and October 1948; seconded to Cabinet Office June 1951 to July 1953; member of Secretariat, Meetings of Commonwealth Ministers concerned with Supply and Production 1951 and Commonwealth Finance Ministers 1952, Commonwealth Economic Conference 1952 and Meeting of Commonwealth Prime Ministers 1953; Calcutta February 1954 to February 1957, with local rank of Assistant Secretary; Assistant Secretary 29th August 1955; Adviser, United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations, September to November 1957 and 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Salisbury, March 1959; Cape Town/Pretoria March 1961 to September 1962 (Minister May 1961 to September 1962); seconded to Central African Office January 1963.

BATES, William Stanley; born 7th September 1920; educated Christ's Hospital 1932-39 and Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, 1939-40 and 1946-47; History Tripos Class I 1947; enlisted Royal Signals 1940; commissioned 1941; 9th Commando 1941-45; Major; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, April 1948; Principal 1st March 1951; Commonwealth Relations Office, on loan 19th July 1954, transferred 1st January 1956; Canberra August 1956 to April 1959; Assistant Secretary March 1962; seconded to Central African Office March 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Kaduna, January 1963.

BAXTER, Ronald William; born 28th March 1921; R.A.F. service in war; then sub-editor for The Scotsman, Daily Mail and London Evening Standard; Editorial Executive, Straits Times group, Singapore, 1948-56 (Editor, Malayan Sunday Times, 1950-56); Sub-editor Daily Express, London, June 1956 to December 1957; Information Officer in charge local press and self-government publicity, Northern Nigeria, January 1958 to October 1959; Information Officer, Madras, November 1959; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th September 1959; Senior Information Officer 12th February 1960; Editor-in-Chief, Information, New Delhi, March 1960; Regional Information Officer, Calcutta, (local Principal Information Officer) March 1962.

BEATTIE, Hugh Ronald Montgomerie; born 21st May 1916; educated George Heriot's School, Edinburgh, 1924-33, University of Edinburgh 1933-38 and University of London 1938-39; First Class Honours in
Modern History; MA; m. 1946 Margaret Reid Russell; Governor's Commission in Sierra Leone Defence Corps 1940; seconded to Sierra Leone Regiment, Royal West African Frontier Force, 1940-41; Sierra Leone Civil Service 1940-61; Assistant District Commissioner 1943; Clerk of Executive Council 1947-48; District Commissioner 1949; Permanent Secretary 1956; Provincial Commissioner 1957; Chairman, Kono District Security Committee, 1957; Administrative Secretary 1959; Acting Deputy Governor August 1960 to March 1961; retired under Retirement Benefits Scheme November 1961; Temporary History Master, Royal High School, Edinburgh, 1962; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st March 1962.

BEER, Ronald George William; born 6th September 1921; educated St. Mary's R.C. School and Salesian College; m. 1942 Dora Annie Carter (1 d. 1946); enlisted in R.A.F. 1941; served as navigator, Bomber Command, in Europe; Prisoner of War March 1944 to May 1945; Temporary Clerk, Dominions Office, 10th December 1945; Clerical Officer 1st January 1949; Executive Officer 30th December 1952; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Lahore 1953-55; Wellington August 1960 to September 1963.

BELCHER, Ronald Harry, CMG (1958); born 5th January 1916; educated Christ's Hospital 1925-34, Jesus College, Cambridge, 1934-38 (Classical Scholar; Classical Tripos Part I Class II Division I, Part II Class I; Diploma in Classical Archaeology) and Brasenose College, Oxford, 1938-39 BA; m. 1948 Hildegarde Jones (1 s. 1948); Indian Civil Service 1938-48; served in the Punjab; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st April 1948; Principal 1st January 1949; seconded to Foreign Service on staff of British Embassy, Washington, March 1951 to October 1953; Private Secretary to Secretary of State 19th October 1953; Assistant Secretary 6th December 1954; Deputy High Commissioner, Capetown/Pretoria, January 1956 to April 1959; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (temporary) 8th August 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Delhi, October 1961; substituting High Commissioner 19th June 1962 to 8th October 1962.

BELL, George Edward; born 25th June 1915; educated Bolton School and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, 1934-38; Modern Languages Tripos (French and German) Class II; BA 1937; Certificate in Education (with Distinction) 1938; m. 1943 Anne Hogarth (1 s. 1948; 1 d. 1949); on staff of The Manchester Grammar School 1938-39; enlisted Royal Tank Regiment 1939; commissioned R.M.C., Sandhurst, 1941; Major 1945; served in N.W. Europe; Public Relations/Information Services Control Branch of Control Commission for Germany (Berlin 1945-48, Kiel 1948-49, Hamburg as Deputy Director, Press Production Branch (Die Welt) 1949-50, Deputy Director of Press Branch, Information Services Division 1950-54); Foreign Office (Director of Press Branch of I.S.D. in Embassy at Bonn 1954-56, Consul i/c Political and Press Department of H.M. Consulate General, Hamburg, 1956-58); Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 16th October 1958; Regional Information Officer, Lahore, November 1958 to February 1962; Information Officer 4th March 1959; Senior Information Officer 26th April 1962; Ibadan (local Principal Information Officer) January 1964.

BENTLIFF, David Gordon Rix; born 9th October 1926; educated Denstone College, Staffs, 1941-44 and Lincoln College, Oxford, 1947-50; 2nd Class in Final School of Jurisprudence; m. 1957 Bridget Eastwood (2 d. 1958, 1960); Royal Navy 1944-47, successively as Midshipman and Sub-Lieutenant, R.N.V.R.; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th November 1950; Colombo February 1952 to December 1953; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 17th February 1955 to 6th February 1956; Principal 30th January 1956; United Kingdom Trade Commissioner, Karachi, April 1958 to July 1961.

BERGSKAUG, Dorothy Evelyn; born 3rd January 1909; educated County Secondary School, Putney, 1919-27 and London School of Economics 1927-30; secretarial work, Paramount Film Service Ltd., 1931-36; secretary to Chairman of Messrs. Eustace Watkins Ltd. 1936-40; Secretary to Mr. Sidney L. Bernstein, Honorary Adviser to Films Division, Ministry of Information, 1940-42; Editorial Secretary, British Paramount News, 1942-47; Temporary Executive Officer, subsequently Temporary Assistant Information Officer, Films Division, Central Office of Information, 1947-51; Temporary Assistant Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 17th October 1951; Assistant Information Officer 14th January 1959; Information Officer 1st August 1959.

BICKFORD, William Reginald, MBE (1943); born 14th September 1911; educated Cheltenham College and Wadham College, Oxford; Lit Hum. Part I Class I, Part II Class II; m. 1939 Elizabeth Edwards (1 s. 1948; 1 d. 1952); Indian Civil Service 1934; served in Burma as Assistant Commissioner until 1939; posted to Home Department April 1939; Civil Affairs Staff, Burma, February 1944; commissioned into A.B.R.O. from same date; served in India and Burma; released with rank of Major October 1945; Secretary, Defence and External Affairs Department, October 1945 to March
1947, and Additional Secretary, Finance Department, to May 1947; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th April 1948; Delhi April 1948 to May 1950; Karachi January 1955; Dacca November 1956 to June 1958 (Acting Deputy High Commissioner February to May 1958); Canberra 5th March 1962.

BISHOP, Major-General William Henry Alexander, CB (1946), CMG (1961), CVO (1961), OBE (Military), Commander, Order of St. John of Jerusalem (1951); born 20th June 1897; educated Plymouth College 1907-14 and Royal Military College, Sandhurst, 1914-15; m. 1925 Mary Corbett (1 s. 1926); joined Dorset Regiment (2nd Lieutenant) April 1915; served in Iraq and Palestine 1915-18; India 1919-25; England, and attended Army Staff College, Camberley, 1926-29; Germany 1930; G.S.O. 3, War Office, 1931-34; R.A.F. Staff College 1935; Staff Officer (G.S.O. 2) to Inspector-General, African Colonial Forces, Colonial Office, 1936-39; Brevet Lieutenant-Colonel 1938; Chief Staff Officer, East Africa Force, 1939-40; Liaison Officer with War Cabinet Offices, Dominions Office, 1940-41; Colonel 1941; Brigadier 1941; Principal Administrative Staff Officer, West Africa, 1941-42; Brigadier, Inter-Allied Planning Staff, North Africa, 1943; Major-General 1944; Director of Quartering, War Office, 1944; Acting Director-General, Political Intelligence Department, Foreign Office, 1945; Foreign Office (Control Commission for Germany) 1945-50 (Chief, Information Services Division, 1945-46, Deputy Chief of Staff 1947-48, Commissioner 'Land', North Rhine-Westphalia, 1948-50): Assistant Secretary, Commonwealth Relations Office, with seniority from 1st July 1948, 1st January 1951; Principal Staff Officer to Secretary of State July 1953; visited Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, India, Pakistan, Ceylon and Malaya 1956-57; Deputy High Commissioner, Calcutta, October 1957 to July 1962; local Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1st October 1957; Director of Information Services and Cultural Relations 16th July 1962.

BLAIR, Oliver Robin; born 7th October 1925; educated Winchester College, West Hill High School, Montreal, 1939-43 and King's College, Cambridge, (Colonial Service Course) 1947-48; Called to Bar 1959; Coldstream Guards 1944-47 (Lieutenant); Administrative Officer Class IV, Gold Coast, 19th January 1949; Class III 1954; Class II 1957; retired from Overseas Civil Service (Ghana) 23rd December 1958; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th June 1959; Calcutta July 1960 to September 1962; Principal (local) July 1960; Principal 1st December 1960; Karachi September 1962.

BLANCHARD, Arthur, MBE (1962); born 8th November 1906; m. 1938 Catherine Gladys Hunt (dec. 1959) (1 d. 1946); enlisted Royal Signals October 1926; served in India 1926-32 and Northern China 1934-38; Instructor to Supp. Reserve 1938-39; B.E.F. September 1939 to June 1940; Mentioned in Despatches; Commissioned 1941; India 1941-42; East Africa and British Somaliland 1943-44; India and Burma 1944-45; released 1945 (Major); Tempy. Appts. Officer, Min. of Lab. & Nat. Service, 1945-48; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th February 1948; Executive Officer 24th May 1951; Bombay 1953-55; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960.

BOOKER, Eleanor Milford, MBE (1951); born 28th June 1918; educated St. Mary's School, Calne, 1930-36 and Westfield College, London University, 1937-40; Class IIA Honours in History; BA 1940; secretarial work, War Office, (Regional Headquarters, Birmingham) March to September 1941; Temporary Assistant Principal, India Office, 22nd September 1941; special duty with Cabinet Mission to India March to July 1946; Information Officer 1st August 1949; Information Officer, Colombo, August 1954 to November 1955; Press Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, April 1957; Senior Information Officer 20th January 1958; Principal Information Officer (temporary) 1st April 1960, (acting) 1st April 1963.

BOOTBY, Ernest Edward; born 22nd August 1923; m. 1948 Nina Hurt (2 s. 1949, 1953; 1 d. 1956); Telegraphist, Central Telegraph Office, 1939; military service, Royal Signals, 1941-47; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, September 1952; Executive Officer December 1954; Wellington July 1958 to August 1961; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

BORTHWICK, James, MBE (Military); born 31st May 1913; educated Whitehill School, Glasgow, 1925-28, Rutherglen Academy 1928-30 and Glasgow University 1930-33; MA; m. 1941 Anne Stewart McKiddie (1 d. 1944; 2 s. 1946, 1950); journalist, Southern Reporter, 1930-32; Courier & Advertiser, Dundee, 1932-35; assistant editor, The Weekly News 1935-40; enlisted Black Watch 1940; commissioned Black Watch 1941; served Middle East, North Africa, Sicily and Italy 1943-44; Mentioned in Despatches; North-West Europe 1944-46; P.R.O., 51st Highland Division, 1943-45; DADPR, 2nd Army and 21st Army Group and BAOR, 1945-46; DADPR, H.W. Western Command, 1946-52; Major; released 1952; Senior Information Officer, H.Q. Western Command, 1952-56; Deputy Director, Information, South Africa, 1956-61; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st December 1957; Principal Information Officer 1st
April 1958; Director of Information, Lagos, 1961–63; Regional Information Officer, Winnipeg, 1963.

BOTTOM, Doreen Joan; born 5th February 1923; educated Glendale County Grammar School, Wood Green, 1934–39; Clerical Assistant, Dominions Office, 17th July 1939; Clerical Officer 28th February 1940; Executive Officer 5th February 1948; Higher Executive Officer 2nd January 1956; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

BOTTOMLEY, James Reginald Alfred; born 12th January 1920; educated King's College School 1933–38 and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1938–40; m. 1941 Barbara Vardon (2 d. 1943, 1946; 2 s. 1944, 1963 and 1 s. dec.); military service 1940–46; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 21st October 1946; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 29th March 1947; Capetown/Pretoria January 1948 to March 1951; Principal 20th September 1949; Karachi September 1953; seconded to Foreign Office and posted to British Embassy, Washington, September 1955; U.K. Mission to the U.N., New York, February to July 1959; Assistant Secretary 2nd February 1959; Deputy High Commissioner, Kuala Lumpur, (local Assistant Under-Secretary of State) September 1963.

BOULTON, John Terence Tyson; born 15th July 1929; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th February 1950; Madras 1957–58; Karachi 1959–63; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

BOURN, James; born 30th August 1917; educated Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School, Darlington; military service 1939–46; Captain; Executive Officer, Ministry of Health, 7th September 1936; Higher Executive Officer, Ministry of National Insurance, 1947; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 1947; Principal November 1949; Secretary to the Salaries Commission, Bahamas, 1948–49; seconded to Tanganyika 1953–55; Commonwealth Relations Office 28th June 1961; seconded to Central African Office March 1962; Dar es Salaam June 1963.

BRANNEY, Louis; born 28th January 1916; educated the Royal Liberty School, Gidea Park, Essex, and King's College, University of London; 1st Class Hons. (Modern History) 1938; BA; Inglis Post-graduate research student in University of London 1938–39; University of Belgrade 1939; m. 1949 Margaret Brittain (4 d.); joined R.A. 1940; commissioned 1941; Political Intelligence Department of Foreign Office/SHAEC 1943; Foreign Office Research Department 1945; Deputy British Editor of the joint Foreign Office/U.S.A. State Department Publication Documents on

German Foreign Policy 1919–45, 1946–48; Research Officer to Colonial Office 1948–63; Research Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd September 1963.

BRIND, Arthur Henry; born 4th July 1927; educated Barry Grammar School 1938–44 and St. John's College, Cambridge, 1944–47; Historical Tripos Class II Division I; m. 1954 Barbara Harrison (1 s. 1961); military service 1947–49; Colonial Administrative Service and H.M.O.C.S. 1950–60; served in Gold Coast and Ghana; Assistant Principal 15th August 1960; Principal 1st August 1961; Ottawa February 1963.

BRITTEN, George Vallette, Brigadier (retd.), CBE (1947; OBE 1942; MBE 1940), American Legion of Merit (1946), West German Grosses Verdienst Kreuz (1959); born 19th March 1909; educated Wellingborough and R.M.C., Sandhurst; m. 1937 Shirley Stewart-Wink (3 s. 1938, 1940, 1949); Commissioned in the Northamptonshire Regiment 1929; served in United Kingdom and Ireland 1929–39; Staff College 1939; North-West Europe 1939–40; Staff Appointments in England and Ireland 1940–41; Commanded an Airborne Battalion, United Kingdom, North Africa and Sicily, 1942–43; Deputy Chief of Staff, 5th U.S. Army, Italy, 1943–44; Planning Staff, H.Q., 21 Army Group, North-West Europe, 1944 to end of war; three times Mentioned in Despatches; Assistant Chief of Staff, Military Government/Civil Affairs (later Control Commission for Germany), 1945–47; Regimental duty, Berlin and Austria, 1947–48; War Office Staff 1949–51; Commandant, Small Arms School, Hythe, and Chairman, Army Rifle Association, 1952–54; British Instructor, U.S. Army Staff College, Fort Leavenworth, U.S., 1954–55; N.A.T.O. Staff, Fontainebleau, 1956–58; Military Attaché, British Embassy, Bonn, 1959–61; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 12th June 1961; Enugu August 1962.

BRITTEN, Rae Gordon; born 27th September 1920; educated Liverpool Institute High School 1932–39 and Magdalen College, Oxford, 1939–41 and 1945–47 (Classical Exhibitioner); Hon. Mods. Class II 1940; Philosophy, Politics and Economics Class II 1947; m. 1952 Valentine Alms (3 d. 1953, 1955, 1959; 1 s. 1956); military service 1941–45; Research Assistant with Common Ground Ltd. October 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd May 1948; Calcutta October 1948; Delhi October 1949 to November 1950; Principal 20th August 1951; United Kingdom delegation to G.A.T.T. Review Session in Geneva 1954–55; Bombay April 1955 to July 1958; Karachi June 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, March 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Lahore, June 1962; Assistant Secretary 1st January 1963.
BROADFOOT, Alexander William; born 29th January 1924; educated Possilpark School and North Kelvinside School, Glasgow, 1935-40; m. 1953 Kathleen Mary Warner (1 s. 1956; 1 d. 1960); Post Office 1941; Royal Corps of Signals 1943-47; rejoined Post Office; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 12th June 1950; Madras February to October 1953; local Executive Officer, November 1953; Canberra November 1953 to November 1956; Executive Officer December 1954; Wellington February 1959 to January 1962; Higher Executive Officer (temporary) 23rd May 1962; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

BROWER, David Russell Francis; born 12th September 1918; educated Liverpool College, enlisted in ranks, R.A. (T.A.), 1938; mobilized September 1939; B.E.F., France and Belgium, 1940; seconded to London University, School of Oriental Studies, for 18 months' study of Japanese 1942; commissioned 1944 into Intelligence Corps and posted G.H.Q. (India) as Army Interpreter in S.E.A. theatre; demobilized 1946; India Office 13th December 1946; Information Officer (temporary Senior Information Officer) with seniority from 1st August 1949; Regional Information Officer, Bombay, December 1946 to May 1953 (temporarily Deputy Director, British Information Services, New Delhi, July to October 1950); Regional Information Officer (and Acting Director, British Information Services), Karachi, May 1953 to January 1954; Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Johannesburg, January 1954 to September 1956; Regional Information Officer, Vancouver, November 1956 to October 1961; Principal Information Officer (local) 1st April 1958; Principal Information Officer 1st October 1960.

BROWN, Alan James; born 28th August 1921; educated Wandsworth School 1931-39 and Magdalene College, Cambridge, 1939-41; Class I Modern and Medieval languages Tripos; MA; Infantry O.C.T.U., Sandhurst, November 1941; commissioned Intelligence Corps April 1942; served in West Africa 1942-44 and in North-West Europe (mainly Germany) 1944-47; Major; released April 1947; Intelligence Officer, Grade I, Control Commission for Germany, 1947-48; Assistant Principal 3rd August 1948; Calcutta November 1948 to April 1951; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 9th July 1951; Principal 1st December 1952; Dacca December 1952; Karachi August 1953 to February 1955; Kuala Lumpur July 1957 to July 1962.

BROWN, Benvenuto Dunelm; born 9th October 1916; educated Queen Elizabeth Grammar School, Darlington; m. 1948 Mehra Vacha; on staff of Northern Echo and Northern Despatch 1933-40; served in Royal Navy 1940-46; Private Secretary to H.E. the Officer Administering the Government of Ceylon 1946-47; Temporary Information Officer, India Office, 5th May 1947; Regional Information Officer in Calcutta August 1947 to May 1954; Information Officer 1st August 1949; Senior Information Officer (temporary) 27th November 1951; Senior Information Officer 23rd May 1953; Information Officer, New Zealand, 10th November 1954; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Pakistan, June 1956 to April 1960; Acting Director May to November 1957 and March to July 1959; local Principal Information Officer 9th June 1957; Deputy Director, B.I.S., India, September 1960; Principal Information Officer 1st October 1960; Director of Information Services, Ceylon, February 1964.

BROWNE, Hablot Robert Edgar, CMG (1955), OBE (1942); born 11th August 1905; educated St. George's, Harpenden, 1914-24 and Christ's College, Cambridge, 1924-28; BA 1927; m. 1933 Perta Tainsh (1 d. 1939); Colonial Administrative Service 1928; served in Nigeria 1928-39; Assistant Colonial Secretary, Barbados, 1939; Assistant Secretary, Jamaica, 1943; Deputy Colonial Secretary 1945; Administrative Officer, Class I, Nigeria, 1950; Civil Secretary, Northern Region of Nigeria, 1951-55; Acting Governor, Northern Region of Nigeria, 1954; retired from Colonial Service 1955; Assistant Adviser to the Government of Qatar, Persian Gulf, 1956-57; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st April 1959.

BROWNELEE, George; born 21st July 1922; educated St. Mary's College, Great Crosby; Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 26th June 1939; war service 1942-46; Parachutist Sgt., Royal Artillery, 6th Airborne Division; served in Normandy, Ardennes, Holland and Rhine; wounded; P.O.W. 1945; Executive Officer 14th November 1947; Karachi 1950-54; Information Officer, Dacca, 1957-59; Colombo June 1959 to July 1962; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Acting British Representative in the Maldive Islands September to December 1961; Information Officer, Kaduna, February 1963.

BURNS, Kevin Francis Xavier; born 18th December 1930; educated Finchley Grammar School 1938-48 and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1950-56; Historical Tripos; BA 1953; m. 1963 Nan Pinto; National Service 1948-50; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th October 1956; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State January 1958 to September 1959; Colombo October 1959 to February 1963; Principal 18th April 1960.
BUSTIN, Frederick William; born 27th February 1904; educated Colfe's School, London, 1916-22 and University College, London; w.; Staff of the Civil and Military Gazette, Lahore, 1926-51; Punjab Light Horse (A.F.I.) 1931-44, Commissioned; part-time head of Journalism Department, Punjab University, 1947-49; Information Services, Government of the Federation of Malaya, 1952-59; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 30th May 1960; Madras 1960 to May 1962; Bombay (Temporary Principal Information Officer) October 1962.

BUTTERFIELD, Charles Harris, QC (Singapore); born 28th June 1911; educated Downside School and Trinity College, Cambridge; Barrister at Law, Middle Temple, 1934; Colonial Legal Service, Crown Counsel, Straits Settlements, 1938; war service 1941-46; P.O.W. (Siam); Solicitor-General, Singapore, 1948; Legislative Council; Attorney-General, Singapore, 1955; Council of Ministers and Legislative Assembly, Singapore; retired from Her Majesty's Overseas Civil Service 1958; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd March 1959; Temporary Legal Assistant 25th August 1961.

BYATT, Hugh Campbell; born 27th August 1927; educated Gordonstoun School and New College, Oxford, 1945 and 1948-51; P.P.E.; MA 1951; m. 1954 Fiona Mary MacKenzie Coats (2 s. 1955, 1962; 1 d. 1957); Royal Navy 1945-48; Sub-Lieutenant, R.N.V.R.; attached Faculty of Letters, University of the Sorbonne, 1951; Nigerian Political Service 1952-57; Provincial Administration 1952-55; Office of the Governor, Eastern Nigeria, 1955-56; on special duty in connexion with the Royal Visit to Nigeria 1956; Office of the Premier, Eastern Nigeria, 1957; Assistant Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th December 1957; Information Officer 1st August 1959; Substituting Senior Information Officer 1st September 1959 to 11th March 1961; Bombay March 1961; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

BYRNE, Mary Sarah Nora, MBE (1959); born 24th November 1902; educated King Edward's Grammar School, Camp Hill, Birmingham; Typist, India Office, 25th May 1925; Shorthand-Writer 28th February 1927; Supervisor 22nd March 1934; Supt./Typists 17th November 1939; Higher Clerical Officer (later Executive Officer) 11th June 1944; Higher Executive Officer (temporary) 8th September 1953; Higher Executive Officer 18th October 1954.

C

CAMBRIDGE, Alan John; born 1st July 1925; educated Beckenham Grammar School; m. Thelma Elliot (3 s. 1948, 1952, 1961; 1 d. 1953); enlisted Fleet Air Arm July 1943; RAF April 1944; Flight-Sergeant Air Gunner, 150 Squadron, Bomber Command; released June 1947; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Pensions, 1947; Clerical Officer January 1948; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 25th April 1955; Madras February 1956 to March 1958; Kuala Lumpur September 1959 to July 1961; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Salisbury June 1962.

CARR, Reginald William Stanley; born 6th August 1918; educated Methodist College, Belfast; m. 1942 Hilda Wylie (1 d. 1950; 1 s. 1952); served in Royal Artillery and Royal Corps of Signals 1939-48; commissioned 1942, served in Algeria, Tunisia, Sicily, Italy and Austria 1942 to April 1948; Captain; Temporary Clerk II, Commonwealth Relations Office, 14th April 1948; Delhi April 1948; Bombay May to November 1948; Delhi 1948-52; unestablished Executive Officer May 1952; Madras March 1952 to February 1953; Executive Officer 5th May 1953; Karachi June 1954 to February 1956; Bombay (local Higher Executive Officer) July 1956; Higher Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Nicosia (local Senior Executive Officer) August 1960 to July 1963; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

CARR-GREGG, John Ralph Edward; born 10th January 1920; educated Seaford College 1932-38 and Downing College, Cambridge, 1939-40 and 1946-48; 2nd Class Honours Eng. Lit Tripos 1947; m. 1949 Charlotte Rona (2 s. 1955, 1958); R.A.F. V.R. 1940-46; commissioned 1942; served with No. 139 Wing, 2nd Tactical Air Force in N.W. Europe; nominated by Foreign Office to represent U.K. on 1st United Nations International Intern Programme, Lake Success, July 1948; Editor, Dept. of Public Information, United Nations, 1948-49; News Editor, British Information Services, New York, 1949-52; Commonwealth Relations Office 17th November 1952; Information Officer, Karachi, January 1953; Regional Information Officer, Lahore, October 1954; Regional Information Officer, Melbourne, August 1956; Information Officer 27th November 1957; Senior Information Officer January 1958; Principal Information Officer (local), Melbourne, April 1959; Director of Information Services, Accra, September 1959 to June 1962; Nairobi October 1962; Principal Information Officer (acting) 1st April 1963.

CARTER, Peter Antony; born 16th January 1914; educated Charterhouse and Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, 1932-35; 2nd Class Honours, Law; m. 1946 Mary Hutchinson (1 d. 1948; 1 s. 1951); Executive Officer, Metropolitan Police Office, 1936-39; 50th Royal Tank Regiment 1939-44; Major; wounded, North Africa; Principal, Colonial Office, 19th
April 1947; seconded Nyasaland Government 1951-53; Commonwealth Relations Office 21st November 1960; Dar es Salaam November 1961.

**Carville**, Mervyn Thornton, **MBE** (Military) (1945); born 3rd January 1910; educated St. Mark's and Cheetham Grammar School, Manchester; m. 1939 Renee May Whitmarsh (1 s. 1942); enlisted Royal Signals 1928; retired with rank of Major 1948; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th July 1948; Delhi July 1948 to July 1951; local Executive Officer 1949 to 1951; Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Passport Officer, Salisbury, August 1953 to August 1956; Colombo June 1957 to June 1959; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962.

**Ceuvorst**, Anthony Paul; born 10th July 1935; educated Chatham House Grammar School, Ramsgate; m. Catherine Mary Gilmartin 1959 (2 s. 1960, 1961); Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th March 1956; Delhi 1957–60; Kuala Lumpur 18th February 1961; Higher Executive Officer 26th May 1962.

**Chadwick**, Gerald Williams St. John, **CMG** (1961); born 28th May 1915; educated Lancing College 1929–34 and St. Catharine's College, Cambridge, (Open Exhibitioner, Modern Languages) 1934–37; 2nd Class Hons. Mod. Languages Parts I and II; BA 1937; m. 1938 Madeleine D'Eguilles (2 s. 1939, 1941); Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 6th October 1938; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State September 1939; following demobilization transferred to Dominions Office as Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 6th June 1940; Assistant Private Secretary to successive Secretaries of State 5th August 1940; Principal (temporary) 1st October 1941; Principal 2nd April 1943; Secretary to Parliamentary Mission to Newfoundland June to September 1943; attended Civil Aviation Conferences, Bermuda, December 1945, Newfoundland, January 1946; visited Newfoundland in connection with Economic and Financial Survey February to May 1946; attached United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations, New York, March to May 1949; Ottawa September 1949 to February 1952; Dublin (Counsellor) February 1952 to August 1953; Assistant Secretary October to December 1953; seconded to United Kingdom Delegation to N.A.T.O., Paris, January 1954 to October 1956; Assistant Secretary 6th December 1954; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 22nd August 1960.

**Champion**, John Stuart, **OBE** (1963); born 17th May 1921; educated Shrewsbury 1935–40 and Balliol College, Oxford, 1940–41; 2nd Class Honour Moderations in Lit. Hum.; War BA; m. 1944 Olive Holt (5 s. 1947, 1950, 1954, 1959, 1962; 2 d. 1953, 1956); military service 1941–46; commissioned 11th Hussars (PAO); Western Desert, Tunisia, Italy and N.W. Europe; Cadet, Colonial Administrative Service, Uganda, 1946; District Officer 1948; Assistant Financial Secretary 1956; Deputy Secretary 1959; Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Entebbe. 1960–63; retired from Overseas Civil Service August 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th August 1963.

**Chandler**, Stanley George; born 26th October 1911; educated Prince Albert School, Winnipeg, and Brook Green School, Hammersmith; m. 1939 Miriam Price (1 s. 1945); Sorter, General Post Office, 10th September 1930; Royal Air Force 1940–46; Clerical Officer, Foreign Office (German Section), 8th September 1947; Executive Officer 1st July 1950; Rehabilitation Officer for Control Commission, Germany, July 1950 to December 1953; Commonwealth Relations Office 11th June 1956; Delhi March 1957 to February 1958; Salisbury (local Information Officer) February 1958 to December 1961; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Kuching (local Senior Information Officer) June 1963.

CROMBIE, George Edmond, CMG (1950); born 14th June 1908; educated Aberdeen Grammar School 1916-21, Fettes College, Edinburgh, 1921-26 and Aberdeen University 1926-31; 1st Class Honours Classics; MA; Assistant Principal, India Office, 19th October 1931; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 24th October 1935, and to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 13th August 1936; Principal 1st April 1937; resigned to take up military service 26th May 1942; commissioned in Frontier Force Regiment, Indian Army, and served in India, Middle East and Italy; Mentioned in Despatches; Lieutenant; re-instated as Principal 2nd May 1945; Assistant Secretary 1st March 1947; on deputation to Burma June 1947; Deputy High Commissioner, Rangoon, September 1947; Counsellor, British Embassy, Rangoon, January 1948 to March 1950; Deputy High Commissioner, Madras, June 1951 to September 1953; Counsellor, Ottawa, October 1955 to June 1957; Deputy High Commissioner, Kuala Lumpur, November 1959 to November 1960; Counsellor, Dublin, January 1961.

Sir Francis Edward Hovell-Thurlow, CMG (1961; CMG 1957); born 9th March 1912; educated Shrewsbury School 1925–30 and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1931–34 and April to July 1935; 1st Class Honours Part I Classics, 2nd Class Part II Economics; BA June 1934; m. 1949 Yvonne Wilson (2 s. 1952, 1962; 2 d. 1954, 1958); Assistant Principal, Department of Agriculture for Scotland, 4th November 1935; Dominions Office 24th May 1937; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1st June 1939; Wellington August 1939 to May 1944; Principal 30th October 1941; Ottawa June 1944 to August 1945; Secretariat, Meeting of Prime Ministers, London, April 1946; served with United Kingdom Delegation at Paris Peace Conference 1946 and at United Nations General Assemblies 1945 and 1948; Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1st October 1946; Assistant Secretary 12th December 1948; Delhi November 1949 to June 1952; Establishment Officer 1952 to 1954; Adviser on External Affairs to Governor of Gold Coast 9th February 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Ottawa, April 1958 to September 1959; High Commissioner in New Zealand February 1960 to 1963; High Commissioner in Nigeria February 1964.
