DAVIES, Robert Henry, MBE (1962), DFC (1943); born 17th August 1921; educated John Bright Grammar School, Llandudno, 1932-40; m. 1945 Marion Ainsworth (1 d. 1946; 1 s. 1948); enlisted in R.A.F. in 1940; served in Southern Rhodesia, South Africa and Middle East; released, Flight Lieutenant, April 1946; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Food, 1946; Executive Officer 1947; Higher Executive Officer November 1951; Commonwealth Relations Office 15th February 1954; Delhi September 1954 to December 1957; Senior Executive Officer 13th May 1959; Ottawa August 1959 to July 1962; Chief Executive Officer 7th August 1962.

DAVIES, Vincent Ellis, OBE (1946); born 3rd June 1903; educated St. John's, Leatherhead, and Peterhouse, Cambridge, (Scholar); m. 1939 Rose Trench Temple (3 s. 1940, 1941, 1948; 1 d. 1944); Indian Civil Service 1926-48; served in Bihar and Orissa; in business 1949-51; Colonial Service 1953-59; Federation of Malaya, Singapore and The Gambia; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th January 1960.

DAVIS, Sidney Arthur William, MBE (1960); born 26th July 1901; educated Acland School, London; m. 1927 Mabel Harrison (1 s. 1930; 1 d. 1935); Boy Clerk, War Office, 1916; Assistant Clerk 19th January 1919; Clerical Officer, India Office, 1st March 1920; Higher Clerical Officer 30th October 1941; Executive Officer July 1947; Higher Executive Officer 21st December 1955.

DAWSON, (née Cox), Lady Winifred Lucy, MBE (1936); born 23rd June 1906; educated Clapham County School 1917-22; m. 1957 Sir Vernon Dawson, KCIE (dec. 1958); Typist, India Office, 17th May 1926; Shorthand-Typist 17th July 1928; Clerical Officer 29th July 1932; Executive Officer 3rd February 1941; Higher Executive Officer 2nd February 1948; resigned on marriage 1st August 1957; re-employed in temporary capacity 1st January 1959; reinstated as Higher Executive Officer 16th February 1959.

DEAN, Cecil Roy; born 18th February 1927; educated Watford Grammar School 1938-45; m. 1954 Heather Sturtridge (1 s. 1962); Member, Institute of Public Relations; served in R.A.F. in India and Pakistan 1945-48; Temporary Assistant, Central Office of Information, 6th December 1948; Executive Officer (with seniority from 1st January 1946) 13th January 1949; Information Officer 18th July 1955; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office 18th September 1958; Colombo November 1958; Acting Director, British Information Services, Ceylon, December 1960 to July 1961; Senior Information Officer (local) 1st June 1961 to 15th March 1962; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st June 1962; Vancouver July 1962; Senior Information Officer (notional) 1st August 1963.

DE FREITAS, Sir Geoffrey, KCMG (1961); born 7th April 1913; educated Haileybury, Clare College, Cambridge, (President of the Union) and Yale (Mellon Fellow); Barrister at Law of Lincoln's Inn (Cholmely Scholar), Midland Circuit; m. 1938 Helen Graham Bell (1 d.; 3 s.); R.A. 1939; R.A.F. 1940-45; Member of Parliament 1945-61; Parliamentary Private Secretary to Prime Minister 1945-46; Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Air 1946-50 and for Home Affairs 1950-51; Chairman, Society of Labour Lawyers, 1955-58; successively Opposition front bench spokesman on Housing, Aviation and Agriculture 1951-61; Commonwealth Parliamentary Association Executive 1955-61; Member of Nature Conservancy 1954-58; Council of Royal Society of Arts 1958-61; Delegate to United Nations 1949, to Council of Europe 1951-54 and to NATO Parliamentarians' Conference (of which he was one of the founders and Treasurer) 1955-60; has travelled widely in Africa, America, Europe, India, Japan and South East Asia; High Commissioner in Ghana December 1961 to October 1963; Head of the British Mission in Nairobi December 1963.

DENT, Margaret Edith, MBE (1961); born 30th July 1913; educated Cambridge County School and Spring Grove Secondary School, Isleworth; Writing Assistant, Public Trustee Office, August 1930; Clerical Officer 1934; Dominions Office 8th March 1937; Higher Clerical Officer 20th June 1945; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962.

DICKSON, George; born 23rd May 1931; educated Aberdeen Academy; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 16th June 1952; Karachi March 1954 to April 1956; Penang September 1957 to October 1959; Executive Officer (local) 23rd May 1959; Executive Officer 1st September 1959; Nicosia January 1960 to July 1962; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Kampala October 1962.

DIGGINS, Christopher Ewart; born 2nd July 1920; educated Haileybury College 1933-38 and Trinity College, Oxford, 1938-40 and 1946-47 (History Scholar); 1st Class Honours Modern History 1947; MA; m. 1946 Mary Walls (1 d. 1950; 1 s. 1952); enlisted in ranks of East Surrey Regiment July 1940; R.A. 1941; commissioned September 1941; served in India, Burma, Malaya and Java; Captain; released in Class B April 1946; Senior History Master, Birkenhead School, Cheshire. 1947-48; Assistant Principal,
Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd January 1949; Principal 21st May 1951; Madras February 1952 to January 1956; Canadian National Defence College September 1958 to July 1959; United Kingdom Mission to the United Nations, New York, July 1959 to March 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Kingston, 6th August 1962; Assistant Secretary 1st January 1963.

Dimes, Eileen Mary; born 6th November 1910; educated Crediton High School 1925-29 and Westfield College, London, 1929-32; 2nd Class Honours in English 1932, in Sanskrit 1958; BA; Diploma in Librarianship of University College, London, 1935; Reference Librarian in various libraries 1933-45; Assistant Librarian, School of Oriental and African Studies, 1945-58; Assistant Keeper, 1st Class, India Office Library, 1st January 1959.

Dixon, Sir Charles William, KCMG (1945; CMG 1932), KCVO (1961), OBE (1924); born 29th April 1888; educated Clifton and Balliol College, Oxford; 1st Class Mods. 1909; 1st Class Lit. Hum. 1911; 2nd Class Clerk, Colonial Office, 11th October 1911; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 8th July 1917; First Class Clerk 1st January 1920; Principal 1st April 1920; United Kingdom Delegations to Assembly of League of Nations 1922, to Imperial Conference 1926 and to International Copyright Conference, Rome, 1928; Assistant Secretary, Dominions Office, 4th September 1929; United Kingdom Delegations to Assembly of the League of Nations 1929 and 1930, and to Imperial Conference 1930 and 1937; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 5th August 1940; Adviser on Constitutional Relations 16th May 1948.

Dixon, Edward Colin; born 4th October 1917; educated Rochdale Secondary School; m. 1945 Phyllis Fletcher (2 s. 1950, 1954); R.A.F. 1937-45; served in Egypt 1939-41 and Sudan 1941-43; Temporary Clerk, India Office, 10th December 1945; Clerical Officer 29th July 1947; Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Bombay July 1953 to July 1955; Accra November 1957 to November 1960; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962.

Dobbs, Iain George; born 20th October 1937; educated Dame Allan's School, Newcastle-on-Tyne, 1949-56 and Durham University 1956-59; 1st Class Honours in Economic Studies; BA; National Service 1959-61; 2nd Lieutenant, R.A.E.C.; served in Germany; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd October 1961; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 2nd February 1962; Private Secretary to Minister of State September 1962 to September 1963.

Dorman, Richard Bostock; born 8th August 1925; educated Sedbergh School 1939-43 and St. John's College, Cambridge, (Scholar) 1948-51; Modern and Mediæval Languages Tripos (Russian and Modern Greek) Parts I and II Class I; m. 1950 Anna Illingworth (2 d. 1953, 1959); served with H.M. Forces 1944 to 1948; commissioned in South Staffordshire Regt. 1945; attached Intelligence Corps, Greece, 1946-48; Assistant Principal, War Office, 24th September 1951; Principal 22nd December 1955; Commonwealth Relations Office 5th May 1958; Nicosia August 1960.

Drysdale, William Douglas, MBE (1944); born 27th September 1904; educated Dollar Academy and Edinburgh University; m. 1949 Wendy E. M. Wilson; in business: Malaya 1924-31, London 1932-39; Offices of the War Cabinet and the Minister of Defence 1939-45; British Military Administration, Malaya, 1945-46; Malayan Civil Service 1946-59; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th June 1959; member of United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations Conference on the renewal of the International Tin Agreement, New York, May to June 1960.

Duke, Sir Charles Beresford, KCMG (1956), CIE (1947), OBE (1946); born 19th December 1905; educated Charterhouse and Lincoln College, Oxford; BA 1928; m. Morag Craigie Grant 1938 (2 d.); Indian Civil Service 1928; posted to United Provinces of Agra and Oudh 1929; Indian Political Service 1934; Assistant Private Secretary to the Viceroy 1934-38; N.W. Frontier 1938-43; External Affairs Department, Government of India, New Delhi, 1943-47; retired as Joint Secretary to Government of India; Foreign Service August 1947; served in Pakistan, Iran and Egypt 1947-54; Ambassador to Jordan 1954-56; Ambassador to Morocco 1957-61; retired from Foreign Service October 1961; re-employed in Foreign Office 1961; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st May 1963.

Duncan, Stanley Frederick St. Clare; born 13th November 1927; educated Latymer Upper School, London, 1939-46; Executive Officer, India Office, 7th October 1946; Assistant Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State January to March 1954; Higher Executive Officer 1st March 1954; Ottawa June 1954; Toronto (Information Officer) August 1955 to July 1957; Wellington March 1958 to July 1960; Senior Executive Officer 20th May 1960; Principal 1st September 1961; seconded to Central African Office 19th March 1962.

Dunrossil, the Viscount John William; born 22nd May 1926; educated Fettes College (Scholar) 1940-44 and Oriel College, Oxford, 1944-45 (R.A.F. Short
Course) and 1948–51; 2nd Class Honours in Modern History 1951; MA; m. 1951 Mavis Spencer-Payne (1 d. 1952; 3 s. 1953, 1956, 1962); R.A.F. 1945; qualified pilot, R.A.F. College, Cranwell, 1946; released as Flight Lieutenant 1948 and transferred to R.A.F.V.R. 1948–54 (recalled for flying duties July to October 1951); Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 29th October 1951; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1st August 1952; Canberra March 1954 to April 1956; Principal 6th August 1957; Dacca September 1958; Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Dacca, August 1959 to September 1960; Pretoria/Cape Town January 1961; seconded to Foreign Service December 1961.

DURBIN, Winefred; born 5th September 1921; educated Wade Deacon Grammar School, Widnes, 1932–38; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Labour, 1st September 1938; A.T.S. 1942–46; Executive Officer, Ministry of Food, 3rd October 1949; Higher Executive Officer, Colonial Office, 17th September 1956; Commonwealth Relations Office 2nd January 1961; Lagos July 1963.

DUTTON, James Macfarlane; born 3rd June 1922; educated Winchester College 1936–41 and Balliol College, Oxford, 1941–43; 2nd Class Honours Modern Greats 1943; m. 1958 Jean McAvoy; Temporary Administrative Assistant, Dominions Office, 5th January 1944; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State August 1945; Dublin August 1946 to April 1948; Assistant Principal 21st July 1948; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State August 1948 to January 1949; Delhi December 1950 to January 1953; Principal 1st July 1952; Dacca August 1955; Karachi November 1956 to August 1958; Canberra December 1958 to January 1962; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 19th August 1963.

EAST, Kenneth Arthur; born 9th May 1921; educated Taunton's School, Southampton, 1932–39 and University College, Southampton, 1939–41; m. 1946 Katherine Blackley (3 d. 1951, 1956, 1963; 2 s. 1952, 1955); served in R.A.F. 1942–46; Assistant Principal, India Office, 1st July 1946; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State August 1946 to March 1947 and October 1947 to May 1950; Principal 10th May 1950; Ottawa August 1950 to October 1953; Colombo May 1956 to April 1960; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 14th July 1961; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962.

EDWARDS, Colonel Ivor Cyrus, CVO (1961), OBE (Military). TD; born 5th August 1907; educated Technical College, Newport; m. 1936 Eluned Edwards (1 s. 1939); commissioned (T.A.) Corps of South Wales Borderers December 1926; Tredegar Iron and Coal Co. 1927; Army Staff College, Camberley, 1938–39; active service 1939–45; Mentioned in Despatches May 1940; M.A. to Assistant Director-General, Political Intelligence Department, Foreign Office, 1945; Military Government and Control Commission for Germany, Berlin, 1945–50 (Deputy Chief and Acting Chief of Information Services Division); Embassy, Bonn, 1950–56 (Deputy Head and Acting Head, British Information Services); Commonwealth Relations Office 3rd September 1956; Principal Information Officer 12th December 1957; Temporary Chief Information Officer (B) 16th December 1957; Director, British Information Services, Pakistan, July 1959.

EDWARDS, Reginald James Mindham; born 13th July 1916; educated Colfe's Grammar School, Lewisham; m. 1942 Olive Greenwood (1 d. 1944); Royal Navy 1940; commissioned, Executive Branch, 1941; Light Coastal Forces; demobilised 1946; Lieutenant; Temporary Assistant, India Office, 1946; Clerical Officer 30th January 1947; Executive Officer 1st March 1951; Lahore 1951–53; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962.

ELLIS, Joseph Stanley, OBE (1962); born 29th November 1907; educated Woodhouse Grove School and University College, London; m. 1933 Gladys Harcombe (1 s. 1947), Lancashire Daily Post (Preston) 1929–30; Manchester Evening News 1930–40; Manchester Guardian and Manchester Evening News (Fleet Street Office) 1940–41; Higher Executive Officer, Publications Division, Ministry of Information, 1941–45; Temporary Information Officer, Dominions Office, 1945; Information Officer, Canberra, 1945–48; Senior Information Officer, Central Office of Information, 1948 (established 6th April 1950); Commonwealth Relations Office 1st August 1951; Regional Information Officer, Karachi, March 1952; Director, British Information Services, Pakistan, (local Principal Information Officer) March 1953; Director, United Kingdom Information Services, Canberra, November 1955; Chief Information Officer (B) 1st December 1957; Director, British Information Services, Kuala Lumpur, 1958 to 1962.

EMERY, Eleanor Jean; born 23rd December 1918; educated Western Canada High School, Calgary, 1933–37 and at Glasgow University 1937–41; 2nd Class Honours in History; MA; Temporary Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 15th September 1941; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1st July 1942; Ottawa December 1945 to January 1948; Assistant Principal 4th May 1948; Principal 1st January 1949; Private
Secretary to Secretary of State 2nd March 1950 to 17th February 1952 and accompanied him on visits to Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Ceylon 1950 and to the Union of South Africa, Southern Rhodesia and the High Commission Territories 1951; Delhi April 1952 to June 1955; Capetown/Pretoria April 1958 to January 1962; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 2nd April 1962; Assistant Secretary 1st January 1963.

Evans, Francis Roy; born 4th February 1926; m. 1952 Connie Roberts (1 d. 1953); war service in R.N. 1944-46; Executive Officer, Ministry of Food, 23rd March 1947; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st May 1954; Colombo February 1955 to June 1957; Dacca September 1957 to December 1960; Higher Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 22nd August 1961; Port of Spain June 1962; Principal 1st August 1963.

Ewans, Martin Kenneth; born 14th November 1928; educated St. Paul's School 1943-47 and Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, (Major Scholar) 1949-52; Classical Tripos Parts I and II Class I; MA; m. 1953 Mary Tooke (1 s. 1954; 1 d. 1957); National Service 1947 to 1949 (2nd Lt. R.A.); Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 16th July 1952; Karachi January 1954; Private Secretary to the Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State January 1956; Principal 6th August 1957; Ottawa July 1958 to September 1961; Lagos February 1962.

F

Fair, Alan S.; born 17th February 1926; educated Ellesmere College 1935-43 and Worcester College, Oxford, 1943-46; 2nd Class Honours Jurisprudence; MA; attended First Devonshire Course at Oxford and the London School of Oriental and African Studies 1947-48; m. 1952 Lalage Milner-White (1 s. 1953; 1 d. 1957); Colonial Administrative Service and H.M. Overseas Civil Service 1949-60; Temporary Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 21st March 1960; Temporary Principal 1st August 1961; Principal 6th December 1961; Ottawa September 1963.

Fingland, Stanley James Gunn; born 19th December 1919; educated Royal High School, Edinburgh; m. 1946 Nellie Lister (1 d. 1949; 1 s. 1953); General Post Office 23rd November 1936; served in Royal Corps of Signals August 1939 to March 1947; commissioned December 1940; served in North Africa, Sicily, Italy and Egypt May 1943 to November 1946; Major; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd August 1948; Delhi October 1948; Bombay July 1950 to April 1951; Principal 20th September 1949; Secretary of United Kingdom Delegation to meeting of Colombo Plan Consultative Committee, Karachi, March 1952; Canberra September 1953 to July 1956; on loan to Government of Nigeria (Lagos) as Adviser on Commonwealth and External Affairs to Governor-General with local rank of Assistant Secretary May 1958 to September 1960; member of United Kingdom delegation to annual conferences of Commission for Technical Co-operation in Africa South of the Sahara in Monrovia 1959 and Tananarive 1960; Assistant Secretary 1st April 1960; Lagos 1st October 1960; Adviser on Commonwealth and External Affairs to the Governor-General of the West Indies, Port of Spain, July 1961, and, on dissolution of Federation, to Governor of Trinidad April 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Trinidad and Tobago, 30th August 1962; Salisbury January 1964.

Footman, Charles Worthington Fowden, CMG (1952); born 3rd September 1905; educated Rossall School and Keble College, Oxford; 3rd Class Honours in Theology; BA 1929; MA 1947 Joyce Marcelle Law (2 d. 1948, 1949; 1 s. 1952); Administrative Officer, Zanzibar, 1930-47; seconded to East African Governors' Conference 1942-43; seconded to Colonial Office 1943-47; Financial Secretary, Nyasaland, 1947-51; Chief Secretary 1951-60; Chairman, Public Services Commissions, Tanganyika and Zanzibar, 1960-61; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 24th January 1962.

Forster, Kenneth David; born 14th July 1922; educated Wade Deacon Grammar School, Widnes; m. 1960 Glenys Bacon (1 d. 1962); Clerical Officer, India Office, 27th June 1939; enlisted Royal Navy September 1941 to June 1946; Executive Officer 8th January 1948; Karachi February 1952 to June 1955; local Higher Executive Officer 17th April 1954; Higher Executive Officer 1st July 1955; Canberra February 1957 to June 1960; Senior Executive Officer 24th August 1960.

Forster, Oliver Grantham, MVO (1960); born 2nd September 1925; educated Hurstpierpoint College 1939-44 and King's College, Cambridge, (Open Scholarship 1943) 1944 and 1948-51; 1st Class Honours in History 1950; BA; MA 1952; m. 1953 Beryl Evans (2 d. 1957, 1960); served in R.A.F. 1944-48 (in Western Europe); Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 16th July 1951; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State September 1953 to January 1954; Karachi July 1954 to September 1956; Principal 1st November 1956; Madras April 1959 to August 1962; seconded to Foreign Service November 1962 and posted to Washington.
FOWLER, Dennis Houston, MBE (1963); born 15th March 1924; educated Alleyn's School, Dulwich; m. 1944 Lilias Burnett (2 s. 1946, 1952; 1 d. 1949); Temporary Clerk, Colonial Office, June 1940; served with R.A.F. September 1942 to December 1946; Clerical Officer, India Office, 6th January 1947; Executive Officer 12th May 1950; Colombo April 1951 to February 1955; Higher Executive Officer 23rd July 1955; Karachi November 1955 to April 1959; Private Secretary to the High Commissioner August 1958 to April 1959; Senior Executive Officer 24th August 1960; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation 24th July 1961; Dar es Salaam November 1961.

FOWLER, Robert William Doughty, CMG (1962); born 6th March 1914; educated Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School, Mansfield, 1923-33 and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, 1933-37; Modern Languages Tripos Parts I and II Class II; m. 1939 Margaret MacLeod (twins and d. 1941); Assistant Commissioner, Burma Civil Service, 23rd September 1937; Defence Department, Government of Burma, March 1941 to December 1943; commissioned March 1944 for service in Civil Affairs Service, Burma; Senior Civil Affairs Officer and Deputy Commissioner from October 1945; Additional Secretary to Governor of Burma from January 1947; retired from the Burma Civil Service January 1948; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, April 1948; Assistant Secretary 1st October 1952; seconded to Foreign Service as member of United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations in New York January 1951 to February 1953; Deputy High Commissioner, Karachi, December 1956 to December 1958 (with periods as Acting High Commissioner); Imperial Defence College January 1959; local Assistant Under-Secretary of State January 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Ottawa, January 1960 to October 1962, Acting High Commissioner 26th April to 23rd May and 18th July to 3rd October 1961; Assistant Under-Secretary of State October 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Lagos, November 1962.

FRASER, James Duncan, CVO (1961), MBE (1947); born 11th January 1915; educated Haileybury College (Organ Scholar) January 1929 to August 1933 and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, (Organ and Classical Scholar) 1933-38; Classical Tripos 1st Class Honours 1936; m. 1943 Margaret Arnold (2 s. 1945, 1947); appointed to Indian Civil Service 1937; served in Punjab 1938-47; Deputy Commissioner in Amritsar from 1945; Principal, Ministry of Works, 13th September 1947; Commonwealth Relations Office 19th February 1951; member of United Kingdom Delegation to African Defence Facilities Conference, Dakar, 1954; Canberra July 1955; Kuala Lumpur April 1958; Assistant Secretary 1st April 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Bombay, July 1960 to February 1963.

FREE, Alan Leslie; born 15th July 1932; m. 1953 Janet Gore (2 d. 1958, 1959); Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 18th July 1949; National Service March 1951 to September 1953; Immigration Officer, Home Office, July 1954 to December 1955; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd January, 1956; Accra August 1956 to 1959; Dacca (local Higher Executive Officer) January 1961 to 1962; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963; Nairobi October 1963.

FRENCH, Neville Arthur Irwin; born 28th April 1920; educated Selhurst Grammar School and London School of Economics; BSc (Econ.) 2nd Class Honours; m. 1945 Joyce Greene (1 s.; 2 d.); war service 1939-45; Chief Radio Officer, Fleet Auxiliary; Colonial Administrative Service, Tanganyika, 1948; District Commissioner 1950-60; Principal Assistant Secretary (External Affairs), Prime Minister's Office, Dar es Salaam, 1961-63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th June 1963; seconded to Central African Office June 1963.

FRYER, Stanley; born 19th January 1918; educated Lowestoft Grammar School 1929-36; m. 1940 Audrey Harwood (2 d. 1943, 1947); Executive Officer, Ministry of Health, 17th September 1936; enlisted in Territorial Army (Royal Engineers) June 1939; commissioned in Royal Artillery June 1941; served overseas in Iraq and in G.H.Q., India; released with rank of Major June 1946; Higher Executive Officer, Ministry of National Insurance, 1st July 1946; Senior Executive Officer 11th September 1950; Chief Executive Officer (designate) 26th August 1957; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th February 1958; Kaduna July 1960 to July 1963; Acting Deputy High Commissioner November 1961 to April 1962 and November 1962 to January 1963.

FULLERTON, Peter George Patrick Downing; born 17th January 1930; educated Radley College 1943-48 and Magdalen College, Oxford, 1949-53; 2nd Class Honours in Lit. Hum.; MA; m. 1962 Elizabeth Evelyn Stevens; National Service Commission in Queen's Own Hussars 1949; District Officer, Kenya Civil Service, 1953-63; District Commissioner 1959 and 1962; retired from Overseas Civil Service under limited compensation scheme 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st March 1963; Private Secretary to the Minister of State 30th September 1963.

FURNESS, Alan Edwin; born 6th June 1937; educated Eltham College 1948-55 and Jesus College, Cambridge, 1955-58;
History Tripos Part I Class I, Part II Class II Div I; BA; MA 1962; Bartle Frere Exhibitioner 1958–60; Research Fellow of the University College of West Indies, Jamaica, 1959–60; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd January 1961; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State April 1961 to February 1962; Delhi April 1962.

G

GABB, Frank; born 22nd October 1917; educated St. Leonard's Collegiate School, Hastings, and the Paston School, North Walsham, Norfolk; commissioned R.A.F., General Duties (Flying) Branch, 1937–40; North Devon Herald 1934–37; Lincolnshire Echo 1940–41; Eastern Daily Press 1941–42; Eastern Evening News 1942–43; B.B.C. Home News 1943–45; War Office contract: Department of Broadcasting, Singapore, 1945–46; Malayan Establishment contract: Chief Editor, Radio Malaya, Singapore, 1946–49; radio freelance 1949–51; Air Ministry Information Officer (Honorary Squadron Leader, R.A.F.V.R.), Headquarters, 2nd Allied Tactical Air Force, Germany, 1951–54 (established 15th February 1951); Information Officer, Ministry of Works, 1954–58; Commonwealth Relations Office 29th December 1958; Information Officer, Accra, 28th April 1959; Delhi 19th February 1960 to June 1963; Regional Information Officer November 1961; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

GAMBOLD, John Henry David; born 14th August 1922; educated Haverfordwest Grammar School; m. 1951 Muriel Crabbe (2 s. 1953, 1954; 2 d. 1957, 1962); Sorting Clerk and Telegraphist, General Post Office, 1939; Royal Air Force May 1941 to August 1946; Sergeant; Mentioned in Despatches; Postal and Telegraph Officer 1947; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd October 1949; Calcutta March 1951 to June 1954; Executive Officer 16th April 1952; Karachi February 1956 to February 1958; Lahore (local Higher Executive Officer) July 1958 to June 1962; Higher Executive Officer 18th June 1959; Senior Executive Officer 22nd August 1961.

GANDEE, John Stephen, OBE (1958); born 8th December 1909; m. (1) May Degenhardt (dec. 1954) (2 d. 1938, 1945; 1 s. 1942); (2) Junia Henman (née Devine) (1 step-s. 1956; 1 step-d. 1957; 1 d. 1962); Post Office Sorting Clerk and Telegraphist 26th July 1925; Clerical Officer, India Office, 12th May 1930; Executive Officer 4th June 1937; Higher Executive Officer 7th November 1941; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 2nd December 1946; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 3rd March 1947; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 6th November 1947 to 20th January 1949; Principal 1st January 1949; Ottawa January 1952 to August 1954; seconded to the Bechuanaland Protectorate June 1959; seconded to Office of High Commissioner for Basutoland, Bechuanaland Protectorate and Swaziland May 1960; seconded to Bechuanaland Protectorate January to June 1961; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 4th September 1961; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962.

GARLAND, Audrey de Forges; born 21st June 1917; educated Hollington Park School 1928–36 and Oxford University 1936–39; BA Honours; MA; Ministry of Information 1940–44; Far Eastern Bureau, New Delhi, 1944–45; Senior Temporary Assistant, Dominions Office, 9th July 1946; Assistant Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st August 1949; Information Officer 20th January 1958; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

GARNER, Sir Joseph John Saville, KCMG (1954); CMG 1948), Hon. LL.D, University of British Columbia (1958), Hon. LL.D, Toronto (1959), Registrar, Order of Saint Michael and Saint George, 1962, born 14th February 1908; educated Highgate School 1916–26 (of which he became a Governor in 1962) and Jesus College, Cambridge, 1926–29; Mod. and Med. Languages Tripos Part I Class II Division I, Part II Class I; BA 1930; m. 1938 Margaret Beckman (2 s. 1939, 1940; 1 d. 1947); assistant modern language master, Haileybury College, September 1929 to April 1930; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 27th October 1930; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 6th March 1935; Principal 1st July 1937; accompanied Lord De La Warr to Australia 1937–38; Private Secretary to Secretary of State 5th August 1940; accompanied Sir Geoffrey Shakespeare in 1941 and Mr. Attlee in 1942 to Newfoundland and Canada; Ottawa June 1943 to July 1946; Deputy High Commissioner, Ottawa, July 1946 to May 1948; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 8th May 1948; Meeting of Commonwealth Foreign Ministers, Colombo, January 1950; acted as temporary Deputy Under-Secretary of State 28th December 1950 to 6th June 1951; Deputy High Commissioner, Delhi, June 1951 to April 1953; Deputy Under-Secretary of State 20th April 1953; High Commissioner in Canada November 1956 to July 1961; Permanent Under-Secretary of State 1st January 1962.

GAUTREY, Peter, CVO (1961); born 17th September 1918; educated Abbotsholme School 1931–35; m. 1947 Marguerite Uncles (1 s. 1948; 1 d. 1951); Clerical Officer, Home Office, 18th March 1936; Executive Officer (in absentia) 1st July
CHAPTER 50

Biographical Notes

1942; enlisted in ranks of 12th R.H.A., (H.A.C.) October 1939; commissioned May 1941; Captain 1945; served in India and Burma April 1942 to October 1945; released April 1946; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th January 1948; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 26th September 1948 to 31st December 1948; Principal 1st January 1949; Dublin October 1950 to April 1953; Delhi September 1955 to September 1957; member of United Kingdom Delegation to UNESCO, Delhi, 1956; Delhi (local Assistant Secretary) August 1960; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Bombay, March 1963.

GIBSON, David Bruce; born 15th November 1926; educated Christ's Hospital; Fellow of the Library Association 1955; m. 1960 Sheila Sonia Rao (1 s. 1961); Westminster Public Libraries 1944; Army 1944-48; Librarian IV, Board of Trade, 1952; Librarian III, India Office Library, August 1963.

GILL, Peter; born 16th February 1924; educated Woodford House School, Birchington; m. 1948 Betty Mary Bond (1 s. 1957; 1 d. 1954); Royal Navy 1942-46; Clerical Officer (temporary), India Office, 8th July 1946; Clerical Officer 18th April 1947; Executive Officer 1952; Karachi April 1954 to April 1956; Salisbury April 1957 to April 1960; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Canberra June 1962.

GILMORE, Brian Terence; born 25th May 1937; educated Wolverhampton Grammar School 1947-54 and Christ Church, Oxford, (Classical Exhibitioner; Hon. Scholar 1956) 1954-58; First Class Hon., Classical Hon. Mods. 1956; Passmore-Edwards Scholar 1957; First Class Hons., Lit. Hum. 1958; m. 1962 Rosalind Fraser; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 29th September 1958; Private Secretary to the Permanent Under-Secretary of State 11th July 1960, to Joint Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State June 1961, to Secretary of State March 1962.

GILMOUR, Alan James; born 2nd May 1911; educated Ellesmere College and University College, London; Royal Tank Regiment 1939-45; served in North Africa and Italy; Ministry of Works June 1950; Assistant Information Officer, Board of Trade, July 1954; Information Officer, Ministry of Education, January 1955; Senior Information Officer, Scottish Office, (in charge London Press Office), April 1956; Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Dar es Salaam, March 1958, Director December 1959, and Zanzibar January 1960; Principal Information Officer 9th December 1961; Director, British Information Office, Dar es Salaam January 1962; Delhi February 1964.

GOLDS, Anthony Arthur, MVO (1961); born 31st October 1919; educated King's School, Macclesfield, 1930-38 and New College, Oxford, (Scholar) 1938-39 and 1946-48; Honours School of English; m. 1944 Suzanne Young (1 s. 1947; 1 d. 1952); enlisted in ranks of York and Lancaster Regiment 1939; commissioned June 1940; R.A.C. 1941-46; served in India 1941-44; Interpreter, German P.O.W. Camp, 1945-46; Lieutenant; released May 1946; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 21st July 1948; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 20th September 1949; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 20th March 1950; Principal 14th April 1951; Calcutta and Delhi April 1951 to July 1953; seconded to Foreign Service and posted to Ankara as First Secretary January 1957; Head of Chancery August 1957 to January 1959; Karachi May 1959 to June 1961; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 24th April 1962; Assistant Secretary 1st January 1963.

GOLDSMITH, Alexander Kinglake; born 16th January 1938; educated Sherborne 1951-55 and Trinity College, Oxford, (Minor Scholar in History) 1958-61; National Service 1956-58; seconded from D.C.L.I. to Queen's Own Nigeria Regiment; 2nd Lieutenant; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th September 1961; training course in Indian Affairs, School of Oriental and African Studies, October 1962; Delhi August 1963.

GOODMAN, Douglas Wickham; born 26th November 1922; educated Wanstead County High School 1932-39; m. 1950 Ann Fuller (1 d. 1962); Clerical Officer, India Office, 10th May 1939; enlisted R.A.F. September 1941; Telecommunications Research Establishment 1943-46; released August 1946; Executive Officer 3rd February 1947 (subsequently seniority from 1st January 1946); Wellington June 1951 to January 1955; Higher Executive Officer 15th June 1955; Karachi July 1955 to April 1959; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 22nd August 1961.

GORDON, James, OBE (1955; MBE 1934); born 27th December 1898; educated Tottenham County School; m. 1927 Edith Ham; Boy Clerk, New Scotland Yard, August 1914 to November 1916; served with Queen Victoria's Rifles with rank of rifleman November 1916 to February 1919; T.C. III February 1919 to October 1921; Clerical Officer, India Office, 3rd October 1921; services lent to Indian Statutory Commission 1929-30; personal assistant to Secretary, General Indian Round Table Conferences, 1930, 1931 and 1932; Secretary to Burma Delegation to Joint Select Committee on India 1933; Executive Officer 6th November 1934; Staff Officer 13th July 1939; Superintendent, Telegraph and Mails Branch, 9th
August 1943; Principal 10th July 1944; United Kingdom Delegation to G.A.T.T. in Geneva November to December 1954.

GORDON-SMITH, David Gerard; born 6th October 1925; educated Rugby School 1939-43 and Trinity College, Oxford, 1943-4 and 1947-48; 2nd Class Hon. Jurisprudence; m. 1952 Angela Kirkpatrick Pile (1 d. 1958; 1 s. 1961); Royal Navy March 1944 to October 1946 as T/Sub-Lieutenant, R.N.V.R.; called to the Bar, Inner Temple, 1949; Legal Assistant, Colonial Office, 1st August 1950; Senior Legal Assistant 1st January 1954; Commonwealth Relations Office 16th September 1963.

GORE, Michael Edward John; born 20th September 1935; educated Xaverian College, Brighton, 1948-52; m. 1957 Monica Marina Shellish (2 d. 1958, 1960); Member, Institute of Public Relations; general reporter, Evening News, Portsmouth, 1952-53; National Service 1955; Short Service Commission, General List, for Army Public Relations Service 1956; Staff Captain, Public Relations, Security Forces, Cyprus, 1956-59; Temporary Information Officer, Air Ministry, 1959; Deputy Command Information Officer, Middle (later Near) East Air Force, 1960-63; Information Officer February 1962; Commonwealth Relations Office 17th June 1963; Jesselton August 1963.

GORE-BOOTH, Sir Paul Henry, KCMG (1957; CMG 1949), KCVO (1961); born 3rd February 1909; educated Eton and Balliol College, Oxford; m. 1940 Patricia Mary Ellerton (2 s.; 2 d.); appointed a Third Secretary, Foreign Office, 12 October 1933; Vienna April 1936; Tokyo December 1937; Second Secretary 12th October 1938; Shanghai October to November 1941; Washington December 1942; First Secretary 1st November 1943; member of the United Kingdom Delegation to International Food Conference, Hot Springs, 1943; U.N.R.R.A. Conference, Atlantic City, 1943; Dumbarton Oaks Conversations, Washington, and International Civil Aviation Conference, Chicago, 1944; San Francisco Conference 1945; Foreign Office 25th October 1945; Secretary to the United Kingdom Delegation to the First Meeting of the United Nations General Assembly, London, January 1946; Counsellor and Head of Refugee and United Nations Economic and Social Departments 1st July 1947; Head of European Recovery Department February 1948; Director of British Information Services in the U.S.A. 21st October 1949; Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary, Rangoon, 6th November 1953; Deputy Under-Secretary of State, Foreign Office, in charge of economic affairs 15th October 1956; High Commissioner in India October 1960.

GORHAM, Robin Stuart; born 15th February 1939; educated Sutton County Grammar School 1950-57 and Oriel College, Oxford, 1958-61; 2nd Class Honours in Philosophy, Politics and Economics; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th September 1961; Resident Clerk December 1961 to September 1962; Ottawa November 1962.

GREATEREX, Cecil Ernest, MBE; born 2nd January 1920; educated English School, Cairo, Victoria College, Alexandria, and American University, Cairo; m. 1941 Regina Mary Savides (1 d. 1943); Société Egyptienne des Industres Textiles 1938-40; Commissioned 1941; Special Services, Libyan Arab Force, 1942; Civil and Political Affairs Officer, Cyrenaica, 1943-44; Staff Major, Political Affairs, Cyrenaica and Tripolitania, 1945-47; Political Liaison Officer to King Idris of Libya 1944-47; Political Affairs Officer, Civil Affairs Agency, Cairo, 1947-48; Political Liaison Officer to Chief Administrator, Tripolitania, 1948-52; Temporary Second Secretary, British Embassy, Libya, 1952-55; First Secretary 1955-56; First Secretary, Foreign Office, 1956-58; Principal Information Officer, Colonial Office, October 1958; Enugu October 1958 to December 1961; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st October 1960; local Senior Information Officer (Acting Principal Information Officer); Information Officer 20th February 1961; Regional Information Officer, Lahore, April 1962; Acting Deputy High Commissioner May to August 1963; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963; Dar es Salaam December 1963.

GREENHILL, Basil Jack; born 26th February 1920; educated Bristol Grammar School 1932-38 and Bristol University 1938-40 and 1945-46 (T. H. Green Scholar in Modern Studies); Philosophy and Economics Honours Class II Division I 1946; BA; m. (1) 1950 Gillian Stratton (dec. 1959) (1 s. 1955); (2) 1961 Ann Giffard; enlisted in ranks of R.N.V.R. August 1941; commissioned October 1942; transferred to Air Branch May 1943; Lieutenant (A); on staff of Director of Naval Air Radio, Admiralty, June 1944; released October 1945; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 23rd September 1946; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 13th May 1948, to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 23rd September 1948; Principal 1st January 1949; Dacca, Karachi and Peshawar August 1950 to February 1954; Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, between November 1952 and April 1953; member of United Kingdom Delegation to 9th Session of United Nations General Assembly in New York 1954; seconded to Foreign Service and posted to British Embassy, Tokyo, April

1955 to March 1958; member of the United Kingdom Delegation to the United Nations Conference on the Law of the Sea, Geneva, 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Dacca, May 1958 to December 1959; Assistant Secretary 1st December 1958; Counsellor, Ottawa, September 1961.

GRIER, Patrick Arthur, OBE (1963); born 2nd December 1918; educated Lancing College 1932-35, Lausanne University 1935-36 and King's College, Cambridge, 1936-39; BA 1939; MA 1946; m. 1946 Anna Fraembs (1 d. 1962); military service 1939-47; Major R.A.; served with Indian Mountain Artillery, NWFP and Burma; Kreis Resident Officer of Mönchengladbach (Military Government of Germany) 1946-47; Nigerian Administrative Service 1947; Administrative Officer Class III 1952; Clerk to Executive Council, Northern Nigeria, 1953-54; seconded to West African Inter-territorial Secretariat, Accra, for Anglo-French liaison 1955-57; Administrative Officer Class II, Northern Nigeria, 1958; Principal Assistant Secretary to Governor of Northern Nigeria 1959-63; Administrative Officer Class I 1960; retired from H.M.O.C.S. 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th May 1963.

GRIFFITH, Owen Glyn, MVO (1954); born 19th January 1922; educated Oundle School 1936-40 and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, 1940-41; m. 1949 Rosemary Earl (2 s. 1957, 1959); O.C.T.U., Sandhurst, December 1941; commissioned May 1942 in Welsh Guards; served in Algeria and Tunisia 1942; wounded; released in November 1943; District Officer, Uganda, 1944-51; Assistant Secretary 1951-52; Private Secretary to Governor 1952-54; District Commissioner 1954-61; Permanent Secretary, Uganda Ministry of Commerce and Industry (later Economic Affairs), 1961-63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th August 1963.

GROVE, Harold John; born 22nd August 1915; educated Alleyn's School, Dulwich, 1924-32; m. 1956 Irene Arbon (2 d. 1957, 1960); Royal Corps of Signals 1940; served in North Russia, France, Belgium and Holland; released 1946; Clerical Officer, Burma Office, 2nd December 1946; Executive Officer 24th September 1951; Calcutta, November 1952 to February 1956; Salisbury August 1959 to July 1962; Higher Executive Officer (local) August 1959; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962.

GRUBB, Geoffrey Harold; born 3rd February 1930; educated Salt High School, Yorkshire, 1940-48; m. 1953 Pamela Betts (3 d. 1955, 1958, 1961); Executive Officer, Colonial Office, September 1948; H.M. Forces October 1948 to June 1950; Higher Executive Officer, Colonial Office, 6th March 1956; seconded to Western Region of Nigeria as Private Secretary to the Governor January 1959 to November 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 13th February 1961.

GWINNETT, Frank Edward; born 17th August 1915; educated Salisbury School and East Kildonan High School, Winnipeg, Canada; m. 1946 Joan Adeline Smith (1 d. 1947); Gloucester Regiment 1936-40; R.A.S.C. 1940-46; Warrant Officer Class I; served in India, Burma and North-West Germany; Temporary Clerk II, India Office, 19th February 1946; Clerical Officer 1st January 1948; Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962.

HALL, Alfred Charles; born 2nd August 1917; educated Oratory School and Polytechnic, London; m. 1946 Clara Strunina (5 s. 1946, 1954, 1956, 1959, 1963); London County Council 1937; war service 1939-41; Foreign Office: Temporary Secretary, North Africa, Saudi Arabia, Iran and U.S.S.R., 1942-46; Press and Information Officer, London County Council, 1946-49; on loan to Commonwealth Relations Office (Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Ottawa) 16th August 1949; Senior Information Officer (temporary Principal Information Officer) with effect from 1st August 1949; Principal Information Officer 1st May 1953; Director, British Information Services, Pakistan, August 1955; Deputy Director, British Information Services, India, December 1956 to 1960; Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Services, Nigeria, 1960 to 1963; Director, British Information Services, Nigeria, (local Chief Information Officer (B)), June 1961; Chief Information Officer (B) (temporary) June 1963; Director of Information Services, Australia, January 1964.

HALL, Ralph Issott; born 11th October 1903; educated Mill Hill School; m. 1941 Phyllis Spencer (1 s. 1945); on staff of Civil and Military Gazette, Lahore, 1923-31; sub-editor, Times of India, 1937; joined Royal Indian Naval Volunteer Reserve in 1939 as Paymaster-Lieutenant and called up 3rd September 1939; released for service as Information Officer, Government of India, April 1940; Assistant Press Adviser, Government of India, November 1941 to October 1942; Deputy Director of Information, Government of Bombay, October 1942 to April 1946; deputy News Editor, Times of India, June to November 1946; Press Officer (Specialist), India Office, 2nd December 1946; Senior Information Officer 1st August 1949; Information Officer, Melbourne, August 1959; local Principal Information Officer 4th July 1959.
HALL, Wilfrid Edward; born 11th March 1911; Bermuda 1934-40; military service 1940-46; Ghana (Gold Coast) 1947-57; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th February 1958; Acting Regional Information Officer, Lahore, March 1958; Rawalpindi November 1959; Chittagong (local Senior Information Officer) October 1961; Colombo March 1962 to June 1963.

HALLILEY, Alec Addison, MBE; born 19th January 1912; educated Christ's Hospital, Royal Military College, Sandhurst, and St. Andrews University 1948-51; 1st Class Honours, School of History; m. 1943 Rosemary Constance Campbell Ogilvie (2 s. 1944, 1952; 1 d. 1945); Indian Army 1936-48 (acting Lieutenant-Colonel); Senior Lecturer, Department of Modern Subjects, Royal Military Academy, Sandhurst, 1951-55; Head of Department 1955-61; Head of Planning and Research Unit (Senior Research Officer), Commonwealth Relations Office, seconded from War Office) 23rd May 1961; transferred to Commonwealth Relations Office 22nd August 1961.

HAMILTON, William Aitken Brown, CMG (1950); born 3rd June 1909; educated Aberdeen Grammar School and Aberdeen University; 1st Class Honours Classics 1931; MA; m. 1936 Barbara Gano (1 s. 1948); Assistant Principal, Board of Education, 2nd November 1931; Private Secretary to Permanent Secretary 1st August 1934; Principal 19th October 1936; Assistant Public Relations Officer 3rd November 1936; Publicity Officer 18th May 1937; Principal, Physical Recreation Committees, 1st June 1937; Joint Secretary to Committee on Nursing Services 4th December 1937; on loan to Ministry of Food 25th October 1939; Head of Division 1st July 1942; Assistant Secretary 1st November 1943; returned to Ministry of Education 1st November 1944; Under-Secretary and Director of Establishments 1st November 1946; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (Director of Establishments and Organisation), Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st March 1949; seconded to United Nations as Director of Personnel March 1959 to April 1962.

HAMMETT, Harold George; born 2nd August 1906; educated St. Olave's 1918-25 and Clare College, Cambridge, 1925-28; Classical Tripos Part I Class II; History Tripos Part II Class II; BA 1928; m. (1) 1936 Daphne Margaret Vowler (1 s. 1937); m. (2) 1947 Natalie Moira Sherratt (1 d. 1949; 1 s. 1953); Malayan Civil Service 1929-57; served in Federated Malay States (Selangor and Negri Sembilan), Straits Settlements (Malacca, Penang and Singapore) and Unfederated Malay States (Johore, Kedah and Kelantan); commissioned R.A.F. February 1942; P.O.W. (Sumatra) 1942-45; retired from post of Resident Commissioner, Malacca, on Merdeka (Independence) Day 31st August 1957; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 24th November 1958.

HAMPSHIRE, George Peter, CMG (1963); born 1st December 1912; educated Repton and Oriel College, Oxford; 2nd Class Hon. Mods. and 2nd Class Lit. Hum.; m. 1956 Eve Buhler; Assistant Principal, War Office, 24th October 1935; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 12th February 1937; Principal 19th June 1939; Assistant Secretary, Control Office for Germany and Austria, 1st January 1946; Foreign Office, German Section, April 1947; Treasury September 1948; on loan to Commonwealth Relations Office (Secretary, Finance, Ottawa) September 1948 to June 1951; transferred to Commonwealth Relations Office 16th July 1951; Deputy High Commissioner, Dacca, February 1953 to March 1955; Imperial Defence College 1956; seconded to Foreign Service and posted as Counsellor, Buenos Aires, August 1957 to February 1960; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1st July 1961; Director of Establishments and Organisation 1st October 1962.

HANBURY, Clement John; born 15th October 1913; educated Monmouth 1925-31; m. 1937 Joan Bull (1 d. 1944); Assistant Clerk, Lydney Guardians Committee, 1932-1937; Assistant Estates Officer, Gloucestershire County Council, 1937-1940; Relieving Officers Certificate, Poor Law Examination Board, 1939; County District Officer, Gloucestershire County Council, 1940-42; enlisted Royal Armoured Corps May 1942; commissioned, Royal Army Service Corps, April 1943; Captain; released October 1946; Battery Commander, Royal Artillery, Territorial Army, 1949-53; County District Officer, Gloucestershire County Council, 1946-48; Executive Officer, National Assistance Board, July 1948; Headquarters Auditor 1953-56; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th April 1956; Delhi November 1957; Senior Executive Officer (temporary) 1st September 1961; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1962.

HAND, Ronald Richard; born 24th February 1924; educated Epsom Grammar School; m. 1954 Nancy Irene Oliver (1 s. 1960; 1 d. 1961); R.A.F. 1942-46; Clerical Officer, India Office, 10th December 1946; Delhi July 1949 to February 1953; Executive Officer 25th July 1953; Karachi July 1955 to July 1957; Peshawar April 1959 to April 1961; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Jamaica January 1963.

HANKINS, Muriel, MBE (1961); born 5th October 1924; educated Mary Datchelor Girls' School, Camberwell, 1936-40 and
Municipal College, Bournemouth, 1941; Clerk, Woolwich Borough Council, January 1942; Temporary Clerk, India Office, February 1944 to August 1946; re-engaged 10th March 1947; Clerical Assistant 24th May 1948; Clerical Officer 22nd July 1949; Executive Officer 31st December 1955; Salisbury 1956; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962.

HANWELL, Reginald Thomas; born 24th November 1906; m. 1940 Rose Ersser; Messenger, G.P.O., 8th January 1921; Sorter 17th June 1925; Clerical Officer, India Office, 21st January 1935; Higher Clerical Officer 7th December 1945; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960.

HARRISON, Francis Anthony Kitchener; born 28th August 1914; educated Winchester and New College, Oxford; Classical Honour Mods. Class I; Lit. Hum. Class II; MA; m. 1955 Sheila Stevenson (2 s. 1956, 1960; 1 d. 1957); Assistant Principal, India Office, 1st November 1937; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 17th February 1941; Principal 30th August 1943; Delhi September 1949 to September 1951; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 1st January 1954, (substantive) 7th November 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, 31st March 1956 to 24th August 1959; Deputy High Commissioner, Wellington, August 1961.

HAWKINS, George Henry; born 15th May 1921; educated Greenwich Central School, London, 1932-37; m. 1943 Helen Adams (2 d. 1945, 1955; 1 s. 1949); volunteered and enlisted Royal Navy June 1940; served as Radar Operator, North Atlantic and Malta convoy escort duty, March 1941 to March 1942; attached R.A.F. for liaison duties April to September 1942; seconded to Royal Norwegian Navy, Coastal Forces Group, for special operations against enemy-occupied Norway, January to October 1943; Instructor, R.N. Training Establishment (Radar), November 1943 to March 1946; released March 1946; Petty Officer; Temporary Clerk, India Office, April 1946; Clerical Officer (Reconstruction Competition) 1st January 1948; Executive Officer 24th May 1951; Higher Executive Officer 18th June 1959; Passport Officer, Canberra, October 1952 to January 1956; Passport Officer, Capetown, June 1960; seconded to Foreign Service December 1961; Capetown June 1962 to October 1963.

HAYDEN, Jack Llewellyn, OBE (Military) and U.S. Legion of Merit; born 26th April 1903; educated Strand School and King's College, London; m. 1931 Margaret Acklam; Ministry of Information, Press Censorship, 1939-41; war service 1941-46; Lieutenant-Colonel 1943; Foreign Office (Information Officer, Northern Italy) 1946-47; Commonwealth Relations Office (Information Officer, Melbourne) 15th September 1949; Information Officer, with seniority from 1st August 1949; Senior Information Officer (temporary), 10th January 1952; Regional Information Officer, Dacca, October 1953; Director, British Information Services, New Zealand, June 1956; Senior Information Officer 20th January 1958; delegate to meeting of SEATO Council of Ministers, Wellington, 1959; Principal Information Officer (local) 1st April 1959.

HAYWARD, Robert; born 21st June 1911; educated Haberdashers' Aske's Reporter or Sub-Editor, Daily Herald, Daily Sketch, Daily Mail, Daily Express, and Assistant Picture Editor, News Chronicle, 1930-39; war service September 1939 to September 1945 (commissioned); Sub-Editor, Daily Mail, 1945, Daily Sketch 1947; Ifunda Technical Training Centre (founder), Overseas Food Corporation, Tanganyika, December 1947; Assistant to Chief Mechanical Engineer, Geita Gold Mining Company, Tanganyika, 1949; East African Standard, Nairobi, 1950; Editor, Baraza (Swahili language newspaper) and Tazama (Swahili language weekly magazine), 1955; Temporary Senior Information Officer September 1961; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Uganda; Acting Director, B.I.S., December 1961 to March 1962 and January to March 1963; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th October 1962.

HEAD, The Rt. Hon. Antony Henry, Viscount Head of Thrope in the County of Wilts., PC (1951), KCMG (1961), CBE (1946), MC (1940); born 19th December 1906; educated Eton and the Royal Military College, Sandhurst; m. 1935 Lady Dorothea Ashley-Cooper (2 s.; 1 d.); commissioned in the 15th/19th Hussars 1926; Life Guards 1928; Brigade Major, 20th Guards Brigade, 1940; Assistant Secretary, Imperial Defence Committee, 1940-41; Staff Officer with the Guards Armoured Division in the United Kingdom; served in Combined Operations Headquarters, Brigadier; took part in the planning of invasion of Europe as Army representative with the Director of Plans for Amphibious Operations; Member of Parliament for Carshalton 1945; Secretary of State for War 1951-56; Minister of Defence 1956-57; High Commissioner in the Federation of Nigeria 1st October 1960 to November 1963; High Commissioner in Malaysia October 1963.

HEAP, Peter William; born 13th April 1935; educated Bristol Cathedral School and Merton College, Oxford; 2nd Class Hons. P.P.E. 1959; m. 1960 Helen Wilmending; National Service, Gloucestershire Regt. and Gold Coast Regt., 1954-56; 2nd Lieut.; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, August 1959; Dublin
July to November 1960; Ottawa November 1960 to December 1962; Colombo (local Principal) March 1963.

HELLINGS, Donald Edward Herbert, MBE (1963); born 16th May 1923; m. 1948 Margaret Kirby (1 s. 1959; 1 d. 1961); Post and Telegraph Officer, G.P.O., 2nd September 1941; joined R.A.F. July 1942, served as Navigator, Bomber Command (Europe) and Transport Command (S.E. Asia); returned to G.P.O. January 1947; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd August 1949; Executive Officer 30th December 1952; Wellington February 1953 to February 1956; Salisbury August 1956 to August 1959; Higher Executive Officer (local) 1st April 1959, (substantive) 18th June 1959; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 8th November 1960 and Parliamentary Clerk 6th February 1961; Nicosia September 1963; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 1st August 1963.

HEPTINSTALL, Leslie George; born 20th August 1919; educated Thames Valley County School and London University; BSc (Econ), 2ns Class Honours; m. 1949 Marion Nicholls (1 d. 1954); military service 1939-46; Captain, Royal Artillery; served in Middle East, Mediterranean and North-West Europe; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 1948; Principal 1951; seconded to West African Inter-Territorial Secretariat, Accra, 1955; Acting Chief Secretary 1958; Acting Administrator, West African Research Office, 1959; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th February 1961; Wellington May 1962.

HICKLING, Ronald; born 3rd January 1915; educated Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School, Mansfield; m. 1947 Doreen Arnold (twin s. 1950; 1 d. 1959); war service, Fleet Air Arm, 1943-46; with R.C.A.F. 1944; Editorial Staff, Nottingham Guardian, 1946-48; Regional Press Officer, North Midlands, Central Office of Information, February 1948; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st August 1949; Senior Information Officer with seniority from 1st August 1949; Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Union of South Africa, August 1949 to January 1954; Deputy Director, British Information Services in Pakistan, January 1954; Deputy High Commissioner (acting), Peshawar, February to April 1956; British Information Services, Lahore, May 1956 to May 1957; Principal Information Officer 1st December 1957; Director, British Information Services, Cyprus, May 1962.

HICKMAN, John Kyrle; born 3rd July 1927; educated Tonbridge School (Scholar) 1941-45 and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, (Scholar) 1945-48; History Tripos, Parts I and II Class I; BA 1948; m. 1956 Jennifer Love (1 d. 1960); military service (commissioned in Royal Artillery) 1948-50; Assistant Principal 15th October 1948; War Office 25th May 1950; Principal 1st August 1955; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st June 1958; Wellington July 1959 to April 1962.

HICKS, Reginald Jack; born 22nd January 1922; educated Enfield Grammar School; m. 1946 Jean Sims (1 d. 1949); Clerical Officer, Ministry of Works, July 1938, R.A.F. October 1941; flying training and instructor in U.S. Army Air Corps 1942-43; served in Middle East, India, Burma and Malaya (No. 28 (FR) Squadron) 1944-46; Flight Lieutenant; demobilized and returned to Ministry of Works October 1946; Executive Officer (in absentia) November 1944; Chief Clerk, Ministry of Works, Delhi, (Temporary Higher Executive Officer) January 1951 to November 1951; Higher Executive Officer November 1951; seconded to the Public Services Commission, Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, May 1957 to December 1957; Senior Executive Officer 20th March 1959; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st November 1961.

HONEYBALL, Phyllis Ada; born 14th March 1905; educated Winterbourne Road School, Thornton Heath, and Pitman's College, Croydon; Research Assistant, Ministry of Information, December 1939; in charge of Administration, M.O.I. Photographic Unit, Accra, Gold Coast, October 1942 to December 1943; Information Department, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st April 1946; Assistant Information Officer 1st August 1949; Information Officer (local), Winnipeg, August 1958 to August 1961; Information Officer 1st August 1959; Information Officer, Commonwealth Information Centre, Marlborough House, March 1962 to August 1963; Senior Information Officer (temporary) 19th August 1963.

HORNER, John Bayley Middleton; born 9th February 1907; educated Radley College; m. (1) 1940 Raymonde Heygate (1 d. 1942); m. (2) 1957 Eve Hewson; military service 1939-46; Staff Captain 1939; DAQMG 1941; AQMG 1942; Colonel i/c Coordination 1945; Administrative Staff School 1941; Managing Director, Winchlass & Co. Ltd., 1947-50; War Office 1951-53; graduated U.S. Psychological Warfare School 1953; Chief of Public Affairs, S.H.A.P.E., 1954-56; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 24th June 1959; Regional Information Officer, Durban, 17th November 1959; seconded to Foreign Service 1st December 1961 to August 1962; Senior Information Officer, Johannesburg, 1st March to August 1962; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Cyprus, December 1962; Information Officer (local Senior Information Officer) 18th March 1963.
CHAPTER 50

Biographical Notes

HOWARD, John Norman; born 19th January 1918; educated Groombridge, Littlehampton; m. 1941 Joffrette Marie Abela (1 d. 1953); Local Government Service 1934-39; commissioned 1941; served with B.E.F. in France and Belgium 1939-40; Middle East, North Africa, Sicily and Italy 1940-46; demobilized 1946; returned to Local Government Service until 1947 then took up journalism; Egyptian Gazette, Cairo, 1948-49; Arab News Agency, Cairo, 1949-51; Globe News Agency, Bombay and Madras, 1951-53; Arab News Agency/Reuters in Egypt, Lebanon, Syria, Persian Gulf, Iraq, Sudan, Aden, North Africa and London 1953-59; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1959; Information Officer, Kuala Lumpur, 1959; Information Officer 17th April 1961; Accra May 1963.

HOWELL, Michael Edward; born 2nd May 1933; educated Newport High School 1944-51; m. 1958 Joan Little (1 s. 1962) National Service with R.A.F. 1951-53; Executive Officer, Colonial Office, November 1951; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st May 1958; Karachi 1959-61; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Bombay May 1962.

HUBBARD, Richard Thomas; born 18th September 1912; educated Acton County School 1924-28; m. (1) 1940 Hilary Ffolliott (1 s. 1941); m. (2) 1952 Freda Winters; R.A.F. 1928-47; Clerical Officer, India Office, 11th August 1947; Executive Officer (1949 Forces examination) 11th March 1950; Delhi November 1955 to February 1959; local Higher Executive Officer November 1955; Higher Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Calcutta 1960-62.

HUGHES, John Turnbull, OBE (1959); born 8th June 1919; educated City Grammar School, Chester, and Liverpool University; war service 1940-45; Private Secretary to Governor of Bengal 1945-46; India Office 2nd December 1946; Deputy Director, Information, India, December 1946 to September 1952; Senior Information Officer (Temporary Principal Information Officer) 4th December 1951; Principal Information Officer 1st February 1953; Director, British Information Services in India (local Chief Information Officer (B) until 1955) 1953-59; Chief Information Officer (B) 8th November 1955; Temporary Chief Information Officer (A) 1st April 1961.

HUGO, Lieutenant-Colonel John Mandeville, CVO (1959), OBE (1947); born 1st July 1899; educated Marlborough College and Royal Military Academy, Woolwich; m. 1952 Joan Hill; commissioned Royal Artillery 1917; transferred to Indian Cavalry 1925; Military Secretary to Governor of Bengal 1938-40; rejoined 7th Light Cavalry 1940; Military Secretary to Governor of Bengal 1946-47; Assistant Ceremonial Secretary, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1948-52; Ceremonial and Protocol Secretary and Gentleman Usher to the Queen 1952.

HUMPHREY, William Swift; born 16th February 1939; educated Uppingham School (Scholar) 1952-56 and Clare College, Cambridge, (Foundation Scholar) 1959-62; Economics Tripos Class I: BA; served in Malaya in Royal Artillery 1957-59; 2nd Lieutenant; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th August 1962; Resident Clerk April to July 1963.

HUNT, Sir David Wathen Strather, KCMG (1963; CMG 1959), OBE (Military); born 25th September 1913; educated St. Lawrence College, Ramsgate, 1927-32 and Wadham College, Oxford, (Scholar) 1932-37; 1st Class Honour Mods. and 1st Class Lit. Hum.; MA 1938; Thomas Whitcombe Greene Prize; Diploma in Classical Archaeology; Fellow of Magdalen College, Oxford, 1937-39; m. 1948 Pamela Medawar, (2 s. 1952, 1954); enlisted January 1940; commissioned May 1940 and served in Middle East and Greece June 1940 to January 1943; Tunisia, Sicily and Italy 1943 to 1945; on staff of General Alexander 1942-45; Colonel G.S. (Intelligence); awarded OBE and U.S. Bronze Star and Mentioned three times in Despatches; organized compilation and wrote part of Official History of Italian Campaign June 1945 to May 1946; accompanied Field-Marshal Alexander to Canada to help in final preparation of despatches on campaigns in Africa, Sicily and Italy June 1946 to May 1947; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 24th June 1947; Principal 14th January 1948; Capetown/Pretoria September 1948 to March 1950; seconded to Prime Minister's Office as one of his Private Secretaries 3rd April 1950 to 30th September 1952; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 1st October 1952; United Kingdom Delegation to Commonwealth, Finance Ministers' Conference in Sydney January 1954; Deputy High Commissioner, Lahore, February 1954 to May 1956; Assistant Secretary 1st January 1954; United Kingdom Delegation to L.C.A.F.E., Bangalore, January to February 1956; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1959; accompanied Prime Minister as adviser on tour of Africa January to February 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Lagos, 1st October 1960 to August 1962; High Commissioner in Uganda 9th October 1962.

HUNT, Kenneth John Ashby; born 4th August 1912; educated Highgate Junior School, Hendon Secondary School and Merchant Taylors' School 1921-30; m. 1947 Mary Georgina Fey (2 s. 1947, 1949); commissioned in 2nd Battalion, The Rangers, the KRRC (TA), June 1939;
seconded to King's African Rifles 1940; served in UK, East Africa, Somaliland and Ethiopia; released with rank of Major September 1945; Elders and Fyffes Ltd. 1930-39 (sales and public relations); Kenya Government 1945-63 (Administration 1945-51; Information Services 1952-63); member of H.M.O.C.S. 1947; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd May 1963; Delhi June 1963.

Hunt, Rex Masterman; born 29th June 1926; educated Coatham School, Redcar, 1937-44 and St. Peter's Hall, Oxford, 1944 and 1948-50; 2nd Class Honours, Jurisprudence; BA; m. 1951 Mavis Amanda Buckland (1 d. 1962); enlisted R.A.F., September 1944; qualified pilot, R.A.F. Hunt, Roland Charles Colin; born 19th March 1916; educated Rugby 1929-34 and Queen's College, Oxford, 1934-39; 2nd Class Classical Mods.; 2nd Class Lit. Hum.; m. 1939 Pauline Garnett (3 s. 1941, 1943, 1951; 2 d. 1947, 1953); Indian Civil Service September 1938 to 1947; served in Madras as Sub-collector and Joint Magistrate and later as Joint Secretary, Board of Revenue; Temporary Administrative Assistant, Colonial Office, 20th October 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 29th January 1948; Principal 1st January 1949; Karachi February 1948 to March 1950; member of United Kingdom Delegation to African Defence Facilities Conference in Nairobi 1951; Capetown/Pretoria October 1952 to January 1955; Assistant Secretary 29th August 1955; Kuala Lumpur November 1956; Deputy High Commissioner, Kuala Lumpur, September 1957 to October 1959 (Acting United Kingdom High Commissioner June to November 1958); Imperial Defence College 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Karachi, February 1962.

James, Sir (John) Morrice Cairns, KCMG (1962: CMG 1957), CVO (1961), MBE (Military); born 30th April 1916; educated Bradfield and Balliol College, Oxford; m. 1948 Elizabeth Piesse (d. 1948, 1950; 1 s. 1956); Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 2nd October 1939; served in Royal Navy and Royal Marines 1940-45; released with rank of Lieutenant-Colonel; Principal (in absentia) 10th March 1944; Cape Town/Pretoria March 1946 to April 1947; Assistant Secretary 12th April 1949; Deputy High Commissioner, Lahore, April 1952 to November 1953; Imperial Defence College Course January 1954; Deputy High Commissioner, Karachi, January 1955; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (temporary) February 1957; accompanied Prime Minister as adviser on his visits to India, Pakistan, Ceylon, New Zealand and Australia January to February 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Delhi, October 1958 to July 1961; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 4th November 1958; High Commissioner in Pakistan October 1961.

LAIRD, Edgar Ord, MBE (1958); born 16th November 1915; educated Rossall School 1929-34 and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, 1935-38; Mathematical Tripos Part I Class III, Geographical Tripos Part I Class II (II) and Part II Class II (I); BA (1938); m. 1940 Heather Lonsdale Forrest (d. 4 d. 1944, 1952, 1953, 1956); Surveyor, Colonial Survey Service, Uganda Protectorate, February 1939; commissioned in East African Engineers October 1939 (later transferred to Royal Engineers); served East Africa, Middle East, United Kingdom and Malaya; Director of Studies, Civil Affairs Staff Centre, Wimbledon, August 1944; Major; released in Malaya March 1946; appointed to Malayan Civil Service January 1947 and held various appointments including Secretary to Government, Federation of Malaya, 1953-55 and Secretary for External Defence, Federation of Malaya, 1956; Secretary, Federation of Malaya Constitutional Com-

LANCASTER, Joan Cadogan, MA, FSA, FRHistS; born 2nd August 1918; educated Charles Edward Brooke School and Westfield College, London, (Exhibitor); 2nd Class Honours in History 1940; BA; MA (Paleography and Diplomatic) 1943; Associate of the Library Association 1943; Assistant Archivist, City of Leicester, and Assistant Librarian, University College, Leicester, 1940-43; A.T.S. 1963-46; Librarian, Command School, London, 1945-46; Archivist, City of Coventry, 1946-48; Assistant Librarian, Institute of Historical Research, 1948-60; Assistant Keeper, 1st Class, India Office Records, 19th April 1960; Honorary Editor of Archives 1957-63; author of "The Coventry forged charters: a reconsideration", Bibliography of historical works issued in the United Kingdom, 1946-56, etc.

McENTEE, Peter Donovan, OBE (1963); born 27th June 1920; educated Haileybury College 1934-37; m. 1945 Mary Elizabeth Sherwood; military service 1939 (Lieutenant), King's African Rifles; service in Abyssinia, Ethiopia, Somaliland, Madagascar and Burma; released (Major) 1945; District Officer, Colonial Service, 1946; Senior Assistant Secretary and African Courts Officer 1959; Senior District Commissioner and Principal of the Kenya Institute of Administration 1960; retired from Colonial Service 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th September 1963.

McINDOE, William Ian; born 11th March 1929; educated Sedbergh School 1942-47 and Corpus Christi College, Oxford, 1947-51; Classical Hon. Mods. Class I; Lit. Hum. Class II; MA; m. 1954 Irene Mudie (1 d. 1957; 1 s. 1959); National Service 1951-53 (2/Lt. with 2 R.H.A. in Germany); Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 14th October 1953; Canberra May 1956; Principal 20th June 1958; Salisbury June 1958 to March 1962; Private Secretary to Secretary of State June 1962; seconded to Cabinet Office as Private Secretary to Secretary to Cabinet August 1963.

MACKILLIGIN, David Patrick Robert; born 29th June 1939; educated Winchester and Pembroke College, Oxford; 2nd Class Honours in Philosophy, Politics and Economics 1961; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 21st August 1961; Salisbury May to August 1962; Karachi September 1962.

McKINNEY, Ian Martin; born 3rd June 1930; educated Royal Grammar School, Lancaster, and Queen's University, Belfast; BSc (Econ.); m. 1960 Carol Wickham-Jones; reporter Belfast Telegraph 1953-54; Temporary Assistant Information Officer, H.Q., Northern Ireland District, 1954-55; served Royal Artillery 1955-57; commissioned 1956; Temporary Assistant Information Officer, Central Office of Information, 1958-59; Temporary Information Officer 1959-60; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st April 1960; Information Officer, Accra, June 1960 to May 1963; Montreal September 1963.

MACLENNAN, Sir Ian Morrison Ross, KCMG (1957: CMG 1951); born 30th October 1909; educated Hymers College, Hull, 1918-28 and Worcester College, Oxford, 1928-32; 2nd Class Honour Mods. 1930; 1st Class Philosophy, Politics and Economics 1932; MA; Gladstone Research Student, St. Deiniol's Library, Hawarden, 1932-33; m. 1936 Margherita Jarratt (1 d. 1938; 1 s. 1940); Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 31st October 1933; accompanied Agricultural Adviser, Colonial Office, on tour to West African Colonies
October 1935 to February 1936; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State, Dominions Office, 15th February 1937; Ottawa April 1938 to April 1943; Principal 2nd January 1939; Private Secretary to Secretary of State December 1943 to May 1944; Capetown/Pretoria May 1945 to August 1948; Assistant Secretary, Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th May 1946; United Kingdom High Commissioner in Southern Rhodesia February 1951, Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland October 1953 to May 1955; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (in absentia) 7th May 1954; High Commissioner in Ghana 1957 to 1959; Ambassador, Dublin, January 1960 to 1963; High Commissioner in New Zealand 1964.

McMullen, Murray; born 29th June 1909; educated Imperial Service College 1923-27 and Jesus College, Oxford, 1928-31; 2nd Class Honours, School of Modern Languages; BA 1931; m. 1945 Fulvia Schenk; war service with Intelligence Corps 1940-46; Temporary Research Specialist, Ministry of Information, 1946; Information Officer, Central Office of Information, 1948; Principal, Colonial Office, 1956; Director, British Information Services, Kenya, 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 18th July 1962; Kuching 1963.

MacConochie, Kenneth John; born 1st July 1911; educated King's College School 1921-29 and University of London 1934-36; 2nd Class Honours in French; m. 1939 Muriel Crowther (1 s. 1942; 1 d. 1944); BBC (Home Service) 1936-41; R.A.F. 1941; commissioned 1943; Russian interpreter with Photographic Reconnaissance Unit, Murmansk, 1944; British Military Mission, Moscow, 1945; demobilized 1946; rejoined BBC (European Service) 1946-58; seconded to Colonial Office as Temporary Principal Information Officer 1958; United Kingdom Information Officer, Ibadan, 1958-61; Temporary Principal Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st October 1960; resigned from BBC 7th September 1961; Senior Information Officer 8th September 1961; Montreal September 1963 (Local Principal Information Officer).

McQuiggan, John, MBE (1955); born 24th November 1922; educated St. Edward's College, Liverpool; m. 1950 Elsie Hadler (3 s. 1956, 1959, 1963; 1 d. 1961); Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 26th February 1940; enlisted in R.A.F. 1st June 1942; West Africa 1943-44; Italy 1945; Malta 1946; Instructor in Mathematics and Geography under R.A.F. Educational and Vocational Training Scheme 1946; demobilized January 1947 and returned to Dominions Office; Executive Officer 14th November 1947; Canberra July 1950 to May 1954; Higher Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; joint Secretary (Administration) to United Kingdom delegation to Commonwealth Finance Ministers' Conference, Sydney, January 1954; Lahore November 1954; British Information Services, Lahore, (acting Regional Information Officer), 4th May 1957 to 29th March 1958; Senior Information Officer (local), Canberra, 15th May 1958 to 2nd May 1961; Acting Director, United Kingdom Information Services in Australia, March to July 1959; Senior Information Officer 1st October 1960; Regional Information Officer, Enugu, (local Principal Information Officer) December 1961.

MacRae, Alastair Christopher Donald Summerhayes; born 3rd May 1937; educated Rugby, Lincoln College, Oxford, (2nd Class Honours in English Literature 1961) and Harvard University (Henry Fellow in International Relations); m. 1963 Mette Willett; military service 1956-57; commissioned, Royal Navy; Dewar Travel Scholarship in Africa 1958; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th September 1962; Dar es Salaam January 1963.

Maher, John Desmond; born 17th January 1922; educated De la Salle College, Weaste, 1933-38; m. 1949 Elizabeth Marian Entwistle (1 d. 1950; 1 s. 1953); Assistance Clerk, Unemployment Assistance Board, June 1938-41; served with Royal Navy April 1941 to January 1947; Ty S/Lt (S), R.N.V.R., August 1945; Assistant Secretary to Capt. Air (East Indies) 1946; Executive Officer, National Assistance Board, September 1948; Captain, R.A., (T.A.R.O.) 1955; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st September 1960; Delhi 1st May 1961.

Mann, Stanley Robert; born 19th July 1922; educated Santley School and Morley College, D.C.; m. 1952 Freda Ilett (1 d. 1958); General Post Office 1941; war service 1942-46; Royal Navy (Communications Branch): Western Approaches (Russian and North African Convoys), Nore Command (Patrols), Portland Command (Staff); Postal and Telegraph Officer 1948; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Health, 1949; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th May 1957; Delhi January 1958 to February 1960; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Karachi April 1962.

Manvell, Eric Manvell; born 20th June 1916; educated Queen Mary's School, Basingstoke; m. 1937 Joan Irene Welding (2 s.; 2 d.); sub-editor, Central News, Fleet Street, 1933-37 and Hampshire Chronicle 1937-40; volunteered 1940, Coldstream Guards; commissioned into Royal Hampshire Regiment October 1940; Adjutant, 70th Battalion, 1942-43; G.S.O. III, 146 Brigade, 1944-45; Mentioned in Despatches; G.S.O. II
MARSH, Gilbert Lingard; born 15th December 1907; educated Osborne House School and Southern College of Art; member of the Institute of Public Relations; freelance publicity overseas (U.S.A., South America, etc.) 1928-38; enlisted Coldstream Guards October 1939; commissioned Royal Hampshire Regiment April 1940; transferred Royal Armoured Corps 1942; served North Africa (8th Army) and Palestine (as DAPM); demobilized with rank of Captain; Central Office of Information July 1947; Temporary Senior Information Officer and deputy to Chief Regional Officer (Southern Region); Information Officer, Air Ministry, 1954; Information Staff, MEAF, Egypt and Cyprus, 1954-56; National Savings Committee 1958; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st October, 1959; Calcutta 1960; Regional Information Officer, Madras, October 1962 to March 1963; seconded to Central African Office (temporary Senior Information Officer) October 1963.

MARTIN, Stanley William Frederick; born 9th December 1934; educated Bromley G.S. 1945-53, University College, Oxford, 1955-58 (Second Class Honours in Jurisprudence) and Inner Temple (Scholar); m. 1960 Hanni Hansen (1 s. 1962); National Service 1953-55 (2nd Lieut. R.A.S.C.); Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st August 1958; Assistant Private Secretary to the Secretary of State September 1959 to April 1962; Canberra (local Principal) June 1962; Principal 25th October 1962.

MARTIN, Victor Cecil; born 12th October 1915; educated Jesus College, Cambridge; Classical Tripos Part I Class II Division I, Part II Class I; Assistant Principal, Office of Works, 14th October 1938; Ministry of Education 9th January 1939; military service October 1939 to December 1945; Major; Intelligence Corps; served in Persia and Iraq Command October 1941 to September 1945; Principal 1st January 1945; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office 29th April 1948; transferred December 1949; Delhi February 1951 to April 1954; Delhi December 1956 to January 1960; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962.
