MASEFIELD, John Thorold; born 1st October 1939; educated Repton School (Scholar) 1953-58 and St. John's College, Cambridge (Exhibitioner and Scholar) 1958-62; Classical Tripos Part I Class II Division I, Archaeological and Anthropological Tripos Parts I and II Class I; m. 1962 Jennifer Trowell; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 3rd September 1962; Private Secretary to the Permanent Under-Secretary of State 12th August 1963.

MASH, Walker Sidney Joseph; born 19th January 1913; educated Stonehouse St. School, Clapham, S.W.4; m. 1951 Edna Nicholls; enlisted R.A.M.C. September 1939; served in France and East Africa Command; demobilized QMS September 1945; Temporary Assistant, India Office, 5th November 1945; Clerical Officer 1st January 1950; Executive Officer 3rd September 1955; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

MATTHEWS, Frederick; born 5th September 1919; educated Mosley and Birmingham Schools of Art; Diploma in Art and Design; m. 1948 Hebe Moulaki (3 children); enlisted Royal Warwickshire Regt. 1939; B.E.F., France, "Vickforce" 1940; 24th (Guards) Independent Brigade Group, London District, 1940-41; Commissioned, Royal Irish Fusiliers, 1942; Italy 1944; Staff Captain, 3 Corps, Salerno, 1944; Greece 1944; Major, Staff H.Q., Land Forces, Greece, 1945; released 1946; resident Athens 1947; Consultant, E.C.A. Information Services, Athens, 1949-52; Production Officer, Public Information Office, Government of Cyprus, 1956-59; Senior Information Officer, Government of Cyprus, London Office, 1959; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th March 1960; Calcutta (local Senior Information Officer) April 1960 to June 1963; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

METCALF, Maurice Rupert, CMG (1954), OBE (1945); born 5th May 1905; educated Oundle School 1915-22 and Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, 1924-27; BA (Agriculture); m. 1928 Dorothy Ring (2 s. 1929, 1933); Assistant Secretary, Horace Plunkett Foundation (Agricultural Co-operation), 1927-32; Assistant Secretary, National Farmers' Union, 1932-41; Secretary, Empire Fruits Council, 1931-41; appointed to Ministry of Food as Head of Branch (temporary) 2nd June 1941; Assistant Private Secretary to Minister June 1942; Principal Private Secretary to Minister 3rd May 1943; transferred to Office of Minister of Reconstruction as Private Secretary to Minister 13th November 1943, and to Office of Lord President of the Council as Personal Assistant to Lord President 15th June 1945; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 1st July 1945; re-transferred to Ministry of Food 13th August 1945: Principal, with
acting rank of Assistant Secretary, 1st January 1946; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st October 1949; Deputy United Kingdom High Commissioner in Ceylon September 1950 to January 1953; High Commissioner, Federation of Rhodesia and Nyassaland, August 1955 to February 1961; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1st August 1960; seconded to Central African Office 19th March 1962.

MIDDLETON, Donald King; born 24th February 1922; educated King Edward's School, Birmingham, Saltley College and St. Luke's College, Exeter; Certificate in Education (distinction); m. 1945 Elizabeth Ryder (1 d. 1949); Civil Defence Corps 1942-46; Regional Organiser, Midland Region Blood Transfusion Service, 1946-52; Administrative Officer (Publicity), Birmingham Regional Hospital Board, 1952-58; Information Officer, Ministry of Health, 1958-61; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th September 1961; Lagos (local Senior Information Officer) September 1961; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

MILES, Frank Stephen; born 7th January 1920; educated Daniel Stewart's College, Edinburgh, and St. Andrew's University, (Scholar) 1938-42; MA in History; Commonwealth Fund Fellowship, Harvard University, U.S.A., 1946-47; degree of Master in Public Administration; m. 1953 Joy Theaker (3 d. 1956, 1958, 1960); enlisted as rating in Fleet Air Arm January 1942; commissioned October 1943; Lieutenant (A) Observer; released July 1946; Assistant to Curator of Historical Records of Scotland, Edinburgh, 1947-48; Temporary Assistant Principal, Scottish Home Department, 18th February 1948; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st May 1948; Wellington February 1949 to April 1952; Principal 1st July 1952; Dacca February 1954; Lahore August 1955 to May 1957 (Acting Deputy High Commissioner May to June 1956); Accra August 1959 to May 1962; Acting Deputy High Commissioner February to May 1962; Kampala September 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Dar es Salaam, June 1963; Acting High Commissioner 15th June 1963.

MILES, John Edwin Alfred, OBE (1961: MBE 1952); born 14th August 1919; educated Hornsey County School 1930-37; m. 1952 Barbara Ferguson (2 s. 1956, 1958; 1 d. 1960); Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 15th February 1937; joined Queen's Royal West Surrey Regiment May 1940; commissioned in North Staffordshire Regiment February 1941; attached Royal Indian Army Service Corps February 1942; Major August 1943; served in India, Persia, Iraq, Palestine and Egypt; released September 1946; Higher Clerical Officer (later Executive Officer) (in absentia) 1st December 1944; returned to Dominions Office August 1946; Wellington May 1948 to June 1951; Higher Executive Officer 3rd February 1951; Principal 14th August 1952; Calcutta July 1953 to November 1956; Adviser, Governor-General's Office, Port of Spain, June 1961; Adviser on Commonwealth and External Affairs to Governor of Jamaica November 1961; Kingston August 1962.

MILLS, Frank; born 3rd December 1923; educated King Edward VI Grammar School, Nuneaton, 1934-42 and Emmanuel College, Cambridge; m. 1953 Trilby Foster (1 s. 1959; 1 d. 1961); served in R.A.F.V.R. 1942-45 as radar mechanic; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st November 1948; Karachi February 1949; Dacca May 1949 to January 1951; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 1st December 1952; Principal 29th September 1953; Secretary, United Kingdom Delegation to the Colombo Plan Conference, Ottawa, September to October 1954; Cape-town/Pretoria January 1955 to March 1958; Private Secretary to the Secretary of State 2nd June 1960; Kuala Lumpur August 1962; Singapore December 1963.

MINOGUE, Martin Michael; born 23rd December 1937; educated King James' Grammar School, Knaresborough, 1950-57 and Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, (Minor Scholar) 1959-62; Historical Tripos Part I Class I; Part II Class II, Division I; National Service with R.A.F. 1957-59; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th September 1962.

MITCHELL, William Arthur; born 2nd July 1904; m. 1928 Edith Salvage; Telegraphist, G.P.O., 17th May 1921; Clerical Officer, Admiralty, 2nd October 1944; India Office 21st January 1946; Higher Clerical Officer 4th May 1946; Executive Officer 4th July 1949; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962.

MOLYNEUX, John Anthony; born 1st August 1923; educated Lancing College 1937-41 and Worcester College, Oxford, 1946-48; Honours Degree in Lit. Hum. 1948; MA; m. 1958 Patricia Dawson (3 s. 1960, 1961, 1962); enlisted as radar mechanic in Royal Navy November 1941; commissioned January 1944; served in North Sea Patrol 1942-43 and in Pacific 1944-45; released April 1946 as T/Sub-Lieutenant (Sp. Sc.), R.N.V.R.; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 6th April 1949; Delhi August 1950 to December 1952; Principal 1st July 1952; Karachi September 1955; member of United Kingdom Delegation to the Council Meetings in Karachi of S.E.A.T.O. March 1956 and of the Baghdad Pact June 1957 and January 1959; Acting Deputy High
Commissioner, Peshawar, August to December 1957; Canberra May 1959 to May 1962.

MOON, Peter James Scott; born 1st April 1928; educated Uppingham and Worcester College, Oxford; called to Bar; m. 1955 Lucile Worms (2 d. 1957, 1962); Assistant Principal, Home Office, 1952; Commonwealth Relations Office 1954; Capetown/Pretoria 1956 to 1958; Principal 24th March 1958; Colombo 1960 to May 1963; Private Secretary to the Secretary of State 12th August 1963.

MOORE, Anthony Beecroft, MBE (1959); born 26th May 1928; educated Milton Academy, U.S.A., Cheltenham College 1940-46 and Oriel College, Oxford, 1948-52; 2nd Class Hons. Modern Languages; m. 1959 Catherine Maxwell (Is. 1961); Colonial Administrative Service and H.M.O.C.S., Tanganyika, 1952-63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, May 1963.

MORETON, John Oscar, MC; born 28th December 1917; educated St. Edward's (Scholar) 1931-36 and Trinity College, Oxford, 1936-39; 2nd Class Classical Hon. Mods.; MA; m. 1945 Margaret Katherine Fryer (3 d. 1946, 1950, 1952); 99th (Royal Bucks Yeomanry) Field Regt., Royal Artillery, 1939-46; France and Belgium 1940; India and Burma 1942-45; MC, Kohima, 1944; Major, Assistant Master, Uppingham School, 1946-48; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 1948; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 1949-50; Principal 1950; seconded to Government of Kenya 1953-5; served as Deputy Secretary, Cabinet Office, and as District Officer; Private Secretary to Secretary of State 1955; Principal Private Secretary 1956-59; Assistant Secretary 28th September 1959; Commonwealth Relations Office 5th September 1960; Lagos June 1961; substituting High Commissioner August to September 1962.

MORGAN, Francis Raymond; born 30th December 1918; educated Lutterworth County School; m. 1941 Gertrude Betty Ellingworth (2 d. 1943, 1948; 1 s. 1950); war service 1939-46; commissioned Royal Artillery 1939; served in France 1940, Belgium, Holland and Germany 1944-45; Military Government, Germany, 1945-46; Major; released September 1946; Temporary Information Officer, Central Office of Information, 1948; Information Officer 1949; seconded to Colonial Office November 1954 and transferred October 1958; Senior Information Officer, Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office, Trinidad, 1954-57; in charge United Kingdom Information Office, Jamaica, October 1957 to October 1959; Acting Director, United Kingdom Information Office, West Indies, December 1958 to July 1959; Principal Information Officer 1st December 1959; Director, British Information Services, Uganda, 1st December 1959.

MORGAN, James Conwy; born 16th April 1910; educated Malvern College and Brasenose College, Oxford; 2nd Class Hon. Mods.; 1st Class Lit. Hum.; BA (1933); m. 1933 Cicely Mary Norman Cobb (1 s. 1936; 2 d. 1939, 1942); Cadet, Tanganyika, 1934; Assistant District Officer 1936; District Officer (in absentia) 1946; military service 1939-47; K.A.R.; Lieutenant-Colonel; Senior Civil Affairs Officer, B.M.A., Somalia; Mentioned in Despatches; Principal, Colonial Office, 1947; Assistant Secretary 1955; attached to Monckton Commission 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st October 1962; on temporary loan to Colonial Office October 1962 to March 1963.

MORGAN, William David James; born 3rd October 1922; m. 1944 Joan Lucas (1 d. 1950); Clerical Officer, Colonial and Dominions Office, 27th March 1940; enlisted R.A.S.C. March 1942, served in Italy and Palestine; demobilized and returned to Commonwealth Relations Office February 1947; Executive Officer 5th February 1948; Delhi October 1951; local Higher Executive Officer October 1953; Higher Executive Officer 18th October 1954; Administration Officer, British Information Services, Delhi, October 1953 to March 1957; Senior Executive Officer (temporary) 20th May 1960; Senior Executive Officer 24th August 1960; Chief Executive Officer (temporary) 19th March 1962, (substantive) 1st September 1962.

MORLEY, Sir Alexander Francis, KCVO (1959; CMG 1955), CBE (1948); born 6th January 1908; educated Rugby 1920-26 and Queen's College, Oxford, 1926-30; 1st class Classical Hon. Mods. 1928; 2nd Class Lit. Hum. 1930; BA; m. 1939 Hedy von Landesberger-Antburg (1 d. 1944); Assistant Principal, India Office, 20th October 1930; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State December 1933; Principal 13th March 1936; Adviser to Indian Government delegations to 21st, 22nd, 23rd and 24th International Labour Conferences 1936-38; Secretary to Indian Delegation to Brussels Nine-Power Conference November 1937; on loan to Ministry of Aircraft Production 17th July 1940 to 17th March 1942; attached to United Kingdom Delegations, Commonwealth Communications Conference and U.N.R.R.A. Council, 1945; Assistant Secretary, Burma Office, 31st December 1945 to 14th December 1947; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations General Assembly January 1946; on loan to Treasury for service as Economic Adviser to Lord Privy Seal 15th December 1947; returned to Commonwealth Relations Office 19th April 1949; Deputy High Commissioner, Wellington,
March 1950 to February 1953; Assistant Under-Secretary of State, 1st June 1954; Deputy High Commissioner, Calcutta, February 1956; High Commissioner in Ceylon December 1957 to June 1962; High Commissioner in Jamaica August 1962.

MORTLOCK, Charles Geoffrey; born 4th July 1920; educated St. Edward's College, Malta, Shooter's Hill School and London University (Senior Country Exhibitioner) 1939; m. Yvonne Gittus (Croix de Guerre) (2 d. 1947, 1961); B.B.C. 1940-42; leader writer, Kemsley Newspapers, 1942-44; Features Editor, Overseas Press Department, British Council, 1944, Director of Department 1955; Temporary Senior Information Officer, C.O.I., 1947; London Editor, Britsky Magazin, 1947-49; Editorial Adviser, Allied Malta Newspapers, 1950-52; State Information Officer, Penang and Province Wellesley, 1952-54; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Colonial Office, 1954; Nigeria 1954-58; Information Officer 1957; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd March 1959; Senior Information Officer, Chittagong, November 1959 to July 1961; Regional Information Officer, Dacca, (local Principal Information Officer) November 1961; Acting Principal Information Officer 1st April 1963; Deputy Director, British Information Services, Nigeria, June 1963; Publication: The Flowing Bowl.

MOUSLEY, Norman Victor; born 12th August 1919; educated West Norwood Central School; m. 1947 Olive Lamburn (1 s. 1949); Royal Army Service Corps January 1940 to April 1946, served in Africa, Sicily and Italy; T.C. II, India Office, June 1946; Clerical Officer 15th May 1948; Karachi January 1952 to April 1955; local Executive Officer April 1954; Executive Officer November 1957; Canberra October 1958 to April 1962; Higher Executive Officer September 1963.

MOYNIHAN, Martin John, MC; born 17th February 1916; educated Birkenhead School and Magdalen College, Oxford, 1934-38; P.P.E.; MA; m. 1946 Monica Hopwood (1 s. 1952; 1 d. 1954); Assistant Principal, India Office, 27th February 1939; O.C.T.U. December 1939; commissioned, Indian Army April 1940; Q.V.O., Corps of Guides; served with Frontier Force Regiment, North West Frontier and Burma (wounded, MC); released November 1945; Principal 31st January 1944; Delhi, Madras and Bombay October 1946 to November 1948; Joint Secretary, Commonwealth Supply and Production Meeting, September 1951; Karachi October 1952; Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, March 1954; Deputy High Commissioner (local Assistant Secretary), Peshawar, December 1954 to February 1956; Assistant Secretary 30th January 1956; Deputy High Commissioner, Lahore, 1956-58; Assistant Secretary October 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Kuala Lumpur (with periods as Acting or Substituting High Commissioner) January 1961 to September 1963.

NAPIER AND ETTRICK, 14th Baron Napier of Nova Scotia, 5th Baron Ettrick and 11th Baronet, Rt. Hon. Sir Francis Nigel; born 5th December 1930; educated Eton College and R.M.A., Sandhurst; m. 1958 Delia Mary Pearson (1 d. 1961; 1 s. 1962); commissioned in Scots Guards 1950; served Malaya 1950-51; Adjutant, 1st Battalion Scots Guards, 1955-57; Equerry to H.R.H. The Duke of Gloucester 1958-60; retired 1960; a Member of the Queen's Bodyguard for Scotland (Royal Company of Archers); Assistant Ceremonial Secretary, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th August 1962.

NEEDHAM, George; born 9th April 1910; educated Barrow-in-Furness Grammar School and Universities of Durham (MA), Montpellier and Breslau; m. 1954 Hermine Bauer (1 s. 1956); Assistant anglais, Lycée Henri IV, Béziers, 1934-35; Lecturer at University of Breslau 1935-39; Reuters, Fleet Street, 1939; B.B.C. Foreign Listening Digest 1939-42; Principal, War Office and Foreign Office, 1942-45; Austrian Control Commission: Head of University and Higher Education Branch, Chairman of the Allied Quadripartite Committee on Universities, Vienna, 1945-48; Information Services, Control Commission, Germany, 1948-51; Foreign Office 1951-59; British Consul (Information), Munich; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st December 1959; Information Officer (Acting Senior Information Officer) 20th February 1962; member of United Kingdom Delegation to Brussels Conference October 1961 to April 1962; Senior Information Officer, Toronto, May 1962.

NEWSAM, Richard William, CVO (1961); born 23rd June 1918; educated St. Paul's 1931-36 and Trinity College, Oxford, 1937-39 and 1945-46; MA with war time degree in History; m. 1952 Joan Rostgard (1 s. 1956); commissioned in R.A.S.C. 1939; served with East African forces in Kenya, Abyssinia, Ceylon and Burma; released with rank of Captain 1945; temporary Administrative Assistant, Colonial Office, 1946; Assistant Principal 1946; Principal 1947; seconded to Nigeria 1952-53; Commonwealth Relations Office 27th May 1957; Colombo July 1958; Karachi February 1960; Assistant Secretary 1st July 1961; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation 24th June 1963.
Nicholas, John William; born 13th December 1924; educated Holly Lodge Grammar School, Birmingham, and Birmingham University 1942-43 and 1947-49; Honours History; m. 1947 Rita Jones (2 s. 1949, 1953); Army 1944-47; commissioned Royal Warwickshire Regiment; seconded to The Rajput Regiment, Indian Army; served in India and Burma; Assistant Principal, War Office, 11th July 1949; Principal 13th November 1954; on loan to Commonwealth Relations Office 23rd September 1957; Kuala Lumpur 1957; transferred to Commonwealth Relations Office 1st April 1958; Kuala Lumpur October 1957 to February 1961; Zomba December 1963.

Nightingale, William Denis; born 2nd April 1913; educated Hampton Grammar School, Middlesex; m. 1940 Wendy Franklin (twin s. 1946; 2 d. 1941, 1948); war service 1939-45; volunteered as private 1939; commissioned 1942; served in Abyssinia, Egypt and Italy; First South African Infantry Division; Sixth South African Armoured Division; Central Mediterranean Training Centre, Benevento, (seconded to British Army as instructor in Armoured Tactics with rank of Major); Odhams Press, London, 1931; North Somerset Independent (Frome) 1932; Bristol Evening World 1933-34; Argus South African Newspapers 1934-56; for two years Vice-President of the South African Society of Journalists; Daily Express, London, 1956-58; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st January 1958; Editor-in-Chief, British Information Service, Delhi, April 1958; Regional Information Officer, Winnipeg, May 1960; local Principal Information Officer May 1960; Principal Information Officer 1st April 1963; Regional Information Officer, Dacca, 3rd May 1963.

Norris, Eric George, CMG (1963); born 14th March 1918; educated Hertford Grammar School 1928-36 and St. Catharine's College, Cambridge, 1936-39. Mathematics Tripos Part I Class II 1937; Natural Science Tripos Part II Class III 1939; m. 1941 Pamela Crane (3 d. 1942, 1944, 1950); Assistant Master, Nautical College, Pangbourne, September 1939 to April 1940; enlisted in ranks of Royal Signals April 1940; commissioned May 1941; served in Germany July 1945 to October 1946; Major; released October 1946; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 2nd December 1946; Dublin February 1948 to September 1950 (local Principal 16th November 1948); Principal 1st January 1949; Karachi March 1952; Lahore October 1953 to August 1955 (Acting Deputy High Commissioner in Lahore July to September 1954, in Peshawar September to December 1954); Delhi October 1956 (local Assistant Secretary); Deputy High Commissioner, Bombay November 1957 to March 1960; Assistant Secretary 2nd December 1957; Imperial Defence College 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Calcutta, (local Assistant Under Secretary) 23rd September 1962.

Nunn, Frederick Norman; born 13th November 1907; m. 1932 Eileen Turner (1 s. 1933; twin d. 1939); Assistant Clerk, Clare Rural District Council, July 1927 to March 1930; General Clerk, Surrey County Council, April 1930 to September 1934; Settlement Officer, Portsmouth City Council, October 1934 to June 1939; Relieving Officer's Certificate, Poor Law Examination Board, 1937; Superintendent Social Welfare Officer June 1939 to August 1948; Executive Officer, National Assistance Board, 3rd August 1948; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st June 1956; Delhi April 1957 to June 1960; Kuala Lumpur July 1960.

Oakley, Rowland Henry; born 28th January 1909; educated Clifton College 1922-27 and New College, Oxford, 1927-30; Honours Modern History; m. 1940 Diana Hayward (twin s. 1941; 2 d. 1946, 1947); Malayan Civil Service 1931-58; Chinese Affairs and Labour Departments; interned, Singapore, 1942-45; Commissioner for Labour, Federation of Malaya, 1954-57; Secretary to Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare 1957-58; retired under Malayanization scheme 1958; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd May 1959; Principal 14th January 1960; an Adviser to the Government Delegation, Forty-fourth International Labour Conference, Geneva, June 1960.

O'Brien, Terence John, MC; born 13th October 1921; educated Gresham's School, Holt, 1935-40 and Merton College, Oxford, 1940-41 and January 1946-47 (Postmaster); 2nd Class Honours in History; MA; m. (1) 1950 Phyllis Mitchell (dec.); m. (2) 1953 Rita Reynolds (1 s. 1954; 2 d. 1957, 1959); enlisted in ranks of R.A. December 1941; commissioned May 1942; served in North-West Europe; MC March 1945; Captain May 1945; released in Class B January 1946; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 14th April 1947; Colombo December 1949 to January 1952; Principal 10th March 1952; seconded to Treasury November 1953 to December 1955; Canberra May 1956 to November 1958; Kuala Lumpur October 1960; Jesselton September 1962 to September 1963; New Delhi November 1963.

O'Connor, John Terence; born 16th April 1922; educated St. Ignatius College, Stamford Hill, 1933-38; m. 1948 Peggy Ellis (2 s. 1952, 1955); Clerical Officer, India Office, 30th May 1939; enlisted R.A.F. January 1941; served in Southern Rhodesia
August 1941 to July 1942 and India and Burma April 1944 to April 1946; rejoined India Office July 1946; Executive Officer 9th January 1948; Capetown December 1950 to May 1954; Higher Executive Officer 3rd August 1955; Canberra January 1956 to July 1959; Delhi March 1961; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 1st August 1963.

O'LEARY, Terence Daniel; born 18th August 1928; educated Dulwich College and St. John's College, Cambridge; BA 1950; Historical Tripos Class II Division I 1951; m. 1960 Janet Douglas Berney (twin s. 1960); military service 1946-48; commissioned in Queen's Royal Regiment; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 17th August 1953; Resident Clerk March 1954 to March 1956; Wellington May 1956 to March 1958; Principal April 1958; Delhi February 1960; Dar es Salaam February 1962 to June 1963.

OLIVER, Lieutenant-General Sir William Pasfield, KCB (1956: CB 1947), KCMG (1962), OBE, DL; born 8th September 1901; educated Radley College and Royal Military College, Sandhurst; m. 1938 Elizabeth Margaret Brind (1 s. 1943; 1 d. 1941); Chief of General Staff, G.H.Q., Middle East, (Major-General), 1945-46; Major-General 1949; Chief Army Instructor, Imperial Defence College, 1949-50; Chief of Staff, Eastern Command, January 1951 to December 1952; Principal Staff Officer to High Commissioner, Federation of Malaya, 1953-54; General Officer Commanding Berlin (British Sector) 1954-55; Vice-Chief of the Imperial General Staff 1955-57; Colonel, The Queen's Own Royal West Kent Regiment, 1949-59; Principal Staff Officer to Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations September 1957 to 1959; High Commissioner in Australia November 1959.

O'REGAN, John William Hamilton, OBE (1955); born 22nd March 1913; educated Marlborough College 1925-32 and Balliol College, Oxford, 1932-35; 2nd Class Honours Botany 1935; MA; m. 1941 Joan Caldecott (3 s. 1943, 1947, 1950); Cadet, Ceylon Civil Service, 1935; Private Secretary to Governor 1938-41; Assistant Government Agent, Kandy, Nuwara Eliya and Trincomalee; Controller, Internal Purchase Scheme, 1944-1950; Deputy Colonial Secretary, Jamaica, 1950-56; acted as Colonial Secretary on several occasions; Permanent Secretary, Western Region, Nigeria, 1956; Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Works and Surveys, Federal Government of Nigeria, 1958-62; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th August 1962; Kampala September 1962.

ORMEROD, Richard Caton; born 22nd January 1915; educated Winchester College 1928-33 and New College, Oxford, 1933-37; 2nd Class Honour Moderations and Lit. Hum.; BA; m. 1947 Elizabeth More (2 d. 1949, 1956; 2 s. 1952, 1954); Assistant Principal, India Office, 11th October 1938; joined Royal Armoured Corps as Trooper November 1941; commissioned October 1942 in Indian Armoured Corps and served initially in India and in 1944-45 in Burma; wounded; Captain; released December 1945; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State for India 10th December 1945; Principal 29th August 1946; Bombay June 1951 to May 1953; Wellington December 1956 to May 1959; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 17th October 1960; Calcutta March 1962; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962; Acting Deputy High Commissioner 11th April to 24th September 1962.

OVERTON, David; born 22nd April 1919; educated Sir George Monoux Grammar School, Walthamstow; m. 1946 Mary Pye (1 d. 1948); Local Government 1936-39, 1946-50; military service 1939-46; commissioned 1942; Captain 1945; served with the R.W.A.F.F. and the 14th Army; Superintendent, B.N.B.C., National Central Library, 1950; Deputy Librarian, Imperial Institute Library, 1952; Librarian 1953; Deputy Librarian, Commonwealth Relations Office and Colonial Office, 1954, and Department of Technical Assistance 1961.

OXLEY, Humphrey Leslie Malcolm, OBE (1956); born 9th October 1909; educated Epsom College 1922-27; m. 1945 Frances Bowden (twin s. 1947); entered solicitor's office as articled clerk 1928; qualified as solicitor and enrolled 1933; Junior Legal Assistant, India Office, 23rd September 1933; appointed Commissioner for Oaths April 1934; Assistant Solicitor 13th March 1944; Senior Legal Assistant, Commonwealth Relations Office and Colonial Office, 1st January 1950; Assistant Legal Adviser 25th August 1961.

P

PACKE, William Wilkinson; born 1st January 1916; m. 1957 Doris Ivy Weston; Royal Army Medical Corps April 1940 to December 1946; Warrant Officer Class I; Temporary Clerk, India Office, 17th February 1947; Clerical Officer 1st January 1948; Executive Officer 24th December 1954; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

PEPPER, Denis Stephen Wetherell; born 7th December 1912; educated Bedford Modern School; m. 1949 Joan Gregson (née Alexander) (1 step-s. 1939; 1 step-d. 1945; 1 s. 1953); commercial advertising 1932-40; Coldstream Guards 1940; commissioned Royal Warwickshire Regiment; Special Operations Executive 1943, served in Egypt and Italy; released as Major
1946; Information Officer, Foreign Office, 1946-56; served in Thailand, Indo-China, China and Cyprus; commercial advertising 1956-59; Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1959; Lagos February 1960; Enugu April 1960; Kaduna August 1960.

PETERS, William, MVO (1961), MBE (1959); born 28th September 1923; educated King Edward VI Grammar School, Morpeth, 1935-41 and Balliol College, Oxford, (Domus Exhibitioner) 1942 and 1946-48; 2nd Class Honours Lit. Hum., BA 1948; MA 1948; m. 1944 Catherine Bailey; enlisted in Queen's Royal Regiment 1943; commissioned in India to King's Own Scottish Borderers 1944; seconded 9th Gurkha Rifles; released as Captain May 1946; appointed H.M. Overseas Civil Service September 1948; First Devonshire Course at Oxford and London Universities 1948-49; Administrative Officer Class IV, Gold Coast, February 1950; Class III September 1953; Class II, Ghana, July 1957; Deputy Secretary to Regional Commissioner, Northern Ghana, January 1958; Secretary July to November 1958; retired from H.M. Overseas Civil Service August 1959; Temporary Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th July 1959; Principal 31st December 1959; Dacca September 1960; Acting Deputy High Commissioner July to October 1962; Nicosia November 1963.

PHILIP, John Clark; born 27th February 1920; educated Acland Central 1931-34; m. 1942 Dorothy Turpin (2 s. 1946, 1948; 1 d. 1954); Sorting Clerk, G.P.O., 7th January 1939; R.N.V.R. 1939-46; Sub-Lieutenant; P. and T.O. 24th May 1948; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 8th August 1949; Executive Officer 24th December 1952; Higher Executive Officer 11th June 1958; Commonwealth Relations Office 17th October 1960; Delhi (Private Secretary to High Commissioner) January 1961 to April 1963; Karachi April 1963.

PHILLIPS, Kenneth; born 1st May 1928; educated Carre's Grammar School, Sleaford, Lincs, and Aylesbury Grammar School; m. 1960 Margaret Oakley (1 s. 1962); Executive Officer, Ministry of Agriculture, May 1949; Commonwealth Relations Office 23rd April 1951; Lahore March to June 1953; Peshawar June 1953 to March 1955; Calcutta July 1956 to March 1957; Accra May 1960 to May 1963; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Colombo December 1963.

PHILLIPS, Albert Edward; born 12th November 1919; m. 1950 Marjorie Phyllis King (2 s. 1951, 1954); Counter Clerk and Telegraphist 26th April 1936; war service 1941-46; Royal Navy (Communications Branch); served in Iceland and Malta; Postal and Telegraph Officer 1947; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 2nd August 1949; Delhi (local Executive Officer) September 1952 to February 1956; Executive Officer 3rd September 1955; British Information Services, Johannesburg. July 1959 to July 1952; Higher Executive Officer 1st September 1963.

PHILLIPS, Douglas Herbert Charles; born 4th November 1924; educated Cardinal Vaughan School, Kensington; m. 1950 Olwen Laverick (1 d. 1954); Royal Navy 1943-46; service in Australia and Ceylon 1945-46; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Civil Aviation, December 1946; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st March 1948; Executive Officer 30th August 1949; Karachi December 1950; Peshawar December 1952 to May 1953; Calcutta January 1954 to May 1957; Higher Executive Officer (local) 28th January 1954, (substantive) 13th June 1955; Bombay September 1959 to December 1962; Senior Executive Officer (local) 3rd September 1959; Senior Executive Officer 24th August 1960; Departmental Training Officer April 1963.

PICKARD, Cyril Stanley; born 18th September 1917; educated Alleyne's School and New College, Oxford; 1st Class Honours School of Modern History 1939; m. 1941 Helen Strawson (3 s. 1946, 1948, 1954; 1 d. 1950); Assistant Principal, Home Office, 2nd October 1939; military service January 1940 to July 1941; Captain; released to Foreign Office for special appointment with Office of Minister of State, Cairo, July 1941 to May 1944; Principal 1st March 1943; served with U.N.R.R.A. in Middle East and Germany on approved employment terms May 1944 to October 1945; returned to Home Office 1st November 1945; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st June 1948; Delhi September 1950; Canberra (local Assistant Secretary) August 1952 to March 1955; Assistant Secretary 7th November 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Wellington, September 1958 to March 1961; Assistant Under-Secretary (temporary) 8th October 1962.

PLANT, Jack; born 1st February 1925; educated Salford Grammar School 1936-41; m. 1947 Nancy Roddick (2 s. 1948, 1953); served in Royal Navy 1942-46; commissioned (Midshipman) 1943; Sub-Lieutenant 1944; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Food, 1946-47; Clerical Officer January 1948; Executive Officer June 1950; Commonwealth Relations Office 2nd June 1954; Colombo February 1955 to March 1957; Accra (local Higher Executive Officer) May 1957 to June 1960; Higher Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Karachi (local Senior Executive Officer) November 1961; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.
PORTER, Patrick Basil; born 15th March 1921; educated London School of Economics and Political Science, University of London; Honours degree in History 1950; BA; Post Graduate Certificate in Education 1951; Academic Diploma in Education 1952; m. 1950 Margaret Rudge (twin s. 1956; d. 1958); R.A.F. 1941-46; 3209 Servicing Commando; served in India, Burma, Normandy, French Indo-China and Siam; History Master, Carshalton, 1951-53; Education Officer, Western Nigeria, 1953-56; Editor for London Publisher 1956-58; Temporary Information Officer, Reference Division, Central Office of Information, 1958; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Colonial Office, 1959; Lagos 1959; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st October 1960; Information Officer 17th July 1962; author of How the People of Britain are Governed.

POTTER, James Aked; born 17th August 1914; educated Saffron Walden School, University College, London, and Heidelberg University; m. 1950 Theresa von Keisenberg; Colonial Office 1939-42; Air Ministry (Intelligence) 1942-43; Political Intelligence Department, Foreign Office, 1943-48; German Section 1948-50; travelled in New Zealand, Canada and U.S.A. 1950-54; locally employed Temporary Assistant Information Officer 1954-56; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, September 1956; Toronto June 1957; Information Officer (local Senior Information Officer) 21st February 1958; Perth 2nd January 1961; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

PRESTON, Myles Park; born 4th April 1927; educated Liverpool Institute High School 1938-45 and Clare College, Cambridge, (Scholar) 1945-48; Mathematical Tripos Part I Class I 1946, Part II Senior Optime, 1948; MA 1952; m. 1951 Ann Betten (1 s. 1955; 1 d. 1957); Instructor Lieutenant (†), Royal Navy, 1948-51; Assistant Principal, Admiralty, 15th November 1951; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st September 1953; Delhi September 1954 to November 1956; Principal (temporary) 28th January 1957; Principal 6th August 1957; Lagos 1959 to 1962; Kampala 1964.

PRICE, Major-General Cedric Rhys, CB, CBE (1945: OBE 1943), MA; born 13th June 1905; educated Wellington College, R.M.A., Woolwich, and Trinity College, Cambridge; 1st Class Mech. Science Tripos; MA; m. 1935 Rosamund Clifford (2 d. 1936, 1940); commissioned, Royal Engineers, 1925; served in India 1932-38; Staff College 1938-39; Military Assistant Secretary, Offices of War Cabinet, 1940-46; Secretary, British Joint Services Mission, Washington 1946-48; Secretary, Chiefs of Staff Committee, 1948-50; Imperial Defence College 1951; Chief of Staff to Chairman, British Joint Services Mission, Washington, 1952-54; Brigadier, General Staff, Eastern Command, 1955-56; Director, Military Intelligence, War Office, 1956-59; Principal Staff Officer to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations 7th September 1959.

PRICE-JONES, Gwilym; born 30th June 1906; educated Jesus College, Oxford, 1924-28; Greats 1928; National Library of Scotland, Edinburgh, 1932-40; Assistant Principal, Department of Health for Scotland, 1940; Principal 19th November 1943; Ministry of Town and Country Planning, London, 1946-51; General Register Office (International Branch) 1951-55; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office 2nd January 1956, transferred 1st April 1957.

PRITCHARD, Sir Neil, KCMG (1962: CMG 1952); born 14th January 1911; educated Liverpool College 1920-29 and Worcester College, Oxford, 1929-33 (Gibbs Scholar 1931); 1st Class Honours Modern History; BA 1932; m. 1943 Mary Burroughes (1 s. 1945); Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 23rd October 1933; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 5th October 1936; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 22nd April 1938; Assistant Secretary to Rhodesia Nyasaland Royal Commission April 1938 to March 1939; Principal 2nd February 1939; Cape Town/Pretoria April 1941 to September 1945; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1946; Dublin April 1948 to October 1949; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 28th December 1950; Deputy High Commissioner, Ottawa, May 1954 to February 1957; Deputy High Commissioner, Canberra, June 1957 to June 1960; Deputy Under-Secretary of State (temporary) 1st July 1961; British High Commissioner, Tanganyika, 9th December 1961 to 11th July 1963; Deputy Under-Secretary of State (temporary) 23rd September 1963.

PUGH, John Arthur; born 17th July 1920; educated Brecon Grammar School 1931-37 and Bristol University 1952-54; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Health, June 1937; Royal Navy June 1941 to October 1945; Executive Officer (in absentia) June 1942; Higher Executive Officer, Ministry of National Insurance, October 1947; Senior Executive Officer, Ministry of Pensions, September 1954; loaned to Gold Coast Administrative Service and served in Ministry of Health and Prime Minister's Office August 1955 to June 1958; Adviser on Organisation and Methods to Ghana Government under United Kingdom/Ghana Technical Co-operation Scheme October 1958 to October 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 4th April 1961; Lagos (local Chief Executive Officer) June 1962; Kuala Lumpur January 1963.
RAFTERY, Peter Albert; born 8th June 1929; educated St. Ignatius College; m. 1952 Margaret Hulse (4 d. 1953, 1955, 1957, 1959); Clerical Officer, India Office, October 1946; National Service 1947–49; Delhi January 1950 to January 1954; Executive Officer February 1956; Peshawar March 1956 to April 1959; Information Officer (local) 5th November 1959; Cape Town November 1959 to May 1962; Acting Regional Information Officer February to September 1960 and March to May 1961; seconded to Foreign Service December 1961 to December 1962; Vice-Consul, Cape Town, May to December 1962; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Kuala Lumpur January 1963.

RAINSFORD, Frederick Fitzpatrick, Air Commodore (retd.), CB, DFC (1949); born 12th December 1909; educated Campbell College and Queen's University, Belfast; Bachelor of Agriculture 1935; m. (1) 1939 Dorothy Kitty Ralph (2 d.); m. (2) 1949 Winifred Audrey Meyer (1 d., 1 s.); farmed in Kenya 1929–31; commissioned in R.A.F. (Special Reserve) 1936; Mentioned in Despatches 1940; short service commission 1936; permanent commission 1947; qualified R.A.F. Staff College 1943; served mainly in Bomber Command until 1945; Commanded 148 Squadron (Middle East) 1941–42 and 115 Squadron (United Kingdom) 1943; Transport Command 1945–46; Deputy Director of Air Transport, Air Ministry, 1947–49; Directing Staff, R.A.F. Staff College, 1949–51; Headquarters, F.E.A.F., 1952–55; Commanded Recruit Training Stations 1955–57; Air Attaché, Greece, 1957–60; Directing Staff, Royal Naval War College, 1960–62; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th April 1962.

RATCLIFFE, Marjorie Louise; born 24th August 1904; educated Southall Secondary School; Typist, India Office, 31st August 1925; General Post Office, Birmingham, 1st November 1926; India Office 6th July 1931; Shorthand-Typist 1st January 1933; Clerical Officer 10th October 1939; Executive Officer 28th March 1945; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962.

REDDPATH, Alexander William, CB; born 4th September 1909; educated Worksop College and R.M.C., Sandhurst (King's Cadet); m. 1936 Rosemary Brenda Cotesworth (2 s. 1939, 1943); commissioned Indian Army 1929; 3/12th Frontier Force; A.D.C. to Governor, N.W.F. Province; entered Indian Political Service 1934 (I.P.S. political, administrative and law examinations); P.A. to A.G.G., Rajputana, (Political and Secretariat training); Assistant Commissioner (under administrative and judicial training), Multan, Punjab; Under-Secretary to A.G.G. (Sub-Judge, Magistrate and J.P.), Central India; Assistant Political Agent (District Magistrate, Senior Sub-Judge, Collector), Gilgit; Under-Secretary to Resident, Punjab States; Secretary to Resident, Eastern States; Political Agent, Bengal States; 1st Secretary and Counsellor (acting), British Legation, Kabul, Afghanistan; Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan; retired from I.P.S. 1948; Bursar, Radley College, 1949–51; contract service with Government of Pakistan 1952–58; Deputy Secretary and Joint Secretary to Government in Cabinet Secretariat; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st July, 1958.

REED, Adrian Harbottle; born 5th January 1921; educated Hele's School, Exeter, 1933–39 and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, (Exhibitioner) 1939–41; Hist. Trip. Part I Class II Division I 1941; BA 1947; m. 1947 Doris Duthie (1 d. 1950; 1 s. 1952); enlisted in Royal Artillery September 1941; commissioned January 1942; served in Iraq, Persia and Italy October 1942 to July 1945; Captain; employed with Control Commission for Germany 1946; released March 1947; Assistant Principal, India Office, 18th June 1947; Lahore January 1948 to April 1950 (local Principal 1st March 1949); Principal 17th July 1950; U.K. Delegation to U.N. General Assembly 1951; Salisbury July 1953 to May 1956 (Acting High Commissioner May to August 1955); Dublin October 1960 to October 1962; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 15th October 1962, (acting) 1st July 1963.

REID, Dougal Gordon; born 31st December 1925; educated Sedbergh School 1939–43 and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, 1944 (R.N. and R.M. Short Course) and 1947–48 (Colonial Service Course); m. 1950 Georgina Elizabeth Johnston (twin s. one dec., 1952); Cadet, Sierra Leone, 1949; Assistant District Commissioner 1952; District Commissioner 1956; Clerk to the Executive Council 1957–58; seconded to Colonial Office as Principal 1958–60; Admin. Officer, Grade II, 1961; Permanent Secretary 1960–62; retired from H.M.O.C.S. April 1962; Arthur Guinness Son and Co. (Park Royal) Ltd. 1962–63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 16th July 1963.

REISS, John Henry; born 26th March 1918; educated Bradfield College; m. 1943 Dora York (1 s. 1943; 2 d. 1945, 1947); war service with East African Forces 1939–42; Officer in Charge, African Section, Kenya Government Information Services, 1945; Officer in Charge, Kenya Information Services, 1949; Director of Information, Kenya, July 1954 to August 1959; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st September 1959; Senior Information Officer 12th February 1960; Principal Information
Officer (temporary) 1st April 1960; Johannesburg August 1961; seconded to Foreign Service 1st December 1961; Wellington February 1963.

REITH, Martin; born 6th December 1935; educated Royal High School of Edinburgh; Scottish Home Department; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office. 1st March 1954; R.A.F. 1954–56; Calcutta 1957–59; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Kampala September 1962.

REYNOLDS, Frank Arrowsmith; born 30th March 1916; educated Addey and Stanhope School and London University; FCII 1948; LLB (2nd class honours) 1950; m. 1938 Joan Lockyer (1 s. 1943; 2 d. 1946, 1953); Royal Insurance Co. Ltd. 1934–40 and 1947–50; military service 1941–46; Lieutenant, R.E.; attached Indian Engineers in India, Burma and Siam; Colonial Administrative Service, Tanganyika: Cadet 1950, District Officer 1952, retired 1961; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 29th January 1962; Principal 12th December 1962; Bombay December 1963.

RICHARDS, Denis Edward; born 25th May 1923; educated Wilson's Grammar School and St. Peter's Hall, Oxford, (Colonial Services Course); m. 1947 Beryl Brown (2 d. 1949, 1952); Royal Navy 1941–46; Lieutenant R.N.V.R.; Gold Coast (Ghana) 1948–60; District Administration 1948–51; Establishment Secretary's Office 1952–56; Secretary, Salaries and Wages Commission, 1956; Ministry of Finance 1957–60; retired July 1960; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd May 1960; Principal 12th July 1960; Karachi June 1961.

RIGNEY, Howard Ernest; born 22nd June 1922; educated University of Western Ontario, Canada, (Honours in English and French; BA) 1941–45, University of Toronto (MA in English 1947) 1945–46 and Université de Paris 1948–50; m. 1950 Margaret Grayling Benn (1 s. 1956); lecturer in English, University of British Columbia, 1946–48; Central Office of Information October 1953 to November 1956; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, November 1956; Regional Information Officer, Dacca, February 1957; Senior Information Officer 16th December 1957; Principal Information Officer (local) April 1958; Regional Information Officer, Montreal, September 1960 to July 1963; Principal Information Officer 1st October 1960.

ROBINS, Kenneth Harold; born 19th March 1917; educated Gravesend Junior Technical School; m. 1946 Eileen Goldsmith (1 d. 1948); Sorting Clerk and Telegraphist, G.P.O., 1935–39; Clerical Officer, Air Ministry, February 1939; R.A.F.V.R. April 1940 to March 1946; Clerical Officer March 1946; Executive Officer 1st April 1951; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 12th June 1962.

ROBINSON, William Douglas, OBE (1945); born 5th November 1907; educated Epsom College, Surrey; m. 1948 Phyllis Spridell née Boden (1 d. 1949); Indian (Imperial) Police 1927; King's Police Medal 1947; retired 1947; Deputy Inspector-General, West Pakistan Police, 1947–49; Deputy Commissioner, Federation of Malaya Police, 1955–57; Director of Intelligence, Cyprus, 1957–59; Temporary Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office 24th January 1963.

ROGERS, Martin Hartley Guy; born 11th June 1925; educated Marlborough College 1939–43 and Jesus College, Cambridge, (Classical Scholar) 1947–49; Law Practice Class II Division I; m. 1959 Jean Chinn (1 d. 1961; 1 s. 1962); enlisted September 1943; commissioned July 1944, 2nd Bn. Royal Lincolnshire Regiment; served with B.A.O.R. and in Middle East 1945–47; Captain; released August 1947; Temporary Assistant Principal, Ministry of National Insurance, 8th August 1949; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th October 1949; Assistant Private Secretary to the Secretary of State 10th May 1950 to 8th July 1951; Karachi November 1951 to October 1953; Principal 20th September 1953; seconded to the Government of the Federation of Nigeria March 1956 to November 1957; Canadian National Defence College September 1960 to July 1961; Ottawa August 1961; Adviser to Jamaican Ministry of External Affairs January to August 1963.

ROSE, Brian; born 26th January 1930; educated Canford School, Dorset, 1943–47; m. 1952 Audrey Barnes; national service with Intelligence Corps, Austria, 1948–50; Executive Officer, Ministry of Food, May 1950; Commonwealth Relations Office 15th May 1954; Peshawar 1955–56; Higher Executive Officer 19th November 1957; Ottawa 1958 to 1961; Kingston (local Senior Executive Officer) July 1962; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

ROSS WILLIAMSON, Reginald Pole; born 25th January 1907; educated privately and at Emmanuel College, Cambridge; BA 1930; MA 1935; m. 1932 Eileen Buchanan; accompanied British Museum expeditions to Upper Egypt 1930–31 and Ur of the Chaldees 1931–32; Editor of The Bookman 1934; attached to Sunday Observer 1934–39; Adviser on Research in Film Industry 1934–43; Specialist, Ministry of Information, 12th September 1939; Admiralty (Press Division) 9th October 1939; Dominions Office (Press Attaché, Dublin) 9th August 1943; Senior Information Officer with seniority from 1st August 1949; Regional Information...
Officer, Bombay, April 1953; Senior Executive Officer January 1955; Dublin 31st January 1955; Regional Information Officer, Capetown, March 1957 to July 1962; Melbourne (local Principal Information Officer) January 1963.

ROWDON, Leslie Raymond Horace; born 24th October 1915; educated Emanuel School; m. Doris Peckover (1 s.); military service 1940-46; released with rank of Captain; Theatrical Manager and Press Officer until 1951; free-lance exhibition deviser for Government Departments 1951-56; Temporary Information Officer, Central Office of Information, April 1956; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 10th June 1958; Johannesburg July 1958 to September 1961; Information Officer 17th February 1959; local Senior Information Officer April 1960; Senior Information Officer 26th April 1962; Regional Information Officer, Madras, April 1963.

RUMBOLD, Sir Horace Algernon Fraser, KCMG (1960: CMG 1953), CIE (1947); born 27th February 1906; educated Wellington 1920-24 and Christ Church, Oxford, (Open Scholarship) October 1924 to December 1927; 2nd Class History School; BA; m. 1946 Adel Hughes (2 d. 1948, 1950); Assistant Principal, India Office, 1st January 1929; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State April 1930 to 1933 and to Permanent Under-Secretary of State December 1933 to September 1934; Principal 24th September 1934; Assistant Secretary 26th July 1943; Deputy High Commissioner, Capetown/Pretoria, September 1949 to February 1953; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 7th November 1955; Temporary Deputy Under-Secretary of State 1st December 1958; Chairman of the Committee on Territorial Questions (Dissolution of Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland) August 1963.

RUMSEY, Alfred William Henry; born 23rd February 1910; m. 1938 Carol Read (1 d. 1954); Post Office 1927; Admiralty 1939; Higher Clerical Officer, India Office, 21st January 1946; Executive Officer 20th May 1946; Commonwealth Relations Office 15th August 1947; Wellington November 1954 to June 1958; Kuala Lumpur (local Higher Executive Officer) June 1959 to March 1962; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Delhi July 1962.

RUTTER, Alma Doris, MBE (1948); born 12th May 1911; educated Putney Business Training College; Shorthand Typist, India Office, 21st September 1936; Clerical Officer 8th December 1942; Superintendent of Typists 1942; Personal Assistant to the Secretary of State for India 1945 and to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations 1948; Executive Officer 16th April 1952; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; seconded to Colonial Office December 1961 to September 1962.

RYMER, Garnet Alexander; born 31st January 1915; educated Westcliff High School, Essex; m. 1944 Sylvia Petts; R.A.F. (Administration) 1931-46; served in Iraq, Kurdistan, India, South Africa and West Africa (Sierra Leone); Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 1st November 1946; Executive Officer 1st March 1951; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Lagos August 1960 to July 1963.

SALES, Norman Amos, MBE (1956); born 13th September 1911; educated Warehousemen, Clerks and Drapers Schools, Purley, and Hastings Central School; m. 1940 Esme Turner (2 s. 1941, 1946); 3rd Class Clerk, Supreme Court of Judicature, 1st October 1932; Admiralty April 1941; Higher Clerical Officer 1942; on loan to Office of United Kingdom High Commissioner in India: Delhi September 1947, Bombay May 1950 to March 1953; Higher Executive Officer 1st January 1948; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st September 1950; Ottawa June 1955 to August 1959; Senior Executive Officer 17th April 1956; Chief Executive Officer 1st March 1961; Delhi March 1962.

SAMPLES, Reginald McCartney, DSO (1942), OBE (1963); born 11th August 1918; educated Rhyl Grammar School and University of Liverpool 1935-40; B. Com.; m. 1947 Elsie Hide (2 s. 1947, 1949; 1 step-d. 1938); R.N.V.R. (Air Branch) 1940-46; Lieutenant (A); Central Office of Information March 1947 to August 1948 (Economic Editor of Overseas Newspapers); Commonwealth Relations Office 25th August 1948; British Information Services, India: Economic Information Officer, Bombay, October 1948, Editor-in-Chief, Delhi, April 1952, Deputy Director, Delhi, September 1953; Information Officer 25th January 1952; Senior Information Officer 23rd May 1953; Principal Information Officer (local) 9th September 1953; Principal Information Officer 8th November 1955; Director, British Information Services, Pakistan (Karachi), 1st November 1956; Chief Information Officer (B) 1st December 1957; Director, British Information Services, Canada (Ottawa), July 1959.

SAUL, Jack; born 12th June 1914; educated Purston National School and Dewsbury Technical College; m. 1949 Eileen May Parker; military service September 1939 to November 1945; Sergeant, Parachute Regiment; Temporary Clerk, India Office, 1946; Clerical Officer 1st January 1947; Executive Officer 1st March 1951; Peshawar December 1951; Karachi
January 1953 to March 1955; Calcutta May 1957 to November 1960; Higher Executive Officer (local) 20th April 1957; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Salisbury July 1961.

SCOTT, David Aubrey; born 3rd August 1919; educated Charterhouse 1933-38 and Birmingham University (Scholar) 1938-39, reading for BSc (Mining Engineering); m. 1941 Vera Ibbotson (1 d. 1942; 2 s. 1944, 1952); enlisted in ranks of R.A. November 1939; commissioned June 1940; served in Egypt as Chief Radar Adviser on British Military Mission 1945-47; Major; released September 1947; Public Relations Officer, Decca Navigator Company, 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st January 1948; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 27th January 1949; Principal 20th September 1949; Capetown/Pretoria January 1951 to August 1953; Joint Services Staff College September 1953 to April 1954; seconded to Cabinet Office July 1954 to March 1956; Member of Secretariat of Prime Ministers' Meeting January to February 1955 and Malta Round Table Conference September to December 1955; Secretary-General, Federation of Malaya Constitutional Conference, January 1956, and British Caribbean Federation Conference, February 1956; seconded to Foreign Service as First Secretary, Office of the Commissioner-General for the United Kingdom in South-East Asia, Singapore, May 1956 to March 1958; temporary Assistant Secretary 15th December 1958; Basutoland Constitutional Discussions 1958-59; member of Committee of Officials on the Review of the Constitution of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland 1959; Assistant Secretary 1st April 1960; Assistant Secretary to the Monckton Advisory Commission 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Salisbury, March 1961; member of team of Advisers on Central Africa appointed by the Rt. Hon. R. A. Butler, Minister for Central African Affairs, July to October 1962.

SCOTT, James Archibald, MVO (1961); born 5th March 1932; educated Dollar Academy, University of St. Andrews and the Queen's University, Kingston, Ontario; m. 1957 Elizabeth Buchan-Hepburn (1 d. 1960; 1 s. 1962); National Service with 2nd Allied Tactical Air Force 1954-56; R.Aux.A.F. 1956; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 30th October 1956; Resident Clerk March 1957; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 20th May 1957; Delhi October 1958 to 1962; Principal (local) 4th April 1961; Principal 1st August 1961; United Kingdom Mission to the United Nations, New York, May 1962.

SCOTT, Michael, MVO (1961); born 19th May 1923; educated Dame Allan's School 1933-40 and Durham University 1947-49; Politics and Economics 1949; BA; m. 1944 Sylvia Vincent-Barwood (3 s. 1945, 1950, 1954); enlisted in Durham Light Infantry 1941; commissioned from Indian Military Academy 1943; 1st Gurkha Rifles; Captain; released 1947; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, November 1949; Principal 14th June 1952; Commonwealth Relations Office 9th April 1957; Karachi October 1958; Deputy High Commissioner Peshawar, August 1959 to January 1962; Delhi (local Assistant Secretary) October 1963.

SCOTT, Thomas Alastair Henderson; born 21st August 1914; educated British West Indies, France and Balliol College, Oxford, 1933-36 (Elton Exhibition 1936) and 1937-39; 1st Class Honours English Language and Literature; BA 1936; BLitt 1939; Journalism 1939-37; Royal Marines 1939-45; Major, R.M.; Central Office of Information 1946-51; N.A.T.O. International Secretariat 1951-55; Principal Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, August 1955; Regional Information Officer, Montreal, August 1955; Chief Information Officer (B) (temporary) May 1958; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation as Public Relations Adviser to Government of Trinidad and Tobago July 1962.

SCRAGG, Robert Thomas Frederick; born 12th November 1918; educated St. Andrew's School, Holborn (Neville Bursary) and Churchdown School, Kent; m. 1944 Hilda Roberts (1 s. 1945; 1 d. 1949); entered Queen's Royal Regiment 1939; war service in France, Belgium, Egypt, Libya, Tunisia and Algeria; Sergeant; invalided (wounds) 1944; Temporary Assistant, War Office, 1944-46; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, August 1946; Executive Officer 1950; Higher Executive Officer 21st March 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st February 1961; seconded to Department of Technical Cooperation 24th July 1961; Dar es Salaam December 1961.

SEAR, Bertram Burlington; born 3rd April 1921; educated Wilson's Grammar School, London, 1932-37; m. 1945 Frances Mary Anderson (3 s. 1947, 1949, 1951; 1 d. 1950); Public Assistance Dept., London County Council, 1937-38; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Education, December 1938; enlisted in R.A.F. October 1940; trained as pilot in North America and South Africa; Sergeant Pilot June 1943; Flight Sergeant June 1944; Training Command, Northern Ireland, 1944-45; commissioned 1945; service in Persian Gulf 1945-46; released, Flying Officer, April 1946; returned to Ministry of Education May 1946; Executive Officer May 1947 (seniority from April 1945); Commonwealth Relations Office 19th March 1951; Madras January 1953 to March 1956;
Delhi (local Higher Executive Officer) 14th April 1959 to June 1962; Higher Executive Officer 18th June 1959.

**Swell**, Charles George Russell, MBE (1959); born 26th December 1898; educated St. Dunstan's College, Catford; m. 1949 Florence Brooker; R.F.A. 1915–19; T.C.I., Imperial War Graves Commission, 1919–26; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Health, 1926–38; India Office 16th May 1938; R.A. and Royal Signals (T.A.) 1920–39; B.E.F. September 1939 to June 1940, (commissioned March 1940); Normandy to the Baltic June 1944 to June 1945; Mentioned in Despatches; West Africa 1946–47; Singapore 1948; released November 1948 (Major); Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th April 1950; Bombay August 1951 to December 1953; Pretoria/Capetown December 1953 to June 1960; Higher Executive Officer (local) 21st December 1953; Higher Executive Officer 21st December 1955; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1962.

**Shannon**, Godfrey Eccleston Boyd, CMG (1951); born 14th December 1907; educated Wellington College 1921–26 and St. John's College, Cambridge, 1926–30; Browne Medal for Greek Epigram 1928; 1st Class in Parts I and II Classical Tripos; BA 1929; Certificate of Competent Knowledge in French 1930; MA 1938; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 27th October 1930; Private Secretary to successive Parliamentary Under-Secretaries of State 23rd January 1935 to 15th February 1937; accompanied the Duke of Devonshire to Australia and New Zealand September 1936 to February 1937; Principal 15th February 1937; served on Secretariat of Imperial Conference 1937; Wellington December 1938 to April 1941; Assistant Secretary 1st April 1943; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to the following Conferences: International Civil Aviation Conference, Chicago, and Commonwealth Air Conversations, Montreal, November 1944, Council of Foreign Ministers, London, and United Nations Preparatory Commission, London, 1945, United Nations General Assembly, London, League of Nations Assembly, Geneva, and United Nations General Assembly, New York, 1946, Council of Foreign Ministers, Moscow, United Nations General Assembly, New York, and Council of Foreign Ministers, London, 1947; Deputy High Commissioner, Ottawa, June 1948 to January 1951 (Acting High Commissioner 6th May to 2nd August 1949); Deputy High Commissioner, Calcutta, (local Assistant Under-Secretary of State), November 1952 to February 1956; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 4th December 1954.

**Sharkey**, Columba John; born 9th June 1931; educated St. Malachy's College, Belfast; m. 1962 Olive Brassil (1 d. 1963); Executive Officer, Ministry of Food, 1949–54 (attached to Government of Northern Ireland); Commonwealth Relations Office 1954; Delhi 1955; Calcutta 1956–58; Dacca (local Information Officer) 1959–61; Information Officer 2nd May 1959; Commonwealth Touring Exhibition 1961–62; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Melbourne 1962.

**Shaw**, John Dennis Bolton, MVO (1961); born 5th July 1920; educated Manchester Grammar School 1931–38 and Balliol College, Oxford, 1938–40 and 1946–48 (History Scholar); 2nd Class Honours Modern History; MA; m. 1955 Isabel Lowe (2 s. 1957, 1961); Royal Artillery (Field) 1940–46; served in Tunisia, Algeria, Egypt, Italy and India; attached Royal West African Frontier Force 1945–46; released as Lieutenant September 1946; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 8th November 1948; Principal 6th November 1950; seconded to Sierra Leone Government October 1955; Acting District Commissioner and Acting Deputy Financial Secretary, Sierra Leone, October 1955 to April 1957; Commonwealth Relations Office 10th July 1957; Karachi November 1958 to February 1961; seconded to Foreign Office and posted to British Embassy, Washington, May 1961 to November 1962; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 3rd December 1962, (acting) 1st July 1963.

**Shears**, Henry James; born 11th March 1918; educated Sloane School, Chelsea; m. 1940 Eileen Marguerite Sadler (2 d. 1942, 1951); enlisted Territorial Army 1939; embodied for war service 24th August 1939; Bombardier 1940; Sergeant 1941; 2nd Lieutenant, East Surrey Regiment, 1944; Acting Captain 1946; demobilized 1946 as temporary Captain; Clerical Officer, India Office, 3rd June 1947; Territorial Reserve of Officers, List 'B'; Officer Commanding, 3rd Cadet Battalion, East Surrey Regiment, March 1953 to March 1954; Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Capetown April 1954 to June 1957; Dublin October 1957 to July 1961; Ottawa (local Higher Executive Officer) August 1961; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962.

**Sigsworth**, Thomas James; born 14th May 1919; Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 10th October 1936; enlisted as Rifleman, 2nd Queen's Westminsters (K.R.R.C.), 1939; Sergeant, Intelligence Corps, H.Q. Eastern Command, 1940; served in North Africa 1941 and 1942; commissioned in Royal Signals 1943; served in Sicily, Italy and Austria; Captain 1945; released 1946; Executive Officer 1st December 1944; Higher Executive Officer 11th May 1951; Karachi September 1951; Dacca April 1954 to March 1955; Senior Executive Officer (temporary) 10th July 1956; Information Officer, Bombay, 29th January 1957 to 27th July 1960; Senior Information Officer, Ministry of Food, 1949–54 (attached to Government of Northern Ireland); Commonwealth Relations Office 1954; Delhi 1955; Calcutta 1956–58; Dacca (local Information Officer) 1959–61; Information Officer 2nd May 1959; Commonwealth Touring Exhibition 1961–62; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Melbourne 1962.
Officer 1st October 1960; Toronto 22nd November 1960; Port of Spain 12th March 1962.

SIMMONS, Guy Lintorn, MVO (1961); born 27th February 1925; educated Bradford College 1939-43 and Oriel College, Oxford, (History Scholar) 1947-49; 2nd Class Honours in Modern History; m. 1951 Sheila Jacob (3 d. 1953, 1955, 1960); R.A.F. October 1943 to December 1946; Sergeant Pilot; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th July 1949; Peshawar December 1950; Lahore 1951; Dacca March 1952 to May 1954; Principal 20th September 1953; Bombay July 1958; Acting Deputy High Commissioner August to September 1958 and March to July 1960; Delhi May 1961.

SIMS, Alfred John; born 7th May 1914; educated Tollington Park School, London; enlisted Royal Engineers August 1940; released March 1946; Clerical Officer, National Insurance, June 1948; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 25th June 1956; Bombay July 1957 to July 1959; Higher Executive Officer (notional) 4th July 1960; Capetown August 1960 to February 1962; Higher Executive Officer February 1962; Ottawa February 1962.

SKINNER, Douglas Maurice Ralph; born 7th October 1921; educated Glyn School, Epsom, 1932-38; m. 1945 Ivy Garner (1 d. 1946); Clerical Officer, Ministry of Education, 1st July 1938; temporarily transferred to Admiralty (Naval Intelligence) August 1939; served in Royal Navy 1942-1946; returned to Ministry of Education August 1946; Executive Officer 1947; (seniority from April 1945); Commonwealth Relations Office 19th March 1951; Colombo February 1953 to March 1955; Higher Executive Officer 1st November 1953; Delhi September 1955 to November 1958; Canberra August 1959 to July 1962; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1962.

SLATER, Gordon James Augustus; born 8th July 1922; educated Sydney, Australia; m. 1952 Beryl Oliver (1 d. 1952; 1 s. 1955); editorial staff, Sydney Daily Telegraph, 1945-46, Brisbane Telegraph, 1947-48; Parliamentary reporter, Press Association (Central News), London, 1949-52; London Daily Telegraph November 1952 to January 1958; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 6th January 1958; Karachi 29th March 1958; Acting Deputy Director, British Information Services, Karachi, 31st March 1960; Regional Information Officer, Dacca (local Principal Information Officer, October 1960 to July 1961; Vancouver (local Principal Information Officer) October 1961; Acting Principal Information Officer 1st April 1963.

SLINGER, Richard; born 8th November 1924; educated Evered High School, Liverpool, 1936-41; qualified L.C.C. Exhibition to London School of Economics and Political Science in British Constitution August 1955; m. Lorna Hodge (2 d. 1947, 1948; 1 s. 1957; 1 adopted d. 1960); Royal Navy (Combined Operations) 1942-46; Royal Fleet Reservist with 5th Destroyer Flotilla 1952-53; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Works, June 1947 to August 1955; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 22nd August 1955; Delhi February 1956 to October 1957; Calcutta February 1958 to February 1960; Lagos June 1960 to March 1962; Enugu March to August 1962; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; Lagos August 1962 to March 1963.

SMALLMAN, Barry Granger; born 22nd February 1924; educated St. Paul's School 1936-42 and Trinity College, Cambridge, (Major Scholar) 1942-43 and 1946-47; Classical Tripos Parts I and II Class I; BA 1947; MA 1952; m. 1952 Sheila Knight (1 d. 1953; 2 s. 1955, 1957); Intelligence Corps 1944-46; served in Australia; released as Lieutenant 1946; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, 15th December 1947; Secretary to Venn Commission of Enquiry into the Sugar Industry of British Guiana December 1948 to March 1949; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State September 1951 to December 1952; Principal 1st January 1953; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations November 1956 to March 1957 and January to April 1958; seconded to the Government of Western Nigeria as Senior Assistant Secretary, Governor's Office, Ibadan, January 1959 to October 1960; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd January 1961; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations September to December 1961 and 1962; Deputy High Commissioner, Freetown, June 1963.

SMALLWOOD, John Evelyn, Commander R.N. (retd.); born 10th May 1910; educated Royal Naval College, Dartmouth, 1923-27 and Royal Naval College, Greenwich, 1931; m. 1943 Estella Dorothy Bragg (2 s. 1945, 1947); served in Royal Navy (specialised Fleet Air Arm 1933) 1927-60; Ministry of Defence 1951-52 and 1955-57; Naval Attaché, Bangkok, 1958-60; retired June 1960; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd November 1960; Principal 7th December 1960; Karachi April 1961.

SMEDLEY, Harold, MBE (Military) (1946); born 19th June 1920; educated Aldenham School 1934-39 and Pembroke College, Cambridge, (Major Scholar) 1939-40 and 1945-46; Classical Tripos Part I Class I 1946; MA 1948; m. 1950 Beryl Brown (2 s. 1952, 1959; 2 d. 1954, 1960); embodied in R.A.(A.A.)1940; commissioned into Royal Marines 1941; Anti-Aircraft duties in United Kingdom, Middle East and Mediterranean 1941-43; Royal Marine
Commandos 1943-45 (Lieutenant); Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 26th August 1946; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 17th September 1947; Wellington September 1948 to September 1950; Principal 20th September 1949; Salisbury January 1951 to November 1953; Acting High Commissioner August to October 1953; Private Secretary to Secretary of State December 1954 to January 1957; accompanied Secretary of State on visits to New Zealand, Australia, Ceylon, India and Pakistan in 1955 and to Canada 1956; Calcutta February 1957; Delhi December 1957 to July 1960; Assistant Secretary 1st April 1960; High Commissioner in Ghana January 1964.

SMELE, William Samuel George; born 9th June 1912; educated Cotham School, Bristol; m. 1947 Stella Pascoe (1 s. 1948); Member, Institute of Public Relations; general reporter and special writer on Bristol newspapers 1929-1940; war service with Royal Artillery and Intelligence Corps 1940-46; Chief Reporter, Bristol Evening World, 1946; Regional Press Officer, South West, Central Office of Information, 1948; Information Officer 1949; Senior Information Officer (Deputy to Chief Regional Officer), Northern Region, C.O.I., 1951; Information Division (Press Office), H.M. Treasury, 1954; Chief Press and Broadcast Officer (Principal Information Officer), General Post Office, 1957; Commonwealth Relations Office 1958; Regional Information Officer, U.K. Information Service, Montreal, 1958 to 1960; Director, British Information Services, South Africa, September 1960; Director, British Information Services, Malaya, August 1962.

SMITH, Arnold Terence; born 7th October 1922; educated Christ Church School, Dover, and Dover Technical College 1931-38; m. 1944 Mary James (1 s. 1959; 1 d. 1961); Post Office August 1939-49; military service August 1939 to October 1946; commissioned 1943; served Middle East and N.W. Europe; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, August 1949; Executive Officer April 1952; Karachi September 1952 to February 1956; Madras (local Higher Executive Officer) August 1956 to November 1959; Higher Executive Officer June 1959; Kuala Lumpur (local Senior Executive Officer) June 1961; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

SMITH, Jack Braddon; born 17th June 1929; educated Dunstable Grammar School 1937-47; m. 1958 Patricia Bruce (1 d. 1961); Open Executive Officer Examination October 1947; National Service, Royal Signals, Egypt, 1948-50; Executive Officer, Ministry of Food, 1950; Commonwealth Relations Office 14th December 1953; Delhi October 1955 to October 1957; Karachi (local Higher Executive Officer) August 1958 to November 1961; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960.

SMITH, Leonard Gordon; born 11th March 1911; m. 1936 Ethel Foster (1 s. 1939; 1 d. 1942); counter clerk and telegraphist, G.P.O., 11th March 1928; Clerical Officer, India Office, 13th March 1933; Higher Clerical Officer 17th December 1945; Higher Executive Officer (temporary) 1st November 1953; Higher Executive Officer 1st March 1954; Canberra April 1954 to February 1957; Sydney January 1960 to April 1962; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1962.

SMITH, Victor William, CBE (1948); born 6th August 1891; educated Dean Close Memorial School, Cheltenham; m. 1936 Susie Gwendoline Martin (1 d. 1938; 1 s. 1940); joined Indian Police 1911; King's Police Medal 1924; retired 1932; Civil Assistant, War Office, 1939 to 1955; Temporary Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, January 1956.

SMITH, William Jeffrey; born 14th October 1916; educated King Edward VII School, Sheffield, 1927-35 and University College, Oxford, (Scholar) 1935-38; BA 1938; MA 1945; m. 1942 Marie Hughes (1 s. 1947; 1 d. 1951); employed by Calico Printers' Association 1938 to 1940; enlisted September 1939; embodied in R.A. September 1940; commissioned June 1941; served in North Africa, Sicily and Italy; transferred to York and Lancaster Regiment March 1945; Captain; released September 1946; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 11th December 1946; Principal 1st August 1948; Capetown/ Pretoria October 1953 to June 1956; sundry international conferences of G.A.T.T. etc.; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 1st March 1959; Assistant Secretary 1st July 1961; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation 24th July 1961.

SNELLING, Sir Arthur Wendell, KCMG (1960; CMG 1954), KCVO (1962); born 7th May 1914; educated Ackworth School, Yorkshire, 1925-31 and University College, London; BSc (Econ.) Class I Honours 1934; m. 1939 Frieda Barnes (1 s. 1948); Study-Group Secretary, Royal Institute of International Affairs, 1934-36; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 22nd October 1936; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 2nd February 1939; accompanied him on visit to Southern Africa May to July 1939; Acting Principal 23rd May 1940; Joint Secretary to the United Kingdom Economic delegation to America September to November 1943 and to the International Monetary Conference, Bretton Woods, U.S.A., June to September 1944; accompanied Lord Keynes on Mission to U.S.A. and Canada October to December 1944; member of United Kingdom Delegation to Repar-
CHAPTER 50

Biographical Notes

SOWDEN, Laurence James; born 22nd July 1906; educated Hugh Myddelton School, London; Telegraphist, G.P.O. (Overseas Section), 3rd September 1923; Clerical Officer, India Office, 24th July 1930; War Office (on loan) 1st January 1940; Higher Clerical Officer (temporary) 8th August 1940; Higher Clerical Officer 23rd March 1943; volunteered for Royal Navy 27th March 1942; served Western Approaches; invalided out 12th May 1943 and returned to India Office; regraded as Executive Officer with effect from 23rd March 1942; Higher Executive Officer 1st October 1960.

STANLEY, Henry Sydney Herbert; born 5th March 1920; educated Eton 1933-38 and Balliol College, Oxford, 1938-40; War Degree History; m. 1941 Margaret Dixon (3 s. 1949, 1951, 1953); enlisted in ranks July 1940; commissioned in King's Royal Rifle Corps December 1940; served in North-West Europe 1944-46 and at H.Q., Control Commission for Germany; Captain; released August 1946; Temporary Officer, Grade III, Foreign Office (German Section), September 1946 to December 1947; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th December 1947; Secretary, United Kingdom/Southern Rhodesia Financial Talks, March 1949; Principal 1st November 1949; Karachi July 1950 to December 1952; seconded to Office of High Commissioner for Basutoland, Bechuanaland Protectorate and Swaziland October 1954 to September 1956; Capetown/Pretoria September 1956 to September 1957; seconded to Foreign Office, and posted to British Embassy, Washington, February 1959 to March 1961; Adviser to Governor of Tanganyika on Commonwealth and External Affairs, June 1961; Deputy High Commissioner, Dar es Salaam, December 1961; Assistant Secretary 1st May 1962; Commonwealth Relations Office Representative in Kenya June 1963.

STANSFIELD, George Norman; born 28th February 1926; educated Liscard High School, Wallasey; m. 1947 Elizabeth Margaret Williams; Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Food, 1942-44 and 1947-49; R.A.F. 1944-47; Clerical Officer 1949; Executive Officer, Ministry of Supply, March 1952; War Office November 1958; Higher Executive Officer 11th July 1960; Administrative Officer to Director-General of Armament Production 1960-61; Secretary of the Armament Production Advisory Committees 1961; Commonwealth Relations Office 8th November 1961; Calcutta October 1962.

STEPHENS, Malcolm George; born 14th July 1937; educated Shooter's Hill Grammar School 1948-53; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th December 1953; Executive Officer 3rd February 1956; National Service May 1956 to May 1958; Accra 1959-62; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962; member of Inspection Team to Kenya, Uganda, Tanganyika and the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland June to August 1962; Nairobi June 1963.

STEPNEY, William Stanley; born 10th December 1923; educated Strand School; m. 1947 Irene Allen (3 s. 1948, 1949, 1951); enlisted Royal Air Force December 1941; served in Southern Rhodesia, South Africa, Middle East, North Africa, Italy and Kenya; Warrant Officer Pilot; released December 1946; R.A.F.V.R. 1949-54; Temporary Clerk, India Office, 30th December 1946; Clerical Officer 23rd October 1947; Executive Officer 30th December 1952; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960.

STOCKWELL, James Arthur, MBE (1959); born 31st August 1921; educated Wembley County School 1931-38; m. 1943 Sheila Mewten (1 s. 1953; 1 d. 1954); Clerical Officer, India Office, 12th December 1938; enlisted in The Buffs (Royal East Kent Regiment) June 1940; commissioned in Welch Regiment July 1942; Captain October 1944; served in North-West Europe 1944-45; Mentioned in Despatches; served in Palestine and Egypt 1943-46; released October 1946; Executive Officer 29th August 1947; toured India, Pakistan, Ceylon, Canada, South Africa and Southern Rhodesia with Batterbee Mission 1951-52; Higher Executive Officer 6th March 1953; Delhi May 1953 to July 1954; Ottawa August 1955 to July 1958; Passport Officer, Capetown, May 1959 to June 1960; Senior Executive Officer 20th May 1960; Capetown/Pretoria June 1960 to May 1962; seconded to Foreign Service December 1961 to May 1962.

STORAR, Leonore Elizabeth Therese; born 3rd May 1920; educated Park School, Glasgow, 1929-38 and St. Andrews University 1938-41; Political Economy and Political Science; MA; Temporary Employment Officer, Ministry of Labour, July 1941 to January 1942; embodied in A.T.S. February 1942; commissioned April 1942; A.T.S. Staff College; G.S.O. II in H.Q., B.A.O.R., September 1945 to May 1946; Junior Commander; released May 1946; Temporary Administrative Assistant, Ministry of Works, 6th January 1947; Executive Officer 20th February
1948; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st September 1948; Principal 8th May 1950; Delhi and Calcutta November 1951 to May 1953; Salisbury May 1956 to June 1958; Colombo September 1960 to November 1962; Assistant Secretary (temporary) 3rd December 1962, (acting) 1st July 1963.

STORRS, Peter John Francis; born 12th January 1916; educated Radley College 1929-33 and Peterhouse, Cambridge, 1934-37; 2nd Class Hons. Modern Languages June 1936; 2nd Class Hons. (1st Division) Modern History June 1937; MA; studied abroad 1938-39; Temporary Secretary, British Legation, Oslo, September 1939; member of British Mission, Northern Norway, May 1940; awarded Norwegian Military Medal; R.A.S.C. August 1940; commissioned Intelligence Corps August 1941; posted to Liaison Mission; Norwegian Brigade; Special Operations Executive August 1942; served in North Africa and France 1944-45; Staff Officer II, Political Division, Control Commission, Berlin, 1945; Information Officer (Eastern France), Strasbourg, August 1946; Private Secretary to the Secretary-General of the Organization for European Economic Co-operation, Paris, August 1948; Secretary of O.E.E.C.
