Missions to Washington 1949 and 1950; member of O.E.E.C. Delegation to International Materials Conference, and later head of O.E.E.C. Mission, Washington, 1951; Assistant Director (later Director), Commonwealth-American Current Affairs Unit of the English-Speaking Union, May 1953; Director of Public Relations, Government of Cyprus, November 1956; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th April 1959; Regional Information Officer, Calcutta, (local Principal Information Officer) May 1959; Regional Information Officer, Ottawa, May 1962; Acting Principal Information Officer 1st April 1963.

STRONG, John Clifford; born 14th January 1922; educated Beckenham Grammar School 1931-40 and London School of Economics and Political Science 1940-42; LL.B.; m. 1942 Janet Browning (3 d. 1949, 1951, 1957); R.N.V.R. 1942; commissioned (Pilot, Fleet Air Arm) 1943; demobilized May 1946; Administrative Officer, Colonial Service (Tanganyika), 1946-63; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th August 1963.

SUTTON, Stanley Cecil, CBE (1961), MSC (Econ.); born 23rd September 1907; educated Tottenham County School, London School of Economics (MSC (Econ.), First Class Honours in Politics 1930, MSC (Econ.) in Politics 1938) and University College, London, (Diploma in Librarianship 1931); m. 1935 Elizabeth Sinclair (2 s. 1938, 1949; 2 d. 1941, 1943); Sub-Librarian, India Office Library, 17th June 1935; Assistant Keeper 17th June 1937; Keeper 1st Class 4th May 1946; Librarian 1st August 1949; in charge of India Office Records 1st March 1954; Keeper of India Office Records from April 1959.

SYDENHAM-CLARKE, Tredway Seymour Sydenham; born 19th January 1913; educated Charterhouse 1926-30 and Peterhouse, Cambridge, 1931-34; 2nd Class Modern Languages Tripos; MA; m. 1940 Marjorie Gourlay (2 d. 1943, 1949); Ceylon Civil Service 1936-46; Secretary, Combined Security Bureau, Ceylon, 1940-43; Joint Secretary, U.K. Delegation to United Nations Preparatory Conference on Tariffs and Trade, Geneva, 1947; U.K. Trade Commissioner, Durban, 1948-55; Administrative Staff College, Henley, 1957; Colonial Development Corporation, High Commission Territories Region, 1958-61; Commonwealth Relations Office Security Officer 18th September 1961.

SYKES, Edwin Leonard; born 1st May 1914; educated Leys School, Cambridge, 1927-32, Grenoble University February to July 1933 and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1933-37; History Tripos Part I Class I, Part II Class I; MA; m. 1946 Margaret McCulloch; Assistant Principal 4th October 1937; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 4th August 1939; military service September 1939 to April 1945; France and Belgium (B.E.F.) November 1939 to May 1940; Major, Royal Signals, 1941; Algeria and Tunisia (First Army) November 1942 to January 1944; Washington, U.S.A., (British Army Staff) February 1944 to April 1945; Principal 2nd April 1943; Ottawa April 1945 to July 1947; seconded to Cabinet Office January 1949 to January 1951; member of Secretariat of Meetings of Commonwealth Finance Ministers 1949, Foreign Ministers 1950, and Prime Ministers 1951, and of Commonwealth Consultative Committee in London 1950; Assistant Secretary 21st May 1951; Delhi July 1952 to September 1954; Imperial Defence College 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Salisbury, July 1956 to March 1959; seconded to Colonial Office November 1961 to July 1962.

SYMINGTON, William Denis; born 15th August 1920; educated Cranleigh School, Surrey, Le Havre, France, and Lucerne, Switzerland; m. 1946 Isobel Margaret Douglas Hamilton (3 d. 1948, 1951, 1958); assistant language master, Cranleigh, 1940; military service 1941-46; commissioned Royal Armoured Corps March 1942; served with Royal Scots Greys in Middle East, Italy and N.W. Europe; Staff Officer, Military Government, Hanover, 1945-46; Major; service with Control Commission and U.K. High Commission, Germany, under Foreign Office (German Section) 1946-55; Regional (later Land) Commissioner's Office, Hanover, 1946; Executive Officer (temporary) 1946; Senior

Temporary Assistant 1949; Higher Executive Officer (temporary), Consulate General, Frankfurt, 1953; United Kingdom Secretary, the Save the Children Fund, 1956-59; Temporary Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 28th September 1959; Wellington January 1960; Information Officer 10th March 1960; Auckland (local Senior Information Officer) September 1960; Salisbury (local Senior Information Officer) June 1963; Senior Information Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

TANNER, George Stephen; born 25th August 1921; educated Sheen County School; m. 1945 Gladys Ellen Charman (d. 1949); enlisted in ranks, R.A. (T.A.), 1938; mobilised September 1939; served 8th Army, Middle East, 1940-45; demobilised 1946; Central Office of Information 29th July 1946; Executive Officer 1st January 1948; Assistant Information Officer 1st August 1949; Temporary Information Officer 8th June 1956; Information Officer 23rd December 1957; Commonwealth Relations Office 18th July 1962.

TENTEN, Theodore Patrick; born 20th March 1919; educated Oratory Central School; m. 1945 Winifred Hilda Brown (d. 1947, 1949); Boy Messenger, Post Office Savings Bank, 1933; Sorter, London Postal Region, 1937; military service 1939-46; Postal and Telegraph Office, London Postal Region, 1948; Clerical Officer, Ministry of Fuel and Power, 1949; seconded to National Coal Board April 1952 to January 1953; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st October 1953; Madras 1954-56; Capetown 1958-61; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Port of Spain August 1962.

THOMAS, Richard; born 18th February 1938; educated Leighton Park School and Merton College, Oxford; MA; National Service in R.A.S.C. 1959-61; 2nd Lieutenant; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 20th November 1961; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 23rd April 1962; accompanied him on visits to Cyprus, Trinidad, Jamaica, Canada, India, Nigeria, Ghana, Sierra Leone and The Gambia; Accra September 1963.

THOMPSON, Averil Fuller, BA; born 21st April 1907; educated Queenswood School, Hatfield, 1920-24, Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, 1925-29 (2nd Class, Honours School of Lit. Hum.; BA) and University College, London, 1929-30 (Diploma in Librarianship (Director's Prize)); appointed Assistant, Higher Grade, India Office Library, 30th August 1937; on loan to Ministry of Aircraft Production June 1940 to February 1943; Burma Office February 1943; Acting Assistant Principal, India Office, May 1943 to April 1946; Assistant Keeper, 1st Class, India Office Library, 22nd August 1949.

THOMPSON, Harold; born 17th September 1917; educated Liverpool Collegiate School 1928-1934; m. 1946 Nancy Barrett; Clerical Officer, General Post Office, 2nd December 1935; enlisted Royal Corps of Signals, March 1940; served with 7th Armoured Division and 7th Independent Armoured Brigade, Middle East and Burma; demobilized and returned to General Post Office February 1946; Ministry of National Insurance 29th April 1946; Higher Clerical Officer (later assimilated to Executive Officer) 30th December 1946; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 20th May 1957; Delhi 9th January 1958 to April 1961; Kampala (local Senior Executive Officer) September 1962; Senior Executive Officer (acting) 1st August 1963.

TORY, Sir Geoffroy William, KCMG (1958: CMG 1956); born 31st July 1912; educated King Edward VII School, Sheffield, and Queens' College, Cambridge, 1931-35; Modern and Mediaeval Languages Tripos (French and German) Part I Class I, Part II Class I; BA 1934; m. (1) 1938 (s. 1939, 1942; d. 1944;) m. (2) 1950 Hazel Winfield; Assistant Principal, Dominions Office, 25th October 1935; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State November 1938 to August 1939; commissioned in Royal Artillery, Territorial Army, 1936; embodied August 1939; Major; released 24th May 1943; Principal (in absentia) 23rd May 1940; Private Secretary to Secretary of State August 1945 to August 1946; Ottawa September 1946 to August 1949; Assistant Secretary (notional) 2nd September 1946; Assistant Secretary 1st August 1948; Dublin October 1949 to July 1950; Counsellor, Dublin, July 1950 to December 1951; Imperial Defence College January to December 1952; Deputy High Commissioner, Peshawar, March 1953 to March 1954; Deputy High Commissioner, Canberra, May 1954 to June 1957; High Commissioner in the Federation of Malaya September 1957 to October 1963; Ambassador to the Republic of Ireland 1963.

TRACY, Ralph George, OBE (1962: MBE 1953); born 29th April 1912; educated Brockley Secondary School 1923-29; m. 1938 Folyette Badger (2 d. 1946, 1952); Clerical Officer, India Office, 6th August 1929; Executive Officer 24th May 1938; Higher Executive Officer 29th October 1942; served in Royal Signals 1942-45; Ottawa July 1950; Colombo (local Senior Executive Officer) December 1952; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1953; Chief Executive Officer 3rd April 1956; Senior Chief Executive Officer 7th August 1959; Deputy Accountant-General.
TROUNSON, Alfred Donald; born 30th September 1905; educated Mill Hill School; m. 1946 Janet Margaret Dow; commissioned R.A.S.C. December 1939; served in North Africa, Sicily and Italy; Staff Officer, Allied Commission, Rome, 1945; Assistant Director Civil Affairs (Lieutenant-Colonel), A.F.H.Q., Caserta, 1946; Second Secretary (temporary), Grade B.4, British Embassy, Rome, January 1947 to July 1953; British Representative on the 4-Power Committee on German Assets in Italy 1948-53; Temporary Senior Executive Officer, Grade B.3, News Department, Foreign Office, 31st May 1954 to 31st December 1957; seconded to the United Kingdom Delegation to the United Nations, New York, for the 12th Session of the General Assembly September to December 1957; Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st January 1958; Press Officer to the Commonwealth Education Conference, Oxford, July 1959; Regional Information Officer, Sydney, (local Principal Information Officer) 19th October 1959; Principal Information Officer (acting) 1st April 1963.

TUFFILL, Leslie William Herbert, MBE (1960); born 31st May 1922; educated Chiswick County Grammar School 1933-39; Matriculation 1938; m. 1947 Elfriede Hildegard (1 s. 1948); Clerk, Sudan Government (London Office), 1939; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 12th September 1939; war service, Royal Tank Regiment, September 1941 to February 1947; Executive Officer 26th July 1948; Assistant Establishment Officer, Uganda, 1951-52; Higher Executive Officer, Colonial Office, 22nd August 1955; Chief Office Supervisor, Government of Aden, 15th March 1956; A/Assistant Secretary (Colony), Aden, March 1957 to April 1958; A/Assistant Secretary (Establishments), Aden, October 1958 to March 1960; Assistant Secretary (Training), Aden, April 1960; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 6th March 1961; Karachi December 1961; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 1st August 1963.

TURNER, Adrian Geoffrey Leslie; born 28th April 1927; educated Highgate School 1937-39 and Clayesmore School, Dorset; 1940-45; qualified for open Exhibition to Cambridge in Mathematics March 1945; National Service 1946-48; a Founder Honorary Fellow of the Heraldry Society July 1954; External Examiner in Western Music, University of the Punjab, May 1957; Executive Officer 1946 with seniority from 1st January; Commonwealth Relations Office 23rd August 1948; attended Fifth Conference of Commonwealth Meteorologists, London, May 1955; Lahore September 1955 to September 1957; local Higher Executive Officer 3rd May 1957; a Government Adviser, Forty-

Third International Labour Conference, Geneva, June 1959; Higher Executive Officer, 18th June 1959; Colombo July 1960; a British Representative on the Colombo Plan Council for Technical Co-operation in South and South-East Asia, Colombo, 1961; Senior Executive Officer (notional) 1st August 1961. Publications, etc., include various articles for the Heraldry Society and over a hundred and twenty broadcasts on Western music for Radio Pakistan and Radio Ceylon.

TURNER, Harold Goodhew, CMG (1960); born 23rd December 1906; educated St Olave's 1918-25 and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1925-28; Classical Tripos Part I Class II; History Tripos Part I Class II; BA 1928; m. 1934 Aileen Mary Mace (2 s. 1935, 1946; 1 d. 1939); Malayan Civil Service 1929-57; served in Federated Malay States (Perak, Pahang and Selangor), Straits Settlements (Singapore and Malacca) and the Unfederated Malay States (Johore and Kelantan); Principal Establishment Officer, Federation of Malaya, 1957; Secretary to Treasury, Federation of Malaya, 1959; retired June 1961; Director of Studies, Royal Institute of Public Administration, December 1961 to June 1962; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 9th July 1962.

TURNER, Harold James; born 18th May 1920; educated St. Benedict's School, Ealing, 1928-36; m. 1947 Gladys Moon; Clerical Officer, Dominions Office, 21st June 1937; joined R.A.F. June 1941; released October 1946; Higher Clerical Officer (later Executive Officer) 10th February 1947; attached to Secretariat of Commonwealth Conference, Canberra, August to September 1947; Colombo January 1948 to May 1950; Higher Executive Officer (temporary) 1st September 1951, (substantive) 2nd July 1952; Delhi January 1953; Bombay (local Senior Executive Officer) August 1954 to May 1956; Senior Executive Officer (temporary) 22nd January 1958; Senior Executive Officer 13th May 1959; Chief Executive Officer 29th May 1961.

TWIST, Henry Aloysius, OBE (Military); born 18th June 1914; educated Liverpool University 1932-36; Hons. Classics Class II Division I; BA; Diploma in Education (with distinction) 1936; m. 1941 Mary Mulhall (1 s. 1944; 1 d. 1947); Senior Classics Master, St. Chad's College, Wolverhampton, 1936-40; Lecturer in English, South Staffordshire High School of Commerce, 1937-40; army service 1940-46; Lieutenant-Colonel; Temporary Principal, Dominions Office, 13th September 1946; Principal 23rd November 1946; Colombo January 1948; Australia April 1949 to July 1952; Secretary to United Kingdom Delegation to meeting of Commonwealth Consultative Committee, Sydney, May 1950; member of Secretariat,

Commonwealth Economic Conference, London, November 1952; Deputy High Commissioner, Bombay, May 1954; Assistant Secretary 29th August 1955; member of United Kingdom Delegation to the Commonwealth Telecommunications Conference, London, June 1958; member of United Kingdom Delegation at S.E.A.T.O. Council Meetings, Wellington 1959, Washington 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Kaduna, October, 1960 to November 1962; Imperial Defence College January 1963.

U

UNWIN, James Brian; born 21st September 1935; educated Chesterfield School, New College, Oxford, (Honorary Exhibitioner) 1955-59 (Classical Hon. Mods. and Lit. Hum.) and Yale University 1959-60 (MA); 2nd Lieutenant, Northamptonshire Regiment, 1954-55; Lieutenant, Sherwood Foresters, T.A., 1955-59; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 12th September 1960; Resident Clerk January to March 1961; Private Secretary to Minister of State February 1961; Salisbury March 1961 (local Principal).

V

VINES, Eric Victor; born 28th May 1929; educated St. Dunstan's College, Catford, 1939-47 and St. Catharine's College, Cambridge, 1949-52; 1st Class Honours in History; MA; National Service (R.A.O.C.) 1947-49; m. 1953 Ellen-Grethe Klüppers; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 13th October 1952; Colombo January 1954 to June 1955; Assistant Private Secretary to Secretary of State 15th August 1955; Private Secretary to Permanent Under-Secretary of State 30th January 1956; accompanied Permanent Under-Secretary of State on tour of India, Pakistan, Malaya and Ceylon January to March 1957; Principal (temporary) 20th May 1957; Commonwealth Prime Ministers Meeting Secretariat June 1957; Principal 6th August 1957; Office of the Commissioner-General for the United Kingdom in South-East Asia February 1958; Private Secretary to United Kingdom Commissioner, Singapore, and Commissioner-General for South-East Asia January 1960 to July 1961; Canberra October 1961.

VINING, Rowena Adelaide; born 25th September 1921; educated privately, at Chiddingstone Castle, Edenbridge, and the International School, Geneva; Political Intelligence Department of the Foreign Office 1941; served in Algeria, Italy and South-East Asia Command; Temporary Higher Executive Officer, Foreign Office, 1947-52; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 18th February 1952; Karachi (local Information Officer) 1955-58; Information Officer, Sydney, 1959 to April 1962; Senior Information Officer 26th April 1962.

W

WAKELEY, Leonard John Dean, OBE (1945); born 18th June 1909; educated Westminster School 1923-28, Christ Church, Oxford, 1928-32 (1st Class Honours Modern History 1931; MA) and School of Oriental Studies, London, 1932-33; Edwin Arnold Memorial Scholarship, University College, Oxford, 1932; m. 1938 Margaret Tinson (2 s. 1939, 1942); Indian Civil Service 1932-47; served in Punjab and in Defence Co-ordination, Defence and Legislative Departments of Government of India; Secretary, Council of State, 1945-47; Joint President, Society of Clerks-at-the-Table in Empire Parliaments 1946; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 5th August 1947; Principal 17th September 1947; attached to United Kingdom Delegation to United Nations, New York, September to December 1949; Cape Town/Pretoria April 1950 to November 1952; attended E.C.A.F.E. Regional Conference on Mineral Resources Development, Tokyo, April 1953; Deputy High Commissioner, Madras, December 1953 to March 1957; Assistant Secretary 29th August 1955; Deputy High Commissioner, Accra, October 1957 to May 1960; Deputy High Commissioner, Ottawa, November 1962; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (local).

WALKER, Sir Charles Michael, KCMG (1963; CMG 1960); born 22nd November 1916; educated Charterhouse 1930-35 and New College, Oxford, 1935-39; 2nd Class Honours Modern Greats; BA; m. 1945 Enid McAdam (1 s. 1947; 1 d. 1949); Clerk of House of Lords 5th June 1939; enlisted in Army October 1939; commissioned in R.A. March 1940; served in India and Iraq March 1940 to December 1943; delegate representing G.H.Q., India, and H.Q., S.E.A.C., at Intelligence Conference, Washington, January 1944; British Army Staff, Washington, April 1944 to December 1945; released March 1946 with rank of Lieutenant-Colonel; Principal 5th June 1946; Dominions Office 1st March 1947; seconded to Foreign Service as First Secretary, British Embassy, Washington, January 1949 to May 1951; Calcutta (local Assistant Secretary) February 1952 to January 1954; Assistant Secretary 1st January 1954; Delhi February 1954 to May 1955; Imperial Defence College January to December 1958; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (temporary) and Director of Establishments and Organization March 1959; Assistant Under-Secretary of State 1st August 1960; High Commissioner in Ceylon November 1962.
WALKER, David Critchlow; born 9th January 1940; educated Manchester Grammar School and St. Catherine's College, Cambridge. 1958-62: Geographical Tripos Class I 1961; Certificate of Education 1962; Assistant Lecturer in Geography at Manchester University 1962-63; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th August 1963.

WALKER, Peter Frederick; born 21st March 1923; educated City of London School, E.C.4, 1933-39; m. 1945 Mary Davidson (1 d. 1950; 1 s. 1953); with Lloyds Bank Ltd. 1939-42; served in R.A.F. March 1942 to January 1947, including service in India 1945-46; Executive Officer, India Office, 24th March 1947; Higher Executive Officer 2nd July 1952; Bombay December 1952 to July 1956; New Delhi March 1957 to June 1960; Senior Executive Officer 20th May 1960; Chief Executive Officer (temporary) 19th March 1962. (substantive) 1st September 1962; Principal 1st August 1963; Nairobi October 1963.

WALKER, Robert; born 1st May 1924; educated Sowerby Bridge Secondary School 1935-42 and Peterhouse, Cambridge, 1942-43 and 1946-48; History Tripos Parts I and II Class II Division I; m. 1949 Rita Thomas (1 s. 1953; 1 d. 1956); N.V.R. ordinary seaman June 1943; commissioned April 1944; Sub-Lieutenant; released September 1946; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st November 1948; Peshawar July 1949; Karachi February 1950 to August 1951; Principal (temporary) 1st December 1952; Principal 20th September 1953; Delhi August 1955 to February 1959; Accra June 1962; Acting Deputy High Commissioner June to July and November 1962 and April to June 1963.

WALKER, William Frederick; born 16th April 1921; educated Reay School, London, S.W.9; m. 1945 Lena Walton; military service 1940-46; served in Libya, India, Burma and Germany; Clerical Officer, Board of Trade, August 1946; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 8th August 1955; Kuala Lumpur (local Higher Executive Officer) May 1957 to February 1961; Higher Executive Officer 4th July 1960; Ibadan July 1961.

WALKER-BRASH, John Douglas Grenville; born 31st July 1919; educated Westminster School; m. 1960 Margaret Sessions; military service 1939-51, Infantry; Brigade Major, 77 Brigade, 2nd Chindit Expedition; Mentioned in Despatches; also served in India, Egypt, Palestine, Eritrea, Greece and Malaya; journalist 1951-58; Commentator, Cyprus Broadcasting Service (Government of Cyprus), 1956-59; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 7th December 1959; First Secretary (Information), Accra, December 1959; Acting Director of Information Services, Accra, December 1960 to April 1961 and July to December 1962; substituting Principal Information Officer 11th August 1962; Regional Information Officer, Edmonton, 20th February 1963.

WALL, Robert Duncan, Commander R.N.; Master Mariner; born 18th March 1912; m. 1939 Jane Dudley (1 d. 1940; 1 s. 1944); Executive and Air Branches of the Royal Navy 1928-45; Dominions Office 20th November 1945 in temporary post of Assistant Secretary (Information), Ottawa, 1945-49; Temporary Senior Information Officer 22nd March 1949; Information Officer 1st August 1949; Director, Information Office, Colombo, 1949-52; Karachi May to October 1952; Regional Information Officer, Lahore and Peshawar, 1952-54; Senior Information Officer (temporary) 10th October 1952; Senior Information Officer 8th November 1955; Deputy Director, U.K.I.S., Ottawa, September 1955 to December 1957; Director U.K.I.S., Salisbury, March 1958 to April 1961; Principal Information Officer 1st October 1960; Director of Information, Cyprus, September 1961.

WALMSLEY, Jeffrey Grayston; born 30th January 1932; educated Preston Grammar School 1942-47; m. 1957 Colleen Barbara Murphy (1 s. 1958; 1 d. 1960); Clerk with Preston County Borough Council Motor Taxation Department 1947-53; national service with R.A.F. 1950-52; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 21st July 1953; Calcutta 1955-57; Madras 1958-62; Higher Executive Officer (temporary) May 1962; Bombay 1963.

WALSH ATKINS, Leonard Brian, CMG (1962), CVO (1961); born 15th March 1915; educated Charterhouse (Scholar) 1928-34 and Hertford College, Oxford, (Scholar) 1934-37; 2nd Class Honours in Lit.Hum.; BA; m. 1940 Marguerite Black (3 s. 1942, 1944, 1949); Assistant Principal, India Office, 11th October 1937; Assistant Secretary to Indian Delegation to League of Nations Assembly September 1938; Fleet Air Arm November 1940; 822 N.A. Squadron, Home Fleet; Lieutenant-Commander (A), and Air Staff Officer, M.V. Adula, Western Approaches, December 1943; Mentioned in Despatches December 1945; Principal (in absentia) 1st November 1941; demobilised July 1945; posted to Burma Office; returned to India Office March 1947; Assistant Secretary 1st March 1949; Counsellor, Dublin, September 1953 to April 1956; Imperial Defence College 1957; Deputy High Commissioner, Karachi, January 1959 to December 1961; Assistant Under-Secretary of State (temporary) 28th May 1962.

WALWYN, Fanny, MBE (1953); born 17th May 1906; educated Heywood (Lancs.) Grammar School 1916-23; S.C. and T.,
Heywood Post Office, 10th September 1923; Clerical Officer, Money-Order Department, 13th January 1929; India Office 3rd April 1933; Executive Officer 10th November 1941; Higher Executive Officer 31st October 1949.

Watson, Arthur Christopher; born 2nd January 1927; educated Norwich School 1940-45, Selwyn College, Cambridge, 1945 and St. Catherine's College, Cambridge, 1948-50 (Honorary Scholar 1950); Archaeology and Anthropology Tripos Part I Class I; BA (1950); MA (1953); m. 1956 Mary Candler (née Earl) (1 step-d. 1948; 1 step-s. 1952; 1 d. 1957); Royal Navy 1945-48; Sub-Lieutenant, R.N.V.R.; First Devonshire Course, London University, 1950-51; Colonial Administrative Service, Uganda, and H.M. Overseas Civil Service 1951-62; District Officer 1953; Principal Assistant Secretary 1961; Secretary, Office of the Governor, March to October 1962; retired from H.M.O.C.S. 1963; Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th June 1963.

Watson, Jean Radcliffe, MA; born 4th September 1925; educated Gateshead Secondary School 1936-43 and Newnham College, Cambridge, (Exhibitioner and Scholar) 1943-47; Modern and Medieval Languages Tripos Part I Class I 1945; Oriental Languages Tripos Part I Class I 1947; Treasury Studentship in Oriental Languages 1948-51; Temporary Assistant Keeper, Class II, India Office Library, 1st October 1951; Assistant Keeper, Class I, 18th June 1954.

Watts, Rosslyn Reginald Gordon; born 24th November 1929; educated City of Bath Boys' School 1941-48; m. 1951 Ivy Young (1 d. 1955; 1 s. 1963); National Service (R.A.O.C.) 1948-50; 2nd Lieutenant; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 22nd May 1950; Higher Executive Officer 18th October 1954; Dacca March 1955 to September 1957, Lahore to July 1958; Senior Executive Officer 24th August 1960; Kuala Lumpur June 1963.

Watts, William John; born 11th March 1923; educated Oakham School 1936-41 and St. Catherine's College, Cambridge, 1946-47; m. 1949 Anne Watt (1 s. 1951; 1 d. 1960); R.A.F. Service 1941-46; R.A.F. Japanese Course 1945-46; Malayan Civil Service 1948; studied Chinese in Macau 1949-51; Chinese Affairs, Kedah, 1951-53; District Officer 1953-55; Assistant Secretary, External Defence, 1956-57; Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Interior and Justice, 1957-59; resigned from Malayan Government Service August 1959; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 18th January 1960; Principal 29th December 1961; Colombo December 1962.

Wehl, David Anthony; born 28th December 1905; educated Merchant Taylors' School; Publicity Officer for Italian State Railways in London 1925; Staff Speaker for Ministry of Information 1940; Lieutenant, Royal Engineers, 1943; Major (Deputy Assistant Director, Public Relations), 14th Army, Far East Land Forces, 1945; Information Officer, Central Office of Information, 1947; Senior Information Officer 1951; Deputy Regional Information Officer, Leeds, 1952; Commonwealth Relations Office, 15th August 1958; Regional Information Officer, Penang, 1958; Acting Director, Information Services, Kuala Lumpur, 1960; Regional Information Officer, Ibadan, 1961 to January 1964; Acting Deputy High Commissioner, Ibadan, August to November 1963; Kuala Lumpur February 1964; author of Field Fare, The Goldfish Bowl, The Birth of Indonesia, The Moon Upside Down, Old Moley, Modern Malay Usage, Toys and Play in Education; productions: Torn Banner, And If I Laugh.

Wellington, Sidney; born 30th December 1922; educated Tottenham County School; m. 1947 Lilian Andrews (2 s. 1948, 1952); Clerical Officer, India Office, 30th May 1939; Executive Officer 8th January 1948; Higher Executive Officer 21st December 1955; Salisbury September 1958 to July 1961; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1962.

Wenban-Smith, William Nigel; born 1st September 1936; educated The King's School, Canterbury and King's College, Cambridge; Classical Tripos Class II Division I 1960; m. 1961 Charlotte Chapman-Andrews; National Service (R.N.) 1955-57; Plebiscite Supervisory Officer, Southern Cameroons, August 1960 to February 1961; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 4th September 1961; Private Secretary to the Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State 12th August 1963.

Whitehead, George Sydney, MVO (1961); born 15th November 1915; educated Boys' County School, Harrow, 1927-34 and London School of Economics (Exhibitioner) 1934-37; BSc (Econ.) 1937; m. 1948 Constance Hart (née Vale) (1 step-d. 1944; 1 d. 1950); Executive Officer, India Office; 12th December 1934; service in R.A. (H.A.A.) June 1940 to September 1945; served in Gold Coast December 1943 to August 1945; Captain; Higher Executive Officer (in absentia) 22nd July 1940; Private Secretary to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State December 1945 to December 1946; Principal, Burma Office, 2nd December 1946; Rangoon, Burma, October 1947 to January 1948; seconded to Foreign Office (British Embassy, Rangoon) January to April 1948; Canberra May 1952 to July 1955; Calcutta
(local Assistant Secretary) 9th January 1958 to August 1961; Assistant Secretary 1st April 1960; Inspector 13th November 1961.

**Wickson**, Dalby Walter Harry, MBE (1951); born 3rd July 1906; educated Bedford Modern School 1918-24; m. 1930 Irene Walduck (3 s. 1932, 1934, 1945; 1 d. 1937); S.C. and T., G.P.O., July 1924; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 12th May 1930; Higher Clerical Officer 6th July 1940; served in R.A.S.C. 1942-46; Sergeant; attached to War Office for duty with Malayan Planning Staff August 1944; released March 1946; Staff Officer (later Higher Executive Officer), Dominions Office, 19th February 1947; Passport Officer, Capetown, December 1949 to May 1953; Senior Executive Officer 18th May 1953; Delhi March 1958 to March 1962; Chief Executive Officer (local) 1st July 1961; Chief Executive Officer (temporary) 30th July 1962.

**Widdows**, Leslie Spencer; born 16th November 1912; educated St. Bartholomew's Grammar School, Newbury, 1924-29; m. 1937 Nanette Thacker (1 d. 1938; 2 s. 1945, 1947); Social Welfare appointments with Southend C.B. Council and Herts and Berks County Councils 1929-37; Certificate, Poor Law Examinations Board, 1936; Social Welfare Officer, Portsmouth City Council, 1937 and Warwickshire County Council, 1939-48; Commissioned as Navigator 1943-45; Executive Officer, National Assistance Board, July 1948; Higher Executive Officer, Colonial Office, 25th November 1957; Commonwealth Relations Office 1st December 1960; Calcutta March 1961.

**Willcocks**, Derek; born 14th June 1930; educated Plymouth College and Devonport High School; m. 1956 Sylvia Freeman (1 s. 1957; 2 d. 1959, 1961); National Service with Royal Air Force 1949-51; Executive Officer, Ministry of Supply, June 1951 (seniority from 1st April 1949); Ministry of Aviation October 1959; Higher Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 17th October 1960; Karachi February 1962.

**Willcocks**, Lieutenant-Colonel John Francis, OBE (1962); born 26th August 1918; educated Radley College and R.M.A. Woolwich; m. 1940 Betty Lloyd (1 s. 1942; 1 d. 1944); commissioned Royal Artillery 1938; served N.W. Europe and Middle East 1939-47; qualified Staff College 1948; served Singapore 1949-52; Directing Staff, Staff College, 1954-57; qualified Armed Forces Staff College, U.S.A., 1957; served B.A.O.R. 1957-59; Commanding Officer, 26th Regiment, R.A., Malaya, 1959-62; Assistant to Principal Staff Officer to Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations 1st October 1962.

**Willey**, Peter; born 12th June 1923; educated Frimley and Camberley County Secondary School 1935-40; m. 1946 Josephine Walsh (1 s. 1961); Temporary Clerk, Ministry of Food, August 1940; Clerical Officer April 1948; Executive Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 1st December 1955; Calcutta February 1957 to December 1958; seconded to Department of Technical Co-operation July 1961; Higher Executive Officer 23rd May 1962.

**Williams**, John Robert; born 15th September 1922; educated Sheen County School and Fitzwilliam House, Cambridge; Geographical Tripos Part I Class II Division I; Archaeological and Anthropological Tripos Part II Class I; m. 1958 Helga Elizabeth Konow Lund (2 d. 1959, 1962; 1 s. 1960); military service 1941-46; enlisted in ranks of King's Royal Rifle Corps; commissioned service with 1st Battalion King's African Rifles in East and Central Africa; Ceylon and Burma campaign; Captain; Assistant Principal, Colonial Office, August 1949; Secretary, Singapore Riots Inquiry Commission, 1951; Principal 26th November 1951; visited Somaliland, Nyasaland and Southern Rhodesia 1954; visited Addis Ababa for negotiation of Anglo/Ethiopian Agreement on Somali Grazing Areas 1954; seconded to Commonwealth Relations Office as Principal 2nd March 1956; Delhi March 1956; transferred to Commonwealth Relations Office 24th June 1958; Deputy High Commissioner, Penang, August 1959 to October 1962; Kuala Lumpur October 1962: Delhi (local Assistant Secretary) May 1963.

**Williams**, Martin John; born 3rd November 1941; educated Manchester Grammar School 1952-59 and Corpus Christi College, Oxford, 1959-63; Classical Moderations Class II, Lit. Hum. Class II; Assistant Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 19th August 1963.

**Winter**, Arnold Martin; born 22nd December 1920; educated Upton House Central School, London; m. 1951 Rita Hillringhaus (1 s. 1951; 1 d. 1956); war service in R.A.F. 1941-46; Temporary Clerk II, Control Commission for Germany, September 1946; Control Officer III 10th May 1948; Clerical Officer, Commonwealth Relations Office, 14th June 1951; Karachi October 1953 to March 1958; Executive Officer 24th December 1954; Colombo May 1959 to June 1961; Higher Executive Officer 29th January 1962; Nicosia September 1963.

**Wool-Lewis**, Cyril Eric, OBE (1951); born 17th June 1906; educated Westminster School and Trinity College, Cambridge, 1925-29; commissioned in East Surrey Regiment 1929; Assistant Commissioner of Police, Sierra Leone, 1935; Assistant District Commissioner, Sierra Leone, 1937; District Commissioner 1942; Com-
missioner of the Turks and Caicos Islands, B.W.I., 1946-51; seconded to the Colonial Office 1951-53; Administrative Officer Class II, Northern Nigeria, 1953; Administrative Officer Class I 1954; transferred to Nigerian Federal Government Service 1956; Staff Grade 1956; Permanent Secretary 1957; retired from Overseas Civil Service June 1961; Temporary Principal, Commonwealth Relations Office, 23rd October 1961.

WOOLVERTON, Kenneth Arthur Frederick; born 4th August 1926; educated Orange Hill Grammar School 1938-44; m. Kathleen Eleanor West; Meteorologist, R.A.F. 1944-48; Hendon Borough Council 1948-50; Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, 3rd April 1950; Executive Officer 19th February 1952; Higher Executive Officer 11th July 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 18th December 1961.

WRIGHT, John Arthur, born 10th January 1932; educated Heanor Grammar School, Derbyshire; m. 1956 Enfsys Ann Roberts (Is. 1962); Clerical Officer, Colonial Office, May 1948; National Service (Royal Air Force) 1950-52; Librarian IV, Commonwealth Relations Office, September 1959; Librarian III September 1962.

WYTHERS, John Rowland Graham, BEM (1945); born 2nd February 1918; educated Soham Grammar School, Camb., 1929-34; m. 1945 Joyce Warren (1 s. 1946; 1 d. 1948); L.C.C. Social Welfare Department 1934-39; Relieving Officers' Certificate, Poor Law Examinations Board, 1936; Territorial Army (Royal Artillery, Heavy A.A.) 1939-42; served in Norway and North Africa; Intelligence Corps 1942; served in Persia and Iraq (Warrant Officer); L.C.C. YEOMAN, Kenneth Stanley; born 9th August 1920; educated Cardinal Vaughan School, London, and Mayfield College, Sussex; m. 1948 Ursula Feord (3 d. 1949, 1951, 1958); Clerical Officer, G.P.O., 21st July 1937; mobilised R.N.V.R. 27th September 1939; commissioned Sub-Lieutenant, R.N.V.R., 1943; demobilised 1946; Executive Officer, G.P.O., 1st November 1947; on temporary transfer Malaya 1952-56; on contract, Nigeria, 1957-61; Higher Executive Officer, G.P.O., (in absentia) 1st April 1960; Commonwealth Relations Office 16th June 1961; Karachi March 1962; Lahore May 1962.

YOUNG, Eric; born 16th November 1924; educated Maltby Grammar School, Yorkshire, 1935-42 and Sheffield University 1942-43 and 1946-48; Honours Class II Division I in English Language and Literature 1948; BA; m. 1949 Sheila Hutchinson (1 d. 1956; 2 s. 1958, 1961); Royal Navy 1943-46; served in Mediterranean, Indian Ocean and Far East; joined Sheffield Telegraph as reporter and leader-writer July 1948; sub-editor, Western Morning News, Plymouth, 1951; sub-editor and later regional news editor, Guardian, Manchester, 1953-58; visited West Africa as reporter 1958; Public Relations Officer, National Coal Board, Manchester, 1958-59; Temporary Senior Information Officer, Colonial Office, and Deputy Director, United Kingdom Information Office in Tanganyika and Zanzibar, January 1960; Senior Information Officer March 1961; Commonwealth Relations Office as Deputy Director, British Information Services, Tanganyika, 19th December 1961 to September 1963; Regional Information Officer (local Principal Information Officer), Kaduna, November 1963.

YOUNG, Joffre Alfred; born 26th March 1915; educated Merton School; m. 1941 Ethel Violet Welfare; Post Office 1929; Clerical Officer, Savings Bank Department, 1938; Clerical Officer, Canterbury Telephone Area, 1948; Higher Clerical Officer, Shrewsbury Telephone Area, 1950; Higher Executive Officer, (Treasury Pooling Scheme), Commonwealth Relations Office, 11th September 1961; Dacca October 1962.
